sentences.zh: 楊鶴，字修齡，武陵人。

translations.literal: Yang He, style name Xiuling, was a man of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Yang He, whose style was Xiuling, came from Wuling.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the thirty-second year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授雒南知縣，調長安。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Luonan and was transferred to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Luonan and later transferred to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 四十年擢御史，上疏請東宮講學。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was promoted to censor and memorialized requesting lectures for the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he was promoted to censor and submitted a memorial asking that the crown prince receive formal instruction.

sentences.zh: 且言：「頃者，愛女被躪於宮奴，館甥受撻於朝市，叩閽不聞，上書不達，壅蔽極矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover he said: "Recently, a beloved daughter was trampled by palace slaves, and a nephew-in-law was beaten in the court marketplace; knocking on the palace gate brought no hearing, and memorials did not reach [the throne]—obstruction has reached an extreme."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Not long ago a beloved daughter was trampled by palace slaves, and a nephew-in-law was flogged in the public market outside court; appeals at the palace gate went unheard, and written petitions never arrived—the channels of communication are utterly blocked.

sentences.zh: 時壽寧主婿冉興讓為掌家宮人梁盈女、內官彭進朝等毆辱，公主三奏不達，興讓掛冠長安門去，故鶴言及之。

translations.literal: At that time Ran Xingrang, son-in-law of the Prince of Shouning, had been beaten and humiliated by the steward palace woman Liang Yingnu, the inner attendant Peng Jinchao, and others; the princess submitted three memorials that did not get through, and Xingrang hung up his official cap and left by the Chang'an Gate—hence He's mention of it.
translations.idiomatic: This referred to Ran Xingrang, son-in-law of the Prince of Shouning, who had been beaten and humiliated by the steward eunuch Liang Yingnu, the inner attendant Peng Jinchao, and others; the princess had submitted three memorials that never reached the throne, and Xingrang had resigned his office and left through the Chang'an Gate—which was why He brought up the case.

sentences.zh: 尋出督兩淮鹽法，巡按貴州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went out to supervise the salt laws of the two Huai regions and served as touring censor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out to supervise salt administration in the two Huai circuits and to serve as touring censor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 貴州接壤烏撒，去川南敘州千里，節制難。

translations.literal: Guizhou bordered Wusa, a thousand li from Xuzhou in southern Sichuan, and control was difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou bordered Wusa, which lay a thousand li from Xuzhou in southern Sichuan, making effective control difficult.

sentences.zh: 土官安雲龍死，其族人與沾益安效良爭印，構兵三十年，後竟為效良所據，其父紹慶又據沾益州，皆川、雲、貴咽喉地。

translations.literal: The native official An Yunlong died; his clansmen and An Xiaoliang of Zhanyi contended for the seal, raised troops for thirty years, and in the end it was seized by Xiaoliang; his father Shaoqing also held Zhanyi Prefecture—all throat regions of Sichuan, Yunnan, and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the native official An Yunlong died, his kinsmen fought An Xiaoliang of Zhanyi for the official seal; the feud raged for thirty years until Xiaoliang finally prevailed, while his father Shaoqing also held Zhanyi Prefecture—all strategic choke points linking Sichuan, Yunnan, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 鶴請割烏撒隸貴州，地近節制便，可弭後患，朝議不決。

translations.literal: He requested that Wusa be cut off and placed under Guizhou; the land was near and control convenient, and later troubles could be quelled—the court deliberated but did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed transferring Wusa to Guizhou jurisdiction so that the nearer distance would ease administration and forestall future trouble, but the court could not reach a decision.

sentences.zh: 未幾，效良為亂，如其言。

translations.literal: Before long Xiaoliang rebelled, just as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiaoliang did rise in rebellion, exactly as He had warned.

sentences.zh: 貴州土官以百數，水西安氏最大，而土地、戶口、貢賦之屬，無籍可稽。

translations.literal: Guizhou native officials numbered in the hundreds; the An clan of Shuixi was the greatest, yet land, households, tribute, and the like had no registers that could be checked.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou had hundreds of native officials; the An clan of Shuixi was the most powerful, yet there were no reliable registers of their lands, populations, or tribute obligations.

sentences.zh: 鶴乃檄宣慰安位盡著之籍，並首領目把主名、承襲源委，悉列上有司。

translations.literal: He then issued a proclamation that Pacification Commissioner An Wei record everything fully in registers, and together with the names of chieftains, sub-chiefs, and headmen and the sources of succession, list them all upward to the supervising offices.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Pacification Commissioner An Wei to enter full records of his domain, together with the names of chieftains, sub-chiefs, and headmen and the lines of hereditary succession, and submit them all to the supervising authorities.

sentences.zh: 自是簿牒始明，奸弊易核。

translations.literal: From this time the ledgers first became clear, and malfeasance was easy to verify.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the records were clear for the first time, and abuses became easy to audit.

sentences.zh: 事竣，不候命徑歸。

translations.literal: When his duties were finished, without awaiting orders he went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour was complete, he returned home without waiting for formal dismissal.

sentences.zh: 久之，還朝。

translations.literal: After a long time he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 楊鎬四路師敗，鶴薦熊廷弼、張鶴鳴、李長庚、薛國用、袁應泰，言：「遼事之失，不料彼己，喪師辱國，誤在經略；

translations.literal: When Yang Gao's four-route army was defeated, He recommended Xiong Tingbi, Zhang Heming, Li Changgeng, Xue Guoyong, and Yuan Yingtai, saying: "The failure in Liaodong affairs lay in not gauging enemy and self; the loss of the army and disgrace to the state was the fault of the frontier commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Gao's defeat on four fronts, He recommended Xiong Tingbi, Zhang Heming, Li Changgeng, Xue Guoyong, and Yuan Yingtai, writing: "The Liaodong disaster stemmed from misjudging the balance of forces; the lost armies and national humiliation were the frontier commissioner's error;

sentences.zh: 不諳機宜，馬上催戰，誤在輔臣；

translations.literal: not understanding the opportune moment, urging battle from horseback, was the fault of the chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: the chief ministers' error was not understanding the situation and pressing for battle from horseback;

sentences.zh: 調度不聞，束手無策，誤在樞部。

translations.literal: dispatch and coordination unheard of, hands tied with no plan, was the fault of the Military Affairs Commission.
translations.idiomatic: the Military Affairs Commission's error was hearing nothing of deployments and having no plan at all.

sentences.zh: 至尊優柔不斷，又至尊自誤。」

translations.literal: The sovereign's being irresolute and undecided was again the sovereign's own error."
translations.idiomatic: And the sovereign's own error was his habitual indecision.

sentences.zh: 當事惡其直，將假他事逐之，乃引疾去。

translations.literal: Those in power hated his bluntness and were about to drive him out on some other pretext; he then pleaded illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power resented his bluntness and were preparing to remove him on some other charge, so he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，起太僕少卿，擢右僉都御史，巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was recalled as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and promoted to right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianqi reign he was recalled as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and promoted to right vice censor-in-chief as grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.

sentences.zh: 未任，丁內艱，而廣寧又敗。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he entered mourning for his mother, and Guangning was again lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he entered mourning for his mother, and Guangning fell again.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢以鶴黨護廷弼，除鶴名。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian, because He was a partisan who protected Tingbi, removed He's name [from office].
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian struck He's name from the rolls because He had been an ally who defended Xiong Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，召拜左僉都御史，進左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was summoned and appointed left vice censor-in-chief, then promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was summoned as left vice censor-in-chief and soon promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 鶴上言：「圖治之要，在培元氣。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The essential of seeking good government lies in nurturing vital energy.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "The key to restoring good government is to nurture the realm's vital strength.

sentences.zh: 自大兵大役，加派頻仍，公私交罄，小民之元氣傷；

translations.literal: Since great armies and great corvée, repeated additional levies, public and private both exhausted, the common people's vital energy was wounded;
translations.idiomatic: Ever since great campaigns and massive corvée, repeated surtaxes have drained both public and private coffers and wounded the common people's strength;

sentences.zh: 自遼左、黔、蜀喪師失律，暴骨成丘，封疆之元氣傷；

translations.literal: since defeats and loss of discipline in eastern Liaodong, Guizhou, and Sichuan, exposed bones heaped like mounds, the frontier's vital energy was wounded;
translations.idiomatic: defeats and broken discipline in Liaodong, Guizhou, and Sichuan have left bones heaped like hills and wounded the empire's frontier strength;

sentences.zh: 自搢紳構黨，彼此相傾，逆奄乘之，誅鋤善類，士大夫之元氣傷。

translations.literal: since gentry formed factions and overthrew one another, the treacherous eunuch seized the chance and executed the good, the scholar-officials' vital energy was wounded.
translations.idiomatic: and since gentry factions have torn one another down, allowing the treacherous eunuch to seize power and purge the good, the scholar-official class has been drained of its strength as well.

sentences.zh: 譬如重病初起，百脈未調，風邪易入，道在培養。」

translations.literal: It is like when a grave illness first arises, the hundred vessels not yet regulated, wind and evil easily enter—the Way lies in nurturing."
translations.idiomatic: It is like a grave illness at its onset: the body's channels are still unsettled, and any wind or pestilence can take hold—the remedy is patient cultivation, not harsh medicine.

sentences.zh: 時以為名言。

translations.literal: At the time this was regarded as a famous saying.
translations.idiomatic: At the time these words were widely praised.

sentences.zh: 先是，遼左用兵，逃軍憚不敢歸伍，相聚剽虜。

translations.literal: Earlier, when troops were used in eastern Liaodong, deserters feared and dared not return to the ranks, gathering to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liaodong was mobilized for war, deserters who feared punishment banded together instead of returning to the ranks and turned to plunder.

sentences.zh: 至是，關中頻歲祲，有司不恤下。

translations.literal: By this time Guanzhong had famine year after year, and the officials did not pity those below.
translations.idiomatic: By now Guanzhong had suffered famine year after year, while local officials showed no concern for the suffering populace.

sentences.zh: 白水王二者，鳩眾，墨其面，闖入澄城，殺知縣張耀采。

translations.literal: Wang Er of Baishui gathered a crowd, blackened their faces, broke into Chengcheng, and killed Magistrate Zhang Yaocai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Er of Baishui rallied a band, blackened their faces, stormed Chengcheng, and killed Magistrate Zhang Yaocai.

sentences.zh: 由是府谷王嘉允、漢南王大梁、階州周大旺群賊蜂起，三邊饑軍應之，流氛之始也。

translations.literal: From this Wang Jiayun of Fugu, Wang Daliang of Hannan, Zhou Dawang of Jiezhou, and bandit groups rose like bees; famine troops of the three frontiers responded—this was the beginning of the roaming bandit scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wang Jiayun of Fugu, Wang Daliang of southern Han, Zhou Dawang of Jiezhou, and other rebel bands rose in swarms, joined by starving soldiers from the three frontiers—this was the beginning of the great roving-rebel movement.

sentences.zh: 當是時，承平久，卒被兵，人無固誌。

translations.literal: At this time, long peace had prevailed; suddenly encountering warfare, people had no firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The realm had known peace so long that when war suddenly struck, no one had a settled will to resist.

sentences.zh: 大吏惡聞賊，曰：「此饑氓，徐自定耳。」

translations.literal: High officials hated to hear of bandits and said: "These are famine mob; in time they will settle of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials hated to hear the word "bandits" and said, "These are only starving rabble; they will quiet down in time."

sentences.zh: 明年，總督武之望死。

translations.literal: The next year Grand Coordinator Wu Zhiwang died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Grand Coordinator Wu Zhiwang died.

sentences.zh: 久之，廷臣莫肯往者，群推鶴。

translations.literal: After a long time no court minister was willing to go; the group pushed He.
translations.idiomatic: For a long time no court minister was willing to take the post, and the court collectively turned to He.

sentences.zh: 帝召見鶴，問方略。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned He for audience and asked his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned He for an audience and asked his plan.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「清慎自持，撫恤將卒而已。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Hold oneself with purity and caution, comfort and pity generals and soldiers—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Keep oneself pure and cautious, and treat the troops with care—that is all.

sentences.zh: 遂拜鶴兵部右侍郎，代之望總督陜西三邊軍務。

translations.literal: He was then appointed right vice minister of War and replaced Zhiwang as grand coordinator of Shaanxi and military affairs of the three frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed right vice minister of War and succeeded Zhiwang as grand coordinator of Shaanxi and military affairs on the three frontiers.

sentences.zh: 至則大梁、大旺、王二已前誅滅，而繼起者益眾。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Daliang, Dawang, and Wang Er had already been executed earlier, but those rising in succession grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Daliang, Dawang, and Wang Er had already been put down, but new rebels were rising in ever greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 鶴素有清望，然不知兵。

translations.literal: He had long had a reputation for integrity, yet he did not understand warfare.
translations.idiomatic: He had long enjoyed a reputation for integrity, but he knew nothing of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 其冬，京師戒嚴，延綏、寧夏、甘肅、固原、臨洮五鎮總兵官悉以勤王行。

translations.literal: That winter the capital was placed on alert; the regional commanders of Yan-sui, Ningxia, Gansu, Guyuan, and Lintao all marched to aid the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the capital went on alert, and the regional commanders of Yansui, Ningxia, Gansu, Guyuan, and Lintao all marched to defend the throne.

sentences.zh: 延綏兵中道逃歸，甘肅兵亦嘩，懼誅，並合於賊，賊益張。

translations.literal: Yansui troops fled back mid-route; Gansu troops also mutinied, fearing execution, and all joined with the bandits—the bandits grew ever bolder.
translations.idiomatic: Yansui troops deserted on the march home; Gansu troops also mutinied, and fearing punishment they merged with the rebels, who grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，王左掛等攻宜川，為知縣成材所卻，轉攻韓城。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Wang Zuogua and others attacked Yichuan, were repelled by Magistrate Cheng Cai, and turned to attack Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Wang Zuogua and others attacked Yichuan, were driven off by Magistrate Cheng Cai, and then turned on Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 軍中無帥，鶴命參政洪承疇禦之。

translations.literal: The army had no commander; He ordered Vice Commissioner Hong Chengchou to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: With no commander in the field, He ordered Vice Commissioner Hong Chengchou to meet them.

sentences.zh: 俘斬三百餘人，圍解，賊走清澗。

translations.literal: More than three hundred were captured and killed, the siege was lifted, and the bandits fled to Qingjian.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred were captured or killed, the siege was lifted, and the rebels fled toward Qingjian.

sentences.zh: 鶴連疏請諸將還鎮，不果，起故將杜文煥任之。

translations.literal: He submitted successive memorials asking that the generals return to their posts; it did not succeed, and the former general Du Wenhuan was recalled to take charge.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized asking that the generals be sent back to their posts, but in vain; instead the former general Du Wenhuan was recalled to take command.

sentences.zh: 二月，延安知府張輦、都司艾穆蹙賊延川，降其魁王子順、張述聖、姬三兒。

translations.literal: In the second month Yan'an Prefect Zhang Nian and Regional Commander Ai Mu pressed the bandits at Yanchuan and received the surrender of their chiefs Wang Zishun, Zhang Shusheng, and Ji San'er.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Yan'an Prefect Zhang Nian and Regional Commander Ai Mu cornered the rebels at Yanchuan and accepted the surrender of their leaders Wang Zishun, Zhang Shusheng, and Ji San'er.

sentences.zh: 別賊王嘉允掠延安、慶陽，鶴匿不奏，而給降賊王虎、小紅狼、一丈青、掠地虎、混江龍等免死牒，安置延綏、河曲間。

translations.literal: Another band, Wang Jiayun, plundered Yan'an and Qingyang; He concealed this and did not report it, yet issued pardons sparing death to surrendered bandits Wang Hu, Little Red Wolf, One-Zhang-Green, Earth-Plundering Tiger, River-Mixing Dragon, and others, settling them between Yansui and Hequ.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the rebel Wang Jiayun was ravaging Yan'an and Qingyang, but He kept this from the throne; instead he issued certificates sparing death to surrendered bandits such as Wang Hu, Little Red Wolf, One-Zhang-Green, Earth-Plundering Tiger, and River-Mixing Dragon, and settled them between Yansui and Hequ.

sentences.zh: 賊淫掠如故，有司不敢問。

translations.literal: The bandits raped and plundered as before; the officials dared not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels continued to rape and plunder as before, and local officials dared not intervene.

sentences.zh: 寇患成於此矣。

translations.literal: The bandit calamity took shape from this.
translations.idiomatic: From this point the bandit scourge became entrenched.

sentences.zh: 七月，嘉允陷黃甫、清水、木瓜，遂陷府谷，文煥擊走之，賊流入山西。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Jiayun took Huangfu, Qingshui, and Mugua, then took Fugu; Wenhuan struck and drove him off, and the bandits flowed into Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Jiayun captured Huangfu, Qingshui, and Mugua, then took Fugu; Wenhuan drove him off, and the rebels spilled into Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 已撫王左掛以白汝學攻綏德州，謀內應。

translations.literal: Wang Zuogua, already pacified, with Bai Ruxue attacked Suide Prefecture, plotting an inside response.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zuogua, whom He had already accepted in surrender, joined Bai Ruxue in attacking Suide Prefecture and plotted collusion from within.

sentences.zh: 事覺，巡按李應期與承疇計誅左掛等綏德，五十七人皆死。

translations.literal: The affair was discovered; Touring Censor Li Yingqi and Chengchou plotted to execute Zuogua and the others at Suide—fifty-seven men all died.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, Touring Censor Li Yingqi and Chengchou arranged the execution of Zuogua and his followers at Suide; all fifty-seven were put to death.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊神一元攻陷新安、寧塞、柳樹澗等堡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the bandit Shen Yiyuan attacked and took the forts of Xin'an, Ningsai, Liushujian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the rebel Shen Yiyuan captured the forts of Xin'an, Ningsai, Liushujian, and others.

sentences.zh: 寧塞，文煥所居，宗人多死。

translations.literal: Ningsai was where Wenhuan lived; many of his clansmen died.
translations.idiomatic: Ningsai was Wenhuan's own home district, and many of his kinsmen were killed.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，賊棄寧塞，陷保安。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the bandits abandoned Ningsai and took Bao'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the rebels abandoned Ningsai and took Bao'an.

sentences.zh: 一元死，弟一魁圍慶陽，陷合水，鶴聞，移駐寧州。

translations.literal: Yiyuan died; his younger brother Yikui besieged Qingyang and took Heshui; on hearing this He moved his headquarters to Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiyuan died, his younger brother Yikui besieged Qingyang and took Heshui; on hearing the news He moved his headquarters to Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 一魁求撫，送還合水知縣蔣應昌，別賊拓先齡、金翅鵬、過天星、田近庵、獨頭虎、上天龍等亦先後降。

translations.literal: Yikui sought pacification and returned Heshui Magistrate Jiang Yingchang; other bandits Tuo Xianling, Golden-Winged Peng, Crossing-the-Sky Star, Tian Jin'an, Lone-Headed Tiger, Ascending Heaven Dragon, and others also surrendered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yikui asked to surrender and returned Heshui Magistrate Jiang Yingchang; other rebels such as Tuo Xianling, Golden-Winged Peng, Crossing-the-Sky Star, Tian Jin'an, Lone-Headed Tiger, and Ascending Heaven Dragon also surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 鶴設御座於城樓，賊跪拜呼萬歲。

translations.literal: He set an imperial seat on the city tower; the bandits knelt and bowed, crying "Long live [the emperor]!"
translations.idiomatic: He set an imperial seat on the city tower, and the rebels kowtowed shouting "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 鶴宣聖諭，令設誓，或歸伍，或歸農，賊佯應之，則立赦其罪，群盜自是視總督如兒戲矣。

translations.literal: He proclaimed the sage edict, ordering them to swear oaths, either return to the ranks or return to farming; the bandits pretended to agree, and he then established amnesty for their crimes—from this the mass of robbers regarded the grand coordinator as child's play.
translations.idiomatic: He read out the imperial message, had them swear oaths to return to the ranks or to farming, and when they pretended to agree he granted them a general amnesty—from that moment the rebel hosts treated the grand coordinator as a figure of mockery.

sentences.zh: 鶴又以一魁最強，致其婿帳中，同臥起，而一魁果至。

translations.literal: He also, because Yikui was strongest, brought his son-in-law into the tent to sleep and rise together with him, and Yikui indeed came.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yikui was the strongest leader, He even had his own son-in-law share a tent with him, eating and sleeping together—and Yikui did come in person.

sentences.zh: 數以十罪，則稽首謝。

translations.literal: Several times he listed ten crimes, and [Yikui] would bow his head in apology.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Yikui with ten offenses on several occasions, and each time Yikui kowtowed in submission.

sentences.zh: 即宣詔赦之，畀以官，處其眾四千餘人於寧塞，使守備吳弘器護焉。

translations.literal: He immediately proclaimed the edict pardoning him, gave him an office, and placed his following of more than four thousand men at Ningsai, making Garrison Commander Wu Hongqi protect them.
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed an imperial pardon, gave Yikui an official title, and settled his following of more than four thousand men at Ningsai under the protection of Garrison Commander Wu Hongqi.

sentences.zh: 文煥聞之，嘆曰：「寧塞之役，賊畏我而逃。

translations.literal: Wenhuan heard of it and sighed: "In the Ningsai campaign the bandits feared me and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenhuan heard of this he sighed and said, "At Ningsai the rebels fled because they feared me.

sentences.zh: 今者賊偽降，楊公信之，借名城為盜資。

translations.literal: Now the bandits falsely surrender and Yang [He] trusts them, lending a famous fortress as capital for robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Now they have only pretended to surrender, yet Yang He trusts them and has handed a famous stronghold over as a base for brigands.

sentences.zh: 我宗人，可與賊逼處此土乎！」

translations.literal: My clansmen—can they be pressed to live on this land together with bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: How can my kinsmen be forced to live cheek by jowl with bandits on this soil!

sentences.zh: 遂以其族行。

translations.literal: He then moved his clan away.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his entire clan away.

sentences.zh: 五月，鶴移駐耀州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month He moved his headquarters to Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month He shifted his headquarters to Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 賊攻破金鎖關，殺都司王廉。

translations.literal: The bandits broke through Jinsuo Pass and killed Regional Commander Wang Lian.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke through Jinsuo Pass and killed Regional Commander Wang Lian.

sentences.zh: 七月，別賊李老柴、獨行狼攻陷中部，田近庵以六百人守馬欄山應之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month other bandits Li Laochai and Lone-Walking Wolf took Zhongbu; Tian Jin'an with six hundred men held Malan Mountain in response.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month other rebels Li Laochai and Lone-Walking Wolf captured Zhongbu, while Tian Jin'an held Malan Mountain with six hundred men in support.

sentences.zh: 而降渠一魁之黨茹成名者，尤桀驁，鶴令一魁誘殺之於耀州，其黨猜懼，挾一魁以叛。

translations.literal: Among the surrendered chieftain Yikui's followers, one Ru Chengming was especially fierce and unruly; He ordered Yikui to lure and kill him at Yaozhou; his followers grew suspicious and fearful and seized Yikui to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Among Yikui's surrendered followers, Ru Chengming was especially violent; He ordered Yikui to lure and kill him at Yaozhou, whereupon the others grew suspicious and fearful and seized Yikui to rise again in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 御史謝三賓言：「鶴謂慶陽撫局既畢，賊散遣俱盡。

translations.literal: Censor Xie Sanbin said: "He claims the Qingyang pacification is finished and the bandits dispersed and sent away entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xie Sanbin wrote: "He claims the Qingyang pacification is complete and that all rebels have been dispersed and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 中部之賊，寧自天降？」

translations.literal: The bandits of Zhongbu—did they fall from heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Did the rebels at Zhongbu fall from the sky?

sentences.zh: 疏下巡按御史吳甡核奏，甡奏鶴主撫誤國。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to Touring Censor Wu Shen to investigate and report; Shen reported that He's policy of pacification had misled the state.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to Touring Censor Wu Shen for investigation; Shen reported that He's appeasement policy had betrayed the state.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，逮鶴下獄，戍袁州。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, arrested He and put him in prison, and banished him to Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, had He arrested and imprisoned, and banished him to Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，子嗣昌擢宣大山西總督，疏辭，言：「臣父鶴以總督蒙譴已三年，臣何心復居此職。」

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year his son Sichang was promoted to grand coordinator of Xuan, Da, and Shanxi; he memorialized declining, saying: "My father He, as grand coordinator, suffered punishment already three years—what heart have I to hold this post again."
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year his son Sichang was promoted to grand coordinator of Xuan, Da, and Shanxi; he declined in a memorial, writing, "My father He was punished as grand coordinator three years ago—how could I bear to hold this same office?

sentences.zh: 帝優詔答之，而不赦鶴罪。

translations.literal: The emperor answered with an excellent edict, but did not pardon He's crime.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a gracious edict but did not pardon He's offense.

sentences.zh: 八年冬，鶴卒於戍所，嗣昌請恤。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighth year He died at his place of exile; Sichang requested posthumous favors.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eighth year He died in exile, and Sichang petitioned for posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 帝復鶴官，而不予恤。

translations.literal: The emperor restored He's office but did not grant favors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor restored He's official rank but granted no posthumous compensation.

sentences.zh: 鶴初以尤世祿寧夏大捷功，進兵部尚書、太子少保，世蔭錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: He had first, on account of You Shilu's great victory merit at Ningxia, been promoted to minister of War and junior guardian of the heir apparent, and Shilu ennobled as a commander of one thousand households in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been promoted to minister of War and junior guardian of the heir apparent on account of You Shilu's great victory at Ningxia, and Shilu was ennobled as a commander of one thousand households in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 十年，敘賀虎臣寧夏破賊功，追加太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, recounting He Huchen's merit in breaking bandits at Ningxia, he was further given the title junior tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when He Huchen's merit in defeating rebels at Ningxia was recorded, He was further made junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又以甘肅敘功，任一子官。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, again on account of Gansu merit, one son was granted an office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year one of his sons was granted an official post in recognition of service in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 從弟鶚，崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: His younger cousin He passed the jinshi in the fourth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin He received his jinshi degree in the fourth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 官御史，有才名，擢順天巡撫。

translations.literal: He served as censor, had a reputation for talent, and was promoted grand coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a censor, won a reputation for ability, and was promoted to grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，南歸，福王以為兵部右侍郎，總督川、湖軍務。

translations.literal: When the capital fell he returned south; the Prince of Fu made him right vice minister of War and grand coordinator of military affairs in Sichuan and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he fled south; the Prince of Fu appointed him right vice minister of War with overall command of military affairs in Sichuan and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 陳奇瑜，字玉鉉，保德州人。

translations.literal: Chen Qiyu, style name Yuxuan, was a native of Baode Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qiyu, whose style was Yuxuan, came from Baode Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-fourth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除洛陽知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，擢禮科給事中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was promoted supervising secretary of the Rites Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Rites Bureau.

sentences.zh: 楊漣劾魏忠賢，奇瑜亦抗疏力詆。

translations.literal: When Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian, Qiyu also submitted a defiant memorial fiercely denouncing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lian impeached Wei Zhongxian, Qiyu also submitted a bold memorial denouncing the eunuch in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 六年春，由戶科左給事中出為陜西副使，遷右參政，分守南陽。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year he went out from left supervising secretary of the Revenue Bureau as vice commissioner of Shaanxi, was transferred to right vice commissioner, and divided defense at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he left the capital as left supervising secretary of the Revenue Bureau to become vice commissioner of Shaanxi, was promoted to right vice commissioner, and took charge of defense at Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，加按察使職，尋歷陜西左右布政使。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Chongzhen he was given the additional post of surveillance commissioner, and soon served successively as left and right administrative commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was given the additional rank of surveillance commissioner and soon served in turn as left and right administrative commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢右僉都御史，代張福臻巡撫延綏。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted right vice censor-in-chief and replaced Zhang Fuzhen as grand coordinator of Yansui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and succeeded Zhang Fuzhen as grand coordinator of Yansui.

sentences.zh: 時大盜神一魁、不沾泥等已殲，而余黨猶眾。

translations.literal: At that time the great bandits Shen Yikui, Bu Zhan Ni, and others had already been destroyed, but the remaining followers were still numerous.
translations.idiomatic: By then the great rebel leaders Shen Yikui and Bu Zhan Ni had been destroyed, but their remaining followers were still numerous.

sentences.zh: 歲大凶，民多從賊。

translations.literal: The year was greatly famine-stricken, and many people followed the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Famine was severe that year, and many common people joined the rebels.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，奇瑜上疏，極言鄜、延達鎮城千餘里饑荒盜賊狀，詔免延安、慶陽田租。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year Qiyu memorialized, speaking at length of famine and bandit conditions over more than a thousand li from Fu to Yan reaching Zhencheng; an edict exempted land tax in Yan'an and Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the following year Qiyu submitted a memorial describing famine and banditry along more than a thousand li from Fu and Yan to Zhencheng; the court ordered land-tax exemptions for Yan'an and Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜乃遣副將盧文善討斬截山虎、柳盜跖、金翅鵬等。

translations.literal: Qiyu then sent Vice General Lu Wenshan to campaign against and behead Mountain-Cutting Tiger, Willow Robber Zhi, Golden-Winged Peng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu then sent Vice General Lu Wenshan to campaign against and kill Mountain-Cutting Tiger, Willow Robber Zhi, Golden-Winged Peng, and others.

sentences.zh: 尋遣遊擊常懷德斬薛仁貴，參政戴君恩斬一條龍、金剛鉆、開山鷂、黑煞神、人中虎、五閻王、馬上飛，都司賀思賢斬王登槐，巡檢羅聖楚斬馬紅狼、滿天飛，參政張伯鯨斬滿鵝，擒黃參耀、隔溝飛，守備閻士衡斬張聰、樊登科、樊計榮、一塊鐵、青背狼、穿山甲、老將軍、二將軍、滿天星、上山虎，把總白士祥斬掃地虎，守備郭金城斬扒地虎、括天飛，守備郭太斬跳山虎、新來將、就地滾、小黃鶯、房日兔，遊擊羅世勛斬賈總管、逼上天、小紅旗，他將斬草上飛、一隻虎、一翅飛、雲裏手、四天王、薛紅旗、獨尾狼，諸渠魁略盡。

translations.literal: Soon he sent Mobile Corps Commander Chang Huaide to behead Xue Rengui; Vice Commissioner Dai Jun'en beheaded One Dragon, Diamond Drill, Mountain-Opening Kite, Black Evil Spirit, Tiger Among Men, Five Kings of Hell, Flying on Horseback; Regional Commander He Sixian beheaded Wang Denghuai; Inspector Luo Shengchu beheaded Horse Red Wolf and Filling-the-Sky Flight; Vice Commissioner Zhang Bojing beheaded Full Goose and captured Huang Canyao and Flying Across the Ditch; Garrison Commander Yan Shiheng beheaded Zhang Cong, Fan Dengke, Fan Jirong, One Lump of Iron, Green-Backed Wolf, Mountain-Piercing Armor, Old General, Second General, Filling-the-Sky Star, and Mountain-Climbing Tiger; Platoon Commander Bai Shixiang beheaded Sweeping-the-Ground Tiger; Garrison Commander Guo Jincheng beheaded Earth-Scratching Tiger and Encompassing-the-Sky Flight; Garrison Commander Guo Tai beheaded Leaping Mountain Tiger, Newly Arrived General, Rolling on the Ground, Little Yellow Oriole, and Room Day Rabbit; Mobile Corps Commander Luo Shixun beheaded Jia the Steward, Forcing Heaven, and Little Red Banner; other generals beheaded Grass-Flying, One Tiger, One-Wing Flight, Cloud-Hand, Four Heavenly Kings, Xue Red Banner, and Lone-Tailed Wolf—the chieftains were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sent Mobile Corps Commander Chang Huaide to kill Xue Rengui; Vice Commissioner Dai Jun'en killed One Dragon, Diamond Drill, Mountain-Opening Kite, Black Evil Spirit, Tiger Among Men, Five Kings of Hell, and Flying on Horseback; Regional Commander He Sixian killed Wang Denghuai; Inspector Luo Shengchu killed Horse Red Wolf and Filling-the-Sky Flight; Vice Commissioner Zhang Bojing killed Full Goose and captured Huang Canyao and Flying Across the Ditch; Garrison Commander Yan Shiheng killed Zhang Cong, Fan Dengke, Fan Jirong, One Lump of Iron, Green-Backed Wolf, Mountain-Piercing Armor, Old General, Second General, Filling-the-Sky Star, and Mountain-Climbing Tiger; Platoon Commander Bai Shixiang killed Sweeping-the-Ground Tiger; Garrison Commander Guo Jincheng killed Earth-Scratching Tiger and Encompassing-the-Sky Flight; Garrison Commander Guo Tai killed Leaping Mountain Tiger, Newly Arrived General, Rolling on the Ground, Little Yellow Oriole, and Room Day Rabbit; Mobile Corps Commander Luo Shixun killed Jia the Steward, Forcing Heaven, and Little Red Banner; and other commanders killed Grass-Flying, One Tiger, One-Wing Flight, Cloud-Hand, Four Heavenly Kings, Xue Red Banner, and Lone-Tailed Wolf—nearly all the rebel chiefs were gone.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜乃上疏曰：「流寇作難，始於歲饑，而成於元凶之煽誘，致兩郡三路皆盜藪。

translations.literal: Qiyu then memorialized: "The roaming bandits rose in rebellion, beginning with yearly famine and taking shape through the incitement of chief villains, until two prefectures and three routes all became bandit lairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu then submitted a memorial: "The roving rebels began with famine and were consolidated by the chief instigators, until two prefectures and three routes had all become bandit strongholds.

sentences.zh: 今未頓一兵，未絕一弦，擒斬頭目百七十七人，及其黨千有奇。

translations.literal: Now without halting a single soldier or breaking a single bowstring, one hundred seventy-seven chieftains have been captured and beheaded, and their followers more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet without halting a single soldier or breaking a single bowstring, we have captured or killed one hundred seventy-seven chieftains and more than a thousand of their followers.

sentences.zh: 頭目既除，余黨自散，向之斬木揭竿者，今且荷鋤負耒矣。」

translations.literal: Once the chieftains were removed, the remaining followers dispersed of themselves; those who once hewed wood and raised poles now shoulder hoes and carry plows."
translations.idiomatic: With the chiefs gone, the rest have dispersed on their own; men who once took up axes and banners now shoulder hoes and carry plows.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，令錄有功將士以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and ordered that meritorious generals and soldiers be recorded and reported.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the report and ordered a record of meritorious officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 延綏群賊多解，獨鉆天哨、開山斧據永寧關。

translations.literal: The bandit groups of Yansui were mostly dispersed; only Drill-to-Heaven Sentinel and Mountain-Opening Axe held Yongning Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the Yansui rebel bands had been broken up; only Drill-to-Heaven Sentinel and Mountain-Opening Axe still held Yongning Pass.

sentences.zh: 永寧在鎮城東，前阻山，下臨黃河，數年不下。

translations.literal: Yongning lay east of Zhencheng, blocked by mountains in front and overlooking the Yellow River below; for several years it could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning lay east of Zhencheng, with mountains blocking the front and the Yellow River below; for several years it could not be captured.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜謂是不可以力取，乃陰簡銳士，陽言總制檄發兵，令賀人龍將之而西，身為後勁，直抵延川。

translations.literal: Qiyu judged that this could not be taken by force; he secretly selected crack troops, openly announced that the supreme commander had issued orders to dispatch troops, had He Renlong lead them west while he himself brought up the rear, and went straight to Yanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu judged that the pass could not be taken by frontal assault; he secretly selected elite troops, publicly announced that the supreme commander had ordered a western campaign under He Renlong, marched in person as rear guard, and advanced straight to Yanchuan.

sentences.zh: 俄策馬東，曰：「視吾馬首所向。」

translations.literal: Suddenly he spurred his horse east, saying: "Watch where my horse's head turns."
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he wheeled his horse east and cried, "Follow where my horse's head turns!

sentences.zh: 潛師疾走入山，賊不虞大兵至，驚潰。

translations.literal: His hidden troops swiftly entered the mountains; the bandits did not expect a great army to arrive and fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: His hidden troops rushed into the mountains; the rebels never expected a major force and broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 焚其巢，斬首千六百有奇，二賊俱馘。

translations.literal: Their nests were burned, heads cut numbered more than sixteen hundred, and both bandits were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Their stronghold was burned, more than sixteen hundred heads were taken, and both rebel leaders were killed.

sentences.zh: 分兵擊斬金翅鵬、一座城，獲首五百五十。

translations.literal: Dividing troops he attacked and beheaded Golden-Winged Peng and One Fortress City, obtaining five hundred fifty heads.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent detachments that killed Golden-Winged Peng and One Fortress City, taking five hundred fifty heads.

sentences.zh: 延水群盜盡平，奇瑜威名著關陜。

translations.literal: The bandit hosts along the Yan River were all pacified, and Qiyu's fame for martial prowess resounded through Guan and Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel bands along the Yan River were all pacified, and Qiyu's military reputation spread throughout Guanzhong and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 於是群盜盡萃於山西，流突河北、畿南。

translations.literal: Thereupon the mass of bandits all gathered in Shanxi and flowed forth to ravage Hebei and the south of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel hosts then concentrated in Shanxi and spilled into Hebei and the region south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 冬冰堅，從澠池渡，躪河南、湖廣，窺四川。

translations.literal: In winter the ice was firm; they crossed from Mianchi, trampled Henan and Huguang, and eyed Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the ice was firm, they crossed at Mianchi, ravaged Henan and Huguang, and threatened Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 明年，廷議諸鎮撫事權不一，宜設大臣統之，多推薦洪承疇。

translations.literal: The next year the court debated that the pacification authority of the various commands was not unified and a great minister should be set over them; many recommended Hong Chengchou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the court debated whether the various frontier commands needed unified authority and agreed that a senior minister should be appointed; many recommended Hong Chengchou.

sentences.zh: 以承疇方督三邊，不可易，乃擢奇瑜兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，總督陜西、山西、河南、湖廣、四川軍務，專辦流賊。

translations.literal: Because Chengchou was then directing the three frontiers and could not be moved, Qiyu was promoted right vice minister of War and concurrently right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of military affairs in Shaanxi, Shanxi, Henan, Huguang, and Sichuan, charged solely with roaming bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chengchou was already directing the three frontiers and could not be moved, Qiyu was promoted to right vice minister of War and right vice censor-in-chief with overall command of military affairs in Shaanxi, Shanxi, Henan, Huguang, and Sichuan, charged solely with suppressing the roving rebels.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜檄諸將會兵陜州。

translations.literal: Qiyu issued orders for the generals to assemble troops at Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu ordered his generals to assemble at Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，老回回、過天星、滿天星、闖塌天、混世王五大營自楚入蜀，陷夔州。

translations.literal: Earlier, the five great camps of Old Huihui, Crossing-the-Sky Star, Filling-the-Sky Star, Charging Collapsing Heaven, and World-Mixing King had entered Shu from Chu and taken Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the five great rebel camps of Old Huihui, Crossing-the-Sky Star, Filling-the-Sky Star, Charging Collapsing Heaven, and World-Mixing King had entered Sichuan from Huguang and captured Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 阻險，復走還楚，分為三：一犯均州，往河南；

translations.literal: Blocked by difficult terrain, they fled back to Chu and divided into three: one raided Junzhou and went toward Henan;
translations.idiomatic: Blocked by difficult terrain, they fled back to Huguang and split into three bands: one raided Junzhou and headed for Henan;

sentences.zh: 一犯鄖陽，往淅川；

translations.literal: one raided Yunyang and went toward Xichuan;
translations.idiomatic: one raided Yunyang and headed for Xichuan;

sentences.zh: 一犯金漆坪，渡河犯商南。

translations.literal: one raided Jinqi Ping, crossed the river, and raided Shangnan.
translations.idiomatic: and one raided Jinqi Ping, crossed the river, and attacked Shangnan.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜乃馳至均州，檄四巡撫會討。

translations.literal: Qiyu then galloped to Junzhou and ordered the four grand coordinators to join in campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu then raced to Junzhou and ordered the four grand coordinators to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 陜西練國事駐商南，遏其西北；

translations.literal: Shaanxi's Lian Guoshi stationed at Shangnan to block their northwest;
translations.idiomatic: Lian Guoshi of Shaanxi stationed at Shangnan to block them from the northwest;

sentences.zh: 鄖陽盧象昇駐房、竹，遏其西；

translations.literal: Yunyang's Lu Xiangsheng stationed at Fang and Zhu to block their west;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiangsheng of Yunyang stationed at Fang and Zhu to block them from the west;

sentences.zh: 河南元默駐盧氏，遏其東北；

translations.literal: Henan's Yuan Mo stationed at Lushi to block their northeast;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mo of Henan stationed at Lushi to block them from the northeast;

sentences.zh: 湖廣唐暉駐南漳，遏其東南。

translations.literal: Huguang's Tang Hui stationed at Nanzhang to block their southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Hui of Huguang stationed at Nanzhang to block them from the southeast.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜乃偕象昇督將士由竹溪至平利之烏林關，十餘戰，斬賊千七百餘級。

translations.literal: Qiyu then together with Xiangsheng directed officers and soldiers from Zhuxi to Wulin Pass in Pingli; in more than ten battles they cut more than seventeen hundred bandit heads.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu then joined Xiangsheng in leading troops from Zhuxi to Wulin Pass in Pingli; in more than ten engagements they killed more than seventeen hundred rebels.

sentences.zh: 越七日，大破之乜家溝，斬千八十餘級，總兵鄧玘功為多。

translations.literal: After seven days they inflicted a great defeat at Miejia Gully, beheading more than one thousand eighty; Regional Commander Deng Yu's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later they won a major victory at Miejia Gully, killing more than one thousand eighty rebels, with Regional Commander Deng Yu contributing the most.

sentences.zh: 已，設伏蚋溪，連戰，斬三百餘級。

translations.literal: Then they set an ambush at Ruoxi, fought successive battles, and beheaded more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: They then laid an ambush at Ruoxi and in successive engagements killed more than three hundred.

sentences.zh: 至獅子山，斬七百二十餘級。

translations.literal: At Shizi Mountain they beheaded more than seven hundred twenty.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizi Mountain they killed more than seven hundred twenty.

sentences.zh: 別將楊化麟、楊世恩、周任鳳、楊正芳等分道擊殺賊，擒其魁闖王、翻山虎等。

translations.literal: Separate commanders Yang Hualin, Yang Shi'en, Zhou Renfeng, Yang Zhengfang, and others struck and killed bandits by separate routes and captured their chiefs Charging King, Mountain-Turning Tiger, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Detached commanders Yang Hualin, Yang Shi'en, Zhou Renfeng, Yang Zhengfang, and others attacked along separate routes, killing rebels and capturing chiefs including Charging King and Mountain-Turning Tiger.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜上言：「楚中屢捷，一時大盜幾盡，其竄伏深山者，臣督鄉兵為向道，無穴不搜，楚中漸有寧宇。」

translations.literal: Qiyu memorialized: "In Chu repeated victories have been won; the great bandits of the moment are nearly all gone; those hiding in deep mountains—your servant has directed local militia as guides, and no cave has gone unsearched; Chu is gradually gaining peace."
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu reported: "We have won repeated victories in Huguang; the great rebel leaders of the moment are nearly all gone. Those hiding in the deep mountains—I have directed local militia as guides and searched every refuge—so Huguang is gradually returning to peace.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉勞之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 乃督副將劉遷等搜竹溪、平利賊，追至五狼河，擒其魁十二人。

translations.literal: He then directed Vice Generals Liu Qian and others to search out bandits in Zhuxi and Pingli, pursued them to Wulang River, and captured twelve chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: He then directed Vice Generals Liu Qian and others to hunt rebels in Zhuxi and Pingli, pursued them to Wulang River, and captured twelve chieftains.

sentences.zh: 遣參將賀人龍等追八晝夜至紫陽，賊死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: He sent Brigade Generals He Renlong and others in pursuit for eight days and nights to Ziyang; more than ten thousand bandits died.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Brigade Generals He Renlong and others in an eight-day pursuit to Ziyang, where more than ten thousand rebels were killed.

sentences.zh: 先是，賊入蜀，復自蜀入秦，由陽平關奔鞏昌，承疇禦之秦州。

translations.literal: Earlier the bandits entered Shu, again from Shu entered Qin, fled through Yangping Pass to Gongchang, and Chengchou resisted them at Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the rebels had entered Sichuan, then returned from Sichuan into Shaanxi, fled through Yangping Pass toward Gongchang, and Chengchou met them at Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊遂越兩當，襲破鳳縣，分為二：一向漢中，取間道犯城固、洋縣；

translations.literal: The bandits then crossed Liangdang, stormed and took Feng County, and divided into two: one toward Hanzhong, taking bypaths to raid Chenggu and Yang County;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then crossed Liangdang, stormed Feng County, and split in two: one band headed for Hanzhong by secret routes to attack Chenggu and Yang County;

sentences.zh: 一由鳳縣奔寶雞、汧陽。

translations.literal: one from Feng County fled toward Baoji and Qianyang.
translations.idiomatic: the other fled from Feng County toward Baoji and Qianyang.

sentences.zh: 於是賊在平利、洵陽間者數萬，自四川入西鄉者二三萬。

translations.literal: Thus bandits between Pingli and Xunyang numbered tens of thousands; those entering Xixiang from Sichuan numbered twenty or thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of rebels were now between Pingli and Xunyang, and another twenty or thirty thousand had entered Xixiang from Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 犯城固、洋縣者，又東下石泉、漢陰，會漢、興，窺商、雒。

translations.literal: Those raiding Chenggu and Yang County again went east down Shiquan and Hanyin, joined Han and Xing, and eyed Shang and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: The band that had attacked Chenggu and Yang County pressed east through Shiquan and Hanyin, converged on Han and Xing, and threatened Shangzhou and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 當是時，奇瑜以湖廣賊盡，鼓行而西，謂賊不足平也。

translations.literal: At this time Qiyu, because Huguang bandits were all gone, marched west with drums beating and judged that the bandits were not worth pacifying.
translations.idiomatic: By then Qiyu believed the Huguang rebels were finished and marched west in triumph, thinking the remaining enemy hardly worth a full campaign.

sentences.zh: 乃遣遊擊唐通防漢中，以護藩封；

translations.literal: He then sent Mobile Corps Commander Tang Tong to defend Hanzhong and protect the princely fief;
translations.idiomatic: He sent Mobile Corps Commander Tang Tong to defend Hanzhong and protect the princely fief;

sentences.zh: 遣參將賀人龍、劉遷、夏鎬扼略陽、沔縣，防賊西遁；

translations.literal: sent Brigade Generals He Renlong, Liu Qian, and Xia Hao to hold Lueyang and Mian County and prevent the bandits fleeing west;
translations.idiomatic: sent Brigade Generals He Renlong, Liu Qian, and Xia Hao to hold Lueyang and Mian County and block a western escape;

sentences.zh: 遣副將楊正芳、余世任扼褒城，防賊北遁；

translations.literal: sent Vice Generals Yang Zhengfang and Yu Shiren to hold Baocheng and prevent the bandits fleeing north;
translations.idiomatic: sent Vice Generals Yang Zhengfang and Yu Shiren to hold Baocheng and block a northern escape;

sentences.zh: 自督副將楊化麟、柳國鎮等駐洋縣，防賊東遁；

translations.literal: personally directed Vice Generals Yang Hualin, Liu Guozhen, and others to station at Yang County and prevent the bandits fleeing east;
translations.idiomatic: and personally led Vice Generals Yang Hualin, Liu Guozhen, and others to station at Yang County and block an eastern escape;

sentences.zh: 又檄練國事、盧象昇、元默各守要害，截賊奔逸。

translations.literal: and again ordered Lian Guoshi, Lu Xiangsheng, and Yuan Mo each to hold strategic points and cut off bandit flight.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Lian Guoshi, Lu Xiangsheng, and Yuan Mo to hold key positions and cut off any breakout.

sentences.zh: 賊見官軍四集，大懼，悉遁入興安之車廂峽，諸渠魁李自成、張獻忠等咸在焉。

translations.literal: The bandits, seeing government troops gathering on four sides, were greatly afraid and all fled into Chexiang Gorge in Xing'an; the chieftains Li Zicheng, Zhang Xianzhong, and others were all there.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing government forces closing in from all sides, the rebels in terror fled into Chexiang Gorge in Xing'an, where the chieftains Li Zicheng, Zhang Xianzhong, and others were all trapped.

sentences.zh: 峽四山巉立，中亙四十里，易入難出。

translations.literal: The gorge had four sides of steep towering mountains; within it stretched forty li—easy to enter, hard to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The gorge was walled by steep mountains on all sides and ran forty li within—easy to enter but nearly impossible to leave.

sentences.zh: 賊誤入其中，山上居民下石擊，或投以炬火，山口累石塞，路絕，無所得食，困甚。

translations.literal: The bandits mistakenly entered it; mountain dwellers rolled stones down or cast torches; at the gorge mouth stones were piled to block it, the road cut off, no food could be obtained—they were extremely distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped inside, the rebels were struck by stones rolled down from above and torches hurled at them; the mouth of the gorge was blocked with piled stone, cutting off escape and food, and they were reduced to desperate straits.

sentences.zh: 又大雨二旬，弓矢盡脫，馬乏芻，死者過半。

translations.literal: Moreover heavy rain fell for twenty days; bows and arrows all came unstrung, horses lacked fodder, and more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain fell for twenty days; bowstrings rotted, horses starved for fodder, and more than half the rebels perished.

sentences.zh: 當是時，官軍蹙之，可盡殲，自成等見勢絀，用其黨顧君恩謀以重寶賄奇瑜左右及諸將帥，偽請降。

translations.literal: At this time government troops pressed them and could have annihilated them entirely; Zicheng and the others, seeing their situation desperate, used their follower Gu Jun'en's plan to bribe Qiyu's attendants and the various commanders with heavy treasure and falsely request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment government troops had them pinned and could have destroyed them entirely; but Zicheng and the others, seeing their position hopeless, followed their follower Gu Jun'en's plan to bribe Qiyu's staff and the field commanders with rich gifts and feign surrender.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜無大計，遽許之，先後籍三萬六千餘人，悉勞遣歸農。

translations.literal: Qiyu had no great plan and hastily agreed; in succession more than thirty-six thousand were registered and all were comforted and sent back to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu had no better plan and hastily agreed; more than thirty-six thousand rebels were registered in all and sent home to farm with provisions and escorts.

sentences.zh: 每百人以安撫官一護之，檄所過州縣具糗糧傳送，諸將無邀撓撫事。

translations.literal: For every hundred men one pacification officer was assigned to escort them; orders went to every prefecture and county passed through to prepare dry rations for relay transport; the generals were not to intercept or obstruct the pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Every hundred men were assigned a pacification officer; every prefecture and county along the route was ordered to supply rations for their passage; and the field generals were forbidden to interfere.

sentences.zh: 諸賊未大創，降非實也，既出棧道，遂不受約束，盡殺安撫官五十餘人，攻掠諸州縣，關中大震。

translations.literal: The bandits had not suffered great injury; the surrender was not real; once they emerged from the plank roads they would not accept restraint, killed more than fifty pacification officers, attacked and plundered various prefectures and counties, and Guanzhong was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had not been broken; the surrender was a sham. Once they emerged from the plank roads they cast off all restraint, killed more than fifty pacification officers, and ravaged prefectures and counties throughout the region—throwing Guanzhong into panic.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜悔失計，乃委罪他人以自解。

translations.literal: Qiyu regretted his miscalculation and shifted blame onto others to exonerate himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu regretted his blunder and tried to shift the blame onto others.

sentences.zh: 賊初叛，猝至鳳翔，誘開城，守城知其詐，紿以縋城上，殺其先登者三十六人，余噪而去。

translations.literal: When the bandits first rebelled they suddenly reached Fengxiang and enticed them to open the gates; the defenders knew their trickery, deceived them by lowering ropes from the wall, killed thirty-six who climbed first, and the rest clamored and left.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels first broke out they suddenly appeared at Fengxiang and tried to trick the garrison into opening the gates; the defenders saw through the ruse, lowered ropes as if to admit them, killed thirty-six who climbed first, and drove the rest away in uproar.

sentences.zh: 其犯寶雞，亦為知縣李嘉彥所挫。

translations.literal: When they raided Baoji they were also repulsed by Magistrate Li Jiayan.
translations.idiomatic: Their attack on Baoji was also beaten back by Magistrate Li Jiayan.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜遂劾嘉彥及鳳翔鄉官孫鵬等撓撫局，撫按官亦異心。

translations.literal: Qiyu then impeached Jiayan and Fengxiang local official Sun Peng and others for obstructing the pacification, and said the pacification officials also had divided hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu then impeached Jiayan and Fengxiang local official Sun Peng and others for sabotaging the pacification, and accused the civil pacification officers of disloyalty as well.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，切責撫按，逮嘉彥、鵬及士民五十餘人。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, sharply rebuked the pacification officials, and arrested Jiayan, Peng, and more than fifty gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, sharply rebuked the pacification officials, and arrested Jiayan, Peng, and more than fifty local gentry and commoners.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜又請敕陜西、鄖陽、湖廣、河南、山西五巡撫各守要害，有失則治諸臣罪，冀以分己過。

translations.literal: Qiyu again requested an imperial order that the five grand coordinators of Shaanxi, Yunyang, Huguang, Henan, and Shanxi each hold strategic points, with loss punished by prosecuting the officials, hoping thereby to divide his own fault.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu also asked for an imperial order that the five grand coordinators of Shaanxi, Yunyang, Huguang, Henan, and Shanxi each hold key positions, with any failure punished—hoping to spread the blame.

sentences.zh: 又委罪巡撫練國事，國事亦被逮。

translations.literal: He again shifted blame onto Grand Coordinator Lian Guoshi, and Guoshi was also arrested.
translations.idiomatic: He also blamed Grand Coordinator Lian Guoshi, who was arrested as well.

sentences.zh: 給事中顧國寶劾奇瑜誤封疆，詔解任候勘。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Gu Guobao impeached Qiyu for misleading the frontier; an edict relieved him of office pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Gu Guobao impeached Qiyu for betraying the frontier; an edict removed him from office pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 御史傅永淳復劾奇瑜解隴州圍報首功不實，詔除名，錦衣官逮訊。

translations.literal: Censor Fu Yongchun again impeached Qiyu for falsely reporting merit in lifting the siege of Longzhou; an edict struck his name from the rolls and Embroidered Uniform Guard officers arrested him for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fu Yongchun further impeached him for falsely claiming credit for relieving the siege of Longzhou; an edict struck his name from the rolls and Embroidered Uniform Guard officers arrested him for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 九年六月謫戍邊。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year he was banished to garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year he was banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 初，奇瑜官南陽，唐王殺其世子，欲並廢世子子聿鍵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qiyu was official at Nanyang, the Prince of Tang killed his heir and wished also to depose the heir's son Yujian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving at Nanyang, Qiyu had intervened when the Prince of Tang killed his heir and tried to depose the heir's son Yujian as well.

sentences.zh: 賴奇瑜力，聿鍵得為世孫。

translations.literal: Relying on Qiyu's effort, Yujian was able to become heir grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Qiyu's intervention, Yujian was confirmed as heir grandson.

sentences.zh: 後聿鍵自立於閩，召奇瑜為東閣大學士。

translations.literal: Later Yujian established himself in Min and summoned Qiyu as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yujian established his regime in Fujian, he summoned Qiyu to serve as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 道遠，未聞命，卒於家。

translations.literal: The road was far; he had not heard the order when he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: The distance was too great; he never received the summons and died at home.

sentences.zh: 元默，字中象，靜海人。

translations.literal: Yuan Mo, style name Zhongxiang, was a native of Jinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mo, whose style was Zhongxiang, came from Jinghai.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the forty-seventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除懷慶推官，擢吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed judicial assistant of Huaqing and promoted supervising secretary of the Personnel Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial assistant of Huaqing and promoted to supervising secretary of the Personnel Bureau.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢焰方熾，以鄉里欲招致之，默謝不可。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian's flame was just blazing; as a fellow townsman he wished to recruit him, but Mo declined and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian's power was at its height; as a fellow townsman he tried to recruit Mo, but Mo firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 言路承忠賢意，劾罷歸。

translations.literal: The remonstrance officials followed Zhongxian's intent, impeached him, and he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The censorial officials, following Zhongxian's wishes, impeached him and drove him from office.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復官，歷遷太常卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen his office was restored; he was transferred through posts to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was restored to office and rose to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 六年春，以僉都御史巡撫河南。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year he became vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he was appointed vice censor-in-chief as grand coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 流賊由均州犯河內，默率左良玉、湯九州、李卑、鄧玘兵待境上；

translations.literal: Roaming bandits from Junzhou raided Henei; Mo led the troops of Zuo Liangyu, Tang Jiuzhou, Li Bei, and Deng Yu to wait at the border;
translations.idiomatic: When roving rebels from Junzhou invaded Henei, Mo led the forces of Zuo Liangyu, Tang Jiuzhou, Li Bei, and Deng Yu to meet them at the border;

sentences.zh: 復率九州乘雪夜薄吳城賊營，大破之。

translations.literal: again led Jiuzhou on a snowy night to press close to the bandit camp at Wucheng and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: and led Jiuzhou in a night attack through the snow on the rebel camp at Wucheng, inflicting a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 嵩、雒以北名城數十，賊避勿敢攻。

translations.literal: North of Song and Luo were several tens of famous cities; the bandits avoided them and dared not attack.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen major cities north of Songshan and Luoyang were spared because the rebels dared not attack them.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜既失李自成於車箱峽，默自汝州移駐盧氏，檄良玉、九州各陳兵守要害，得稍寧者數月。

translations.literal: After Qiyu had lost Li Zicheng at Chexiang Gorge, Mo moved his headquarters from Ruzhou to Lushi, ordered Liangyu and Jiuzhou each to deploy troops guarding strategic points, and gained several months of relative calm.
translations.idiomatic: After Qiyu had let Li Zicheng escape at Chexiang Gorge, Mo moved his headquarters from Ruzhou to Lushi, ordered Liangyu and Jiuzhou to hold key positions, and secured several months of relative calm.

sentences.zh: 當是時，賊勢張，良玉等承督師檄，守備尚固。

translations.literal: At this time bandit power was expanding; Liangyu and the others, receiving the grand coordinator's orders, still held defense firmly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time rebel strength was still growing, but Liangyu and the others, acting under the grand coordinator's orders, still maintained solid defenses.

sentences.zh: 默率諸將斬獲多，賊多趨秦、楚境。

translations.literal: Mo led the generals in many beheadings and captures; the bandits mostly headed toward Qin and Chu territory.
translations.idiomatic: Mo led his generals to many victories, and most rebels were pushed toward Shaanxi and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 已，分為三，自潁州犯鳳陽皇陵，中州所在告急。

translations.literal: Thereafter they divided into three bands; from Yingzhou they attacked Fengyang and the imperial mausoleums, and every place in the Central Plain sent urgent alarms.
translations.idiomatic: They then split into three columns, marched from Yingzhou against Fengyang and the imperial tombs, and alarm spread across the central provinces.

sentences.zh: 八年夏，默被逮去。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eighth year Mo was arrested and taken away.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eighth year Yuan Mo was seized and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，得釋歸，八年卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he was released and returned home; he died in the eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was released and sent home, and died in the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 熊文燦，貴州永寧衛人。

translations.literal: Xiong Wencan was a man of Yongning Guard in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Wencan was from Yongning Guard, Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the thirty-fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 35 (1607).

sentences.zh: 授貴州推官，遷禮部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor in Guizhou, was transferred to secretary in the Ministry of Rites, and rose through the ranks to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Guizhou investigating censor, was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Rites, and advanced to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 出封琉球還，擢山東左參政、山西按察使、山東右布政使。

translations.literal: Returning from a mission to confer investiture on Ryukyu, he was promoted to left vice administrator of Shandong, surveillance commissioner of Shanxi, and right provincial administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: After the Ryukyu investiture mission he was promoted to left vice administrator of Shandong, surveillance commissioner of Shanxi, then right provincial administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 憂歸，自是徙家蘄水。

translations.literal: He returned home in mourning; thereafter he moved his household to Qishui.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for mourning and afterward settled his family at Qishui.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起福建左布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled to serve as left provincial administration commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 (1628) he was recalled as left provincial administration commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 三月，就拜右僉都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: In the third month he was at once appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of that region.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was immediately named right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 海上故多劇盜，袁進、李忠既降，楊六、楊七及鄭芝龍繼起。

translations.literal: The sea had long had many fierce pirates; after Yuan Jin and Li Zhong had surrendered, Yang Liu, Yang Qi, and Zheng Zhilong rose in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The coast had long been infested with formidable pirates; after Yuan Jin and Li Zhong submitted, Yang Liu, Yang Qi, and Zheng Zhilong took their place.

sentences.zh: 總兵官俞咨臯招六、七降，芝龍猖獗如故。

translations.literal: The regional commander Yu Zhaogao induced Six and Seven to surrender, but Zhilong was as rampant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Yu Zhaogao persuaded Yang Liu and Yang Qi to surrender, while Zheng Zhilong remained as defiant as ever.

sentences.zh: 然芝龍常敗都司洪先春，釋不追；

translations.literal: Yet Zhilong often defeated the regional vice commander Hong Xianchun and released him without pursuit;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhilong often routed regional vice commander Hong Xianchun and let him go unharried;

sentences.zh: 獲一遊擊，不殺；

translations.literal: when he captured a mobile corps commander, he did not kill him;
translations.idiomatic: captured a mobile-corps commander and spared him;

sentences.zh: 咨臯戰敗，縱之走。

translations.literal: when Zhaogao was defeated in battle, he let him escape.
translations.idiomatic: and when Yu Zhaogao himself was beaten, allowed him to flee.

sentences.zh: 當事知其可撫，遣使諭降之。

translations.literal: Those in charge knew he could be pacified and sent envoys to persuade him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities concluded he might be brought in by negotiation and sent envoys urging surrender.

sentences.zh: 文燦至，善遇芝龍，使為己用。

translations.literal: When Wencan arrived, he treated Zhilong well and made use of him.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan arrived, treated Zheng Zhilong generously, and turned him to his own purposes.

sentences.zh: 其黨李魁奇再降，再叛去，芝龍擊擒之。

translations.literal: His follower Li Kuiqi surrendered again, rebelled again and left; Zhilong attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: His lieutenant Li Kuiqi submitted, rebelled again, and fled; Zheng Zhilong struck and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 海警漸息，而鐘斌又起。

translations.literal: Sea alarms gradually subsided, but Zhong Bin rose again.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal alarms eased, then Zhong Bin rebelled anew.

sentences.zh: 斌初亦就撫，後復叛，寇福州。

translations.literal: Bin had at first also submitted to pacification, but later rebelled again and raided Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Bin had first accepted pacification, rebelled again, and attacked Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 文燦誘斌往泉州，令芝龍擊敗之。

translations.literal: Wencan lured Bin to Quanzhou and ordered Zhilong to attack and defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan enticed Zhong Bin to Quanzhou and had Zheng Zhilong rout him.

sentences.zh: 既而蹙之大洋，斌投海死。

translations.literal: Presently he pressed him on the open sea, and Bin threw himself into the sea and died.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove him onto the open ocean; Zhong Bin leaped into the sea and drowned.

sentences.zh: 閩中屢平巨寇，皆芝龍力，文燦亦敘功增秩焉。

translations.literal: Within Fujian great bandits were repeatedly suppressed—all by Zhilong's strength—and Wencan also had his merits recorded and rank raised.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian's great pirates were repeatedly crushed, largely thanks to Zheng Zhilong; Wencan's rank rose with the recorded merit.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，擢文燦兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，總督兩廣軍務，兼巡撫廣東。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year Wencan was promoted to vice minister of the right in the Ministry of War with concurrent right vice censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of the military affairs of the two Guang provinces and grand coordinator of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Chongzhen 5 he was promoted to vice minister of war and right vice censor-in-chief, with overall command of military affairs in the two Guang provinces and the grand coordinator's portfolio for Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 先是，海寇鐘靈秀既降復叛，為芝龍所擒，其黨潰入長汀，轉掠江西屬邑，文燦檄芝龍屢敗賊。

translations.literal: Earlier the sea bandit Zhong Lingxiu had surrendered and rebelled again; captured by Zhilong, his faction broke into Changting and turned to plunder subordinate counties of Jiangxi; Wencan repeatedly ordered Zhilong by dispatch to defeat the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the pirate Zhong Lingxiu had submitted and rebelled again; Zheng Zhilong captured him, but his men spilled into Changting and raided Jiangxi counties. Wencan repeatedly ordered Zheng to beat them back.

sentences.zh: 而福建有紅夷之患，海盜劉香乘之，連犯閩、廣沿海邑，帝以責文燦。

translations.literal: Yet Fujian suffered from the red barbarians, and the pirate Liu Xiang took advantage, repeatedly attacking coastal districts of Fujian and Guang; the emperor held Wencan responsible.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian meanwhile faced Dutch raids, and the pirate Liu Xiang exploited the confusion, repeatedly striking Fujian and Guangdong coasts; the emperor blamed Wencan.

sentences.zh: 文燦不能討，乃議招撫，賊佯許之。

translations.literal: Wencan could not subdue them and therefore discussed pacification by enrollment; the bandits pretended to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to destroy them, Wencan turned to negotiations; the pirates feigned acceptance.

sentences.zh: 參政洪雲蒸，長沙人，初官廣西參政，嘗搜靈秀余黨，斬三十餘級，盡毀其巢。

translations.literal: Administrator Hong Yunzheng, a man of Changsha, had first served as administrator in Guangxi; he once searched out Lingxiu's remnant followers, beheaded more than thirty, and utterly destroyed their nests.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Hong Yunzheng, a native of Changsha, had served in Guangxi and once hunted down Zhong Lingxiu's remnants, executing more than thirty men and destroying their lairs.

sentences.zh: 文燦乃令雲蒸與副使康承祖，參將夏之本、張一傑入賊舟宣諭，俱被執。

translations.literal: Wencan then ordered Yunzheng together with vice commissioner Kang Chengzu and regional vice commanders Xia Zhiben and Zhang Yijie to enter the bandit ships to proclaim the decree; all were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan sent Yunzheng, vice commissioner Kang Chengzu, and vice commanders Xia Zhiben and Zhang Yijie aboard the pirate fleet to announce imperial terms; all were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 文燦懼罪，奏諸臣信賊自陷。

translations.literal: Wencan feared punishment and memorialized that the officials had trusted the bandits and brought disaster on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful of blame, Wencan reported that his officers had trusted the pirates and walked into a trap of their own making.

sentences.zh: 給事中朱國棟劾之，詔貶秩，戴罪自效。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Zhu Guodong impeached him; an edict demoted his rank and ordered him to redeem his fault in service.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Zhu Guodong impeached him; the throne reduced his rank and ordered him to win redemption on campaign.

sentences.zh: 八年，芝龍合廣東兵擊香於田尾遠洋。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Zhilong combined with Guangdong troops to attack Xiang in the distant sea off Tianwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Zheng Zhilong joined Guangdong forces to fight Liu Xiang in the open sea off Tianwei.

sentences.zh: 香脅雲蒸止兵，雲蒸大呼曰：「我矢死報國，急擊勿失！」

translations.literal: Xiang coerced Yunzheng to halt the troops; Yunzheng shouted aloud: "I swear to die serving the state—strike hard and do not miss!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang tried to force Hong Yunzheng to call off the attack; Hong cried out, "I have sworn to die for the realm—press the assault and do not hesitate!"

sentences.zh: 遂遇害。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was then slain.

sentences.zh: 香勢蹙，自焚溺死，承祖等脫還。

translations.literal: Xiang's strength was pressed; he burned himself and drowned; Chengzu and the others escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang, cornered, set fire to his ship and drowned; Kang Chengzu and the rest got away.

sentences.zh: 賊黨千餘人詣浙江歸款，海盜盡平。

translations.literal: More than a thousand bandit followers came to Zhejiang to submit; sea pirates were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand pirates surrendered in Zhejiang, and coastal piracy was brought to an end.

sentences.zh: 文燦官閩、廣久，積貲無算，厚以珍寶結中外權要，謀久鎮嶺南。

translations.literal: Wencan had long held office in Fujian and Guang and amassed incalculable wealth; with treasures he thickly cultivated powerful persons at court and in the provinces, scheming for long tenure over Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: After long service in Fujian and Guangdong, Wencan had amassed fabulous wealth and lavished jewels on courtiers and provincial magnates, angling to hold the south for years on end.

sentences.zh: 會帝疑劉香未死，且不識文燦為人，遣中使假廣西采辦名，往覘之。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor doubted that Liu Xiang was not dead and did not know what manner of man Wencan was; he sent a palace eunuch under the pretense of a Guangxi procurement mission to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted whether Liu Xiang was really dead and knew little of Wencan personally; he dispatched a eunuch under cover of a Guangxi procurement tour to look him over.

sentences.zh: 既至，文燦盛有所贈遺，留飲十日。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Wencan showered him with gifts and kept him drinking for ten days.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Wencan loaded him with gifts and kept him feasting for ten days.

sentences.zh: 中使喜，語及中原寇亂，文燦方中酒，擊案罵曰：「諸臣誤國耳。

translations.literal: The eunuch was pleased; speaking of bandit turmoil in the central plain, Wencan was just drunk and, striking the table, cursed: "The ministers have ruined the state!
translations.idiomatic: In good spirits, the eunuch spoke of rebellion in the interior; Wencan, drunk, slammed the table and swore, "The ministers have ruined the empire!

sentences.zh: 若文燦往，詎令鼠輩至是哉！」

translations.literal: If Wencan were sent, how could such rat-like fellows come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Send me, and those vermin would never have grown so bold!

sentences.zh: 中使起立曰：「吾非往廣西采辦也，銜上命覘公。

translations.literal: The eunuch rose and said: "I did not come for Guangxi procurement; I carry the emperor's command to observe you.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch stood and said, "I am not here to buy supplies for Guangxi—I carry orders from His Majesty to appraise you.

sentences.zh: 公信有當世才，非公不足辦此賊。」

translations.literal: You truly have talent for the age; without you this banditry cannot be settled.
translations.idiomatic: You truly have the talent the times demand; no one but you can finish off these rebels.

sentences.zh: 文燦出不意，悔失言，隨言有五難四不可。

translations.literal: Wencan was caught unawares, regretted his slip, and immediately spoke of five difficulties and four impossibilities.
translations.idiomatic: Caught off guard, Wencan regretted his boast and at once listed five difficulties and four reasons it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 中使曰：「吾見上自請之，若上無所吝，即公不得辭矣。」

translations.literal: The eunuch said: "I will ask His Majesty on my own authority; if His Majesty withholds nothing, then you cannot decline.
