translations.idiomatic: The eunuch said, "I will recommend you to the throne myself; if His Majesty holds nothing back, you will not be able to refuse.

sentences.zh: 文燦辭窮，應曰「諾」。

translations.literal: Wencan had no further argument and answered, "Very well."
translations.idiomatic: With no escape, Wencan answered, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 中使還朝，果言之帝。

translations.literal: The eunuch returned to court and indeed told the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch returned and did as he had promised.

sentences.zh: 初，文燦徙蘄水，與邑人姚明恭為姻妮，明恭官詹事，又與楊嗣昌善。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wencan moved to Qishui, he became related by marriage with his fellow townsman Yao Minggong; Minggong held the office of junior tutor and was also on good terms with Yang Sichang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wencan settled at Qishui he married into the family of fellow townsman Yao Minggong, who served as junior tutor and was close to Yang Sichang.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌握兵柄，承帝眷，以帝急平賊，冀得一人自助，明恭因薦文燦，且曰：「此有內援可引也。」

translations.literal: Sichang held military power and enjoyed the emperor's favor; as the emperor was eager to pacify bandits, he hoped for someone to aid him; Minggong therefore recommended Wencan, saying: "He has inside backing that can be drawn upon.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang held the armies and the emperor's trust; eager to crush the rebels, he wanted a dependable deputy. Yao Minggong recommended Wencan, adding, "He has patrons at court who can be enlisted.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌喜，遂薦之。

translations.literal: Sichang was pleased and thereupon recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang was delighted and put his name forward.

sentences.zh: 十年四月，拜文燦兵部尚書兼右副都御史，代王家禎總理南畿、河南、山西、陜西、湖廣、四川軍務。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year Wencan was appointed minister of war with concurrent right vice censor-in-chief, replacing Wang Jiazhen as supreme commander of military affairs in the Southern Metropolitan Region, Henan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Huguang, and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Chongzhen 10 Wencan was made minister of war and right vice censor-in-chief, succeeding Wang Jiazhen as supreme commander of campaigns in the southern capital district, Henan, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Huguang, and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 文燦拜命，即請左良玉所將六千人為己軍，而大募粵人及烏蠻精火器者一二千人以自護，弓刀甲胄甚整。

translations.literal: On receiving the appointment Wencan at once requested the six thousand men led by Zuo Liangyu as his own army, and on a large scale recruited one or two thousand Cantonese and Wuman expert musketeers for his own guard; bows, blades, and armor were very well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he immediately secured Zuo Liangyu's six thousand troops as his personal command and recruited another thousand or two of Cantonese and Wuman musketeers as a bodyguard, all excellently armed and armored.

sentences.zh: 次廬山，謁所善僧空隱。

translations.literal: Stopping at Mount Lu, he paid a visit to the monk Kongyin, whom he favored.
translations.idiomatic: He paused at Mount Lu to visit his friend the monk Kongyin.

sentences.zh: 僧迎謂曰：「公誤矣。」

translations.literal: The monk greeted him and said: "Your Lordship is mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: The monk met him saying, "Your Excellency has taken a wrong turn.

sentences.zh: 文燦屏人問故，僧曰：「公自度所將兵足制賊死命乎？」

translations.literal: Wencan dismissed attendants and asked the reason; the monk said: "Does Your Lordship measure that the troops you lead are enough to compel the bandits to fight to the death?"
translations.idiomatic: Wencan sent his attendants away and asked why. Kongyin said, "Do you believe your soldiers can force these rebels to fight for their lives?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「不能。」

translations.literal: He said: "They cannot."
translations.idiomatic: No," Wencan said."

sentences.zh: 曰：「諸將有可屬大事、當一面、不煩指揮而定者乎？」

translations.literal: He said: "Among the generals is there anyone to whom great affairs can be entrusted, who can hold a sector without troubling command and be settled on his own?"
translations.idiomatic: Is there a commander you could trust with a whole front—someone who could win without your constant direction?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「未知何如也。」

translations.literal: He said: "I do not yet know how it stands."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot yet tell."

sentences.zh: 曰：「二者既不能當賊，上特以名使公，厚責望，一不效，誅矣。」

translations.literal: He said: "If both alike cannot meet the bandits, His Majesty has sent Your Lordship only for your name, with heavy expectation—if once you fail, you will be executed."
translations.idiomatic: If neither your troops nor your generals can match the enemy, the throne has summoned you for your reputation alone and expects much. Fail once and you die."

sentences.zh: 文燦卻立良久，曰：「撫之何如？」

translations.literal: Wencan stepped back and stood a long while, and said: "What of pacifying them?"
translations.idiomatic: Wencan stepped back, silent a long while, then said, "What if I pacify them instead?"

sentences.zh: 僧曰：「吾料公必撫。

translations.literal: The monk said: "I calculate that Your Lordship will surely pacify.
translations.idiomatic: The monk said, "I expect you will try appeasement.

sentences.zh: 然流寇非海寇比，公其慎之。」

translations.literal: Yet roaming bandits are not to be compared with sea bandits—Your Lordship must be careful."
translations.idiomatic: But river-bandits are not sea pirates—be careful.

sentences.zh: 文燦去，抵安慶，帝所遣中官劉元斌、盧九德監勇衛營軍者亦至。

translations.literal: Wencan departed, reached Anqing; the palace eunuchs Liu Yuanbin and Lu Jiude, whom the emperor had sent to supervise the Yongwei Camp army, also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan went on to Anqing, where the eunuchs Liu Yuanbin and Lu Jiude arrived to supervise the Yongwei Camp.

sentences.zh: 良玉宿將桀驁，不受文吏節制，會其下與粵軍不和，大詬。

translations.literal: Liangyu was a veteran general, proud and untamed, and did not accept the restraint of civil officials; it happened that his subordinates were at odds with the Cantonese troops and reviled one another greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu, a veteran and famously unruly, would not bow to civil authority; his men clashed with the Cantonese guard and exchanged fierce abuse.

sentences.zh: 文燦不得已，遣還南兵，然良玉軍實不為用。

translations.literal: Wencan had no choice and sent the southern troops back, yet Liangyu's army in truth was not put to use.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan had no choice but to send the southern troops home, yet Zuo Liangyu's army was barely usable in practice.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌言於帝，乃以邊將馮舉、苗有才兵五千人隸焉。

translations.literal: Sichang spoke to the emperor, and then the frontier generals Feng Ju and Miao Youcai with five thousand troops were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang intervened, and five thousand troops under border generals Feng Ju and Miao Youcai were assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 有才敗於真陽，而京營將黃得功連破賊兵，威甚振。

translations.literal: Youcai was defeated at Zhenyang, but the capital-garrison general Huang Degong repeatedly broke bandit forces and his prestige shook greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Youcai was beaten at Zhenyang, but capital-garrison commander Huang Degong routed the rebels again and again, and his fame soared.

sentences.zh: 當是時，嗣昌建「四正六隅」之策，增兵餉大半，期滅賊，賊頗懼。

translations.literal: At this time Sichang devised the strategy of "four fronts and six corners," increased troops and funds by more than half, and set a term for exterminating bandits; the bandits were rather afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang was pushing his "four fronts, six corners" plan, raising troops and pay sharply in hope of annihilating the rebels, who were genuinely alarmed.

sentences.zh: 及文燦至，京軍屢捷，益懼。

translations.literal: When Wencan arrived, the capital troops won repeatedly, and they feared all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan's arrival coincided with fresh victories by the capital armies, and fear deepened.

sentences.zh: 文燦顧決計招降。

translations.literal: Wencan, however, resolved on pacification by surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan nonetheless fixed on surrender and amnesty.

sentences.zh: 初抵安慶，即遣人招張獻忠、劉國能，二人聽命。

translations.literal: As soon as he first reached Anqing, he sent men to win over Zhang Xianzhong and Liu Guoneng; the two obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Anqing he immediately opened talks with Zhang Xianzhong and Liu Guoneng, both of whom agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃益刊招降檄，布通都。

translations.literal: Thereupon he further printed proclamations to induce surrender and spread them through the metropolitan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He printed more surrender proclamations and posted them across the region.

sentences.zh: 又請盡遷民與粟閉城中，賊無所掠，當自退。

translations.literal: He also requested that all civilians and grain be moved behind closed city walls so the bandits would have nothing to plunder and would withdraw of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed evacuating the populace and grain into walled cities so the rebels, having nothing to loot, would withdraw on their own.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，譙讓文燦。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and reproached Wencan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌亦心非之，既已任之，則曲為文燦解。

translations.literal: Sichang too inwardly disapproved, but since he had already entrusted him, he bent to explain away for Wencan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang privately disapproved but, having backed the appointment, made excuses for him at court.

sentences.zh: 因其請，畀以畿輔、山西兵各三千。

translations.literal: In response to his request, three thousand troops each from the capital district and Shanxi were given him.
translations.idiomatic: To satisfy his requests, the throne gave him three thousand men each from the capital zone and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，國能果降，而獻忠襲據谷城。

translations.literal: The next year Guoneng indeed surrendered, while Xianzhong raided and seized Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Liu Guoneng did submit, while Zhang Xianzhong seized Gucheng by assault.

sentences.zh: 會得功又大破賊舞陽，馬士秀、杜應金夜半降信陽城下。

translations.literal: Just then Degong again inflicted a great defeat on bandits at Wuyang; Ma Shixiu and Du Yingjin at midnight surrendered below Xinyang city.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Degong meanwhile crushed rebel forces at Wuyang; Ma Shixiu and Du Yingjin surrendered outside Xinyang in the dead of night.

sentences.zh: 獻忠為左良玉所創，幾被擒，其下饑困多散去。

translations.literal: Xianzhong was wounded by Zuo Liangyu and was almost captured; his followers, hungry and distressed, mostly dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong was mauled by Zuo Liangyu and nearly taken; hunger drove most of his men away.

sentences.zh: 獻忠窮蹙，亦因陳洪範以降。

translations.literal: Xianzhong, cornered, also surrendered through Chen Hongfan.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Zhang Xianzhong also submitted through Chen Hongfan.

sentences.zh: 於是嗣昌議功罪，絀洪承疇、曹變蛟等，而稱文燦功焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sichang deliberated merits and faults, demoted Hong Chengchou, Cao Bianjiao, and others, and praised Wencan's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang then graded rewards and punishments—demoting Hong Chengchou, Cao Bianjiao, and others while praising Wencan's achievement.

sentences.zh: 已而京軍解遂平圍，斬獲三千有奇。

translations.literal: Presently the capital troops relieved the siege of Suiping and beheaded and captured somewhat more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the capital armies lifted the siege of Suiping and killed or captured somewhat more than three thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 時文燦在裕州，馬進忠、羅汝才十三家賊聚南陽，文燦下令，殺賊者償死。

translations.literal: At this time Wencan was at Yuzhou; Ma Jinzhong, Luo Ruocai, and the bandits of thirteen houses gathered at Nanyang; Wencan issued an order that whoever killed bandits would compensate with death.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan was at Yuzhou when Ma Jinzhong, Luo Ruocai, and thirteen rebel bands gathered at Nanyang. He decreed that soldiers who slew rebels would themselves be put to death.

sentences.zh: 賊不肯從，則賫金帛酒牢犒之，名曰「求賊」。

translations.literal: If bandits would not comply, then gold, silk, wine, and livestock were sent to reward them, called "seeking bandits."
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels refused terms, he sent gold, silk, wine, and livestock as rewards—a practice called "seeking the bandits."

sentences.zh: 帝诇得狀，曰：「文燦大言無實。」

translations.literal: The emperor learned the situation by secret inquiry and said: "Wencan's big talk has no substance.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this through intelligence, the emperor said, "Wencan talks big but delivers nothing.

sentences.zh: 文燦恐。

translations.literal: Wencan was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan was terrified.

sentences.zh: 孫傳庭出關擊賊，文燦不救，而嗣昌已入政府掌中樞矣。

translations.literal: Sun Chuanting went out of the pass to strike bandits; Wencan did not rescue him, while Sichang had already entered the government and held the central pivot.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuanting marched out to fight the rebels; Wencan did not support him, while Yang Sichang had already entered the cabinet and controlled the central government.

sentences.zh: 九月，文燦次襄陽，賊分踞鄖、襄諸險。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wencan halted at Xiangyang; bandits divided and held the dangerous passes of Yun and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he took station at Xiangyang as rebels seized strongpoints across Yun and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 諸將請戰，文燦議分兵。

translations.literal: The generals requested battle; Wencan deliberated on dividing the army.
translations.idiomatic: His commanders asked to fight; Wencan proposed splitting forces.

sentences.zh: 盧九德曰：「兵分則力弱，一失利，全軍搖矣。

translations.literal: Lu Jiude said: "If troops are divided, strength is weak; one defeat and the whole army is shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jiude objected: "Split the army and you weaken it; one setback shakes the whole force.

sentences.zh: 莫若厚集其力而合擊之。」

translations.literal: Better thickly to concentrate force and strike together.
translations.idiomatic: Better to mass everything for one combined blow.

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The assembly said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: All agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃以僉事張大經監大將左良玉、陳洪範軍，以通判孔貞會監副將龍在田軍，戰於雙溝，大破之，斬首二千餘級。

translations.literal: Thereupon intendant Zhang Dajing supervised the armies of great generals Zuo Liangyu and Chen Hongfan, and subprefect Kong Zhenhui supervised Vice General Long Zaitian's army; they fought at Shuanggou, inflicted a great defeat, and beheaded more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They appointed intendant Zhang Dajing to oversee Zuo Liangyu and Chen Hongfan, subprefect Kong Zhenhui to oversee vice commander Long Zaitian, fought at Shuanggou, routed the enemy, and took more than two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 羅汝才、惠登相率九營走均州，李萬慶率三營走光、固。

translations.literal: Luo Ruocai and Hui Dengxiang led nine camps to flee toward Yunzhou; Li Wanqing led three camps to flee toward Guang and Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Ruocai and Hui Dengxiang fled toward Yunzhou with nine camps; Li Wanqing took three camps toward Guang and Gu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，京師戒嚴，召洪承疇、孫傳庭入衛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the capital declared martial alert and summoned Hong Chengchou and Sun Chuanting to defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, as Beijing went on alert, Hong Chengchou and Sun Chuanting were recalled to defend the capital.

sentences.zh: 汝才等以為討己也，懼而叩太和山提督中官，求撫於文燦，許之。

translations.literal: Ruocai and the others thought it was to attack them; afraid, they appealed to the eunuch superintendent of Mount Taihe and sought pacification from Wencan, who agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Ruocai and the others feared the move was aimed at them; they petitioned the eunuch superintendent on Mount Taihe and asked Wencan for peace terms, which he granted.

sentences.zh: 處汝才及一丈青、小秦王、一條龍四營於鄖縣，處登相及王國寧、常德安、楊友賢、王光恩五營於均州。

translations.literal: He stationed Ruocai and the four camps Yizhangqing, Xiao Qinwang, and Yitiaolong at Yun county; he stationed Dengxiang and the five camps Wang Guoning, Chang Dean, Yang Youxian, and Wang Guang'en at Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He settled Luo Ruocai's four camps—including Yizhangqing, Little Qin Wang, and One Dragon—at Yun county, and Hui Dengxiang's five camps—including Wang Guoning, Chang Dean, Yang Youxian, and Wang Guang'en—at Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 上言：「臣於李萬慶、賀一龍、馬光玉及順天王主剿，他皆主撫。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Your subject will chiefly suppress Li Wanqing, He Yilong, Ma Guangyu, and Shuntian Wang; the rest will chiefly be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "I propose to pursue Li Wanqing, He Yilong, Ma Guangyu, and Shuntian Wang, while pacifying the rest.

sentences.zh: 請赦汝才等罪，授之官。」

translations.literal: I beg to pardon the crimes of Ruocai and others and grant them offices.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Luo Ruocai and the others be pardoned and given official posts.

sentences.zh: 可之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 時京軍、良玉軍皆以入衛行，馬士秀、杜應金遂叛於許州。

translations.literal: At this time the capital army and Liangyu's army were both on the road to enter the capital guard; Ma Shixiu and Du Yingjin then rebelled at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With the capital troops and Zuo Liangyu's forces all marching to defend the throne, Ma Shixiu and Du Yingjin rebelled at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，士秀等降，良玉以其眾處許之郊外。

translations.literal: Initially Shixiu and the others had surrendered; Liangyu stationed their troops in the suburbs of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiu and his men had earlier submitted; Liangyu had quartered them outside Xu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 許，大州也，良玉諸將寄孥與賄焉。

translations.literal: Xu was a great prefecture; Liangyu's generals lodged wives and children there and offered bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was a major prefectural seat, and Liangyu's officers kept their families there and paid bribes.

sentences.zh: 良玉久征不歸，士秀、應金在文燦軍中，偽請急，假良玉軍號入城。

translations.literal: Liangyu had been on campaign long without returning; Shixiu and Yingjin were in Wencan's army; they feigned an emergency plea and, borrowing Liangyu's army designation, entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu was still away on campaign. Shixiu and Yingjin, serving under Wencan, faked an urgent dispatch and entered the city under Liangyu's banner.

sentences.zh: 夜半，兵從府第出，燒城南樓，劫庫，殺官吏，挈其貲投萬慶。

translations.literal: At midnight troops issued from the prefectural residence, burned the southern tower of the wall, looted the treasury, killed officials, and took their wealth to join Wanqing.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight his men burst from the yamen, torched the southern gate tower, raided the treasury, killed officials, and carried the loot to Wanqing.

sentences.zh: 萬慶者，賊魁射塌天也。

translations.literal: Wanqing was the bandit chieftain Shedetian.
translations.idiomatic: Wanqing was the rebel leader known as Shedetian.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，良玉還，破降馬進忠，使劉國能擊降萬慶，士秀、應金亦再降。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year Liangyu returned, defeated and received the surrender of Ma Jinzhong, had Liu Guoneng attack and receive the surrender of Wanqing; Shixiu and Yingjin also surrendered again.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year twelve Liangyu returned, broke Ma Jinzhong and took his surrender, sent Liu Guoneng to subdue Wanqing, and Shixiu and Yingjin submitted once more.

sentences.zh: 順天王已前死，其黨順義王為其下所殺。

translations.literal: Shuntian Wang had already died earlier; his follower Shunyi Wang was killed by his own subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian Wang was already dead; his lieutenant Shunyi Wang was killed by his own men.

sentences.zh: 文燦遂上言：「臣兵威震懾，降者接踵。

translations.literal: Wencan then memorialized: "Your servant's military prestige inspires awe; those who surrender follow one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan memorialized, "My troops have struck such fear that surrendering rebels come in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 十三家之賊，惟革、左及馬光玉三部尚稽天誅，可歲月平也。」

translations.literal: Of the bandits of thirteen houses, only the Ge, Zuo, and Ma Guangyu three divisions still await heaven's punishment—they can be pacified within months."
translations.idiomatic: Of the thirteen rebel bands, only the Ge, Zuo, and Ma Guangyu factions still defy imperial justice; they can be crushed within a few months."

sentences.zh: 帝優詔報之。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a gracious edict of approval.

sentences.zh: 初，張獻忠之降也，擁兵萬人踞谷城，索十萬人餉，文燦及中外要人曰與之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zhang Xianzhong surrendered, he held ten thousand troops and occupied Gucheng, demanding provisions for a hundred thousand men; Wencan and powerful men inside and outside the court daily gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xianzhong first submitted, he kept ten thousand men at Gucheng and demanded rations for a hundred thousand; Wencan and court favorites supplied them day after day.

sentences.zh: 為請官、請地、請關防矣，獻忠列軍狀曰請備遣，既而三檄其兵不應，朝野知獻忠必叛也。

translations.literal: They had requested offices, land, and seals of authority; Xianzhong listed a military roster saying he requested deployment; soon three imperial decrees summoning his troops went unanswered, and court and countryside knew Xianzhong would surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: He had been granted posts, land, and seals, and filed troop rolls asking to be sent on duty; yet three summonses to move his men went ignored, and everyone knew Xianzhong would rebel.

sentences.zh: 其後，汝才降，不肯釋甲。

translations.literal: Afterward Ruocai surrendered but refused to lay down armor.
translations.idiomatic: Later Luo Ruocai submitted but would not disarm.

sentences.zh: 及進忠、萬慶等並降，文燦以為得策，謂天下且無賊也。

translations.literal: When Jinzhong, Wanqing, and the rest all surrendered, Wencan thought he had hit on the right strategy and said the realm would soon be without bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jinzhong, Wanqing, and the others had all surrendered, Wencan believed his policy had worked and declared that banditry was nearly ended.

sentences.zh: 五月，獻忠遂反於谷城，劫汝才於房縣，於是九營俱反。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Xianzhong then rebelled at Gucheng, seized Ruocai at Fang county, and thereupon all nine camps rebelled together.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Xianzhong rose again at Gucheng, dragged Luo Ruocai away at Fang county, and all nine camps followed him into revolt.

sentences.zh: 初，均州五營懼見討，自疑，相與歃血拒獻忠，無何亦叛去。

translations.literal: Initially the five camps at Junzhou feared being attacked, grew suspicious, swore blood oaths together to resist Xianzhong, and before long also rebelled and left.
translations.idiomatic: The five Junzhou camps, fearing punishment, grew uneasy, swore blood brotherhood to resist Xianzhong, and soon broke away as well.

sentences.zh: 帝聞變，大驚，削文燦官，戴罪視事。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of the upheaval, was greatly alarmed, stripped Wencan of rank, and ordered him to continue duties while bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of the disaster he was shaken, demoted Wencan, and made him serve on while under sentence.

sentences.zh: 七月，良玉擊獻忠羅英山，敗績。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Liangyu attacked Xianzhong at Luoyingshan and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Liangyu fought Xianzhong at Luoyingshan and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，命嗣昌來代。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered Sichang to come replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and summoned Yang Sichang to take his place.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌已至軍，即遣使逮文燦下獄，坐大辟，所親姚明恭柄國而不能救也。

translations.literal: Sichang had already reached the army and immediately sent envoys to arrest Wencan and put him in prison; sentenced to death by the utmost penalty; his intimate Yao Minggong held state power but could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang had barely reached headquarters when he had Wencan arrested and jailed on a capital charge. Yao Minggong, his patron at court, held power but could not save him.

sentences.zh: 十三年十月，文燦竟棄市。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year Wencan was finally executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year thirteen Wencan was put to death in public.

sentences.zh: 練國事，字君豫，永城人。

translations.literal: Lian Guoshi, style name Junyu, was a native of Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Guoshi, courtesy name Junyu, came from Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授沛縣知縣，調山陽。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Pei county and transferred to Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Pei county, then transferred to Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，征授御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he was called up and made a censor.

sentences.zh: 廣寧失守，國事請薊州、宣府、大同及山東、山西、河南撫臣各練兵萬，以壯山海聲援。

translations.literal: When Guangning fell, Guoshi requested that the grand coordinators of Jizhou, Xuanfu, Datong, and Shandong, Shanxi, and Henan each train ten thousand troops to strengthen the voice of support for Shanhai Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangning was lost he urged the governors of Jizhou, Xuanfu, Datong, Shandong, Shanxi, and Henan each to drill ten thousand men to reinforce the Shanhai front.

sentences.zh: 又請捕誅殺大同妖人。

translations.literal: He also requested that the sorcerers of Datong be captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: He also called for the arrest and execution of the Datong sorcerers.

sentences.zh: 又疏論魏忠賢使群閹辱尚書鐘羽正，索冬衣，傷國體。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that Wei Zhongxian had his eunuchs insult Minister Zhong Yuzheng and demand winter garments, injuring the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He further denounced Wei Zhongxian for letting his eunuchs humiliate Minister Zhong Yuzheng and demand winter clothing, an affront to the court.

sentences.zh: 國事在諫垣，匡救多。

translations.literal: While Guoshi was in the remonstrance office, his corrections and rescues were many.
translations.idiomatic: During his years as a censor he offered many timely remonstrances.

sentences.zh: 給事中趙興邦，忠賢私人也，以國事為趙南星黨，劾之，削籍。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhao Xingbang, a man of Zhongxian's private faction, treated Guoshi as a partisan of Zhao Nanxing, impeached him, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Zhao Xingbang, a Wei Zhongxian ally, attacked Guoshi as a follower of Zhao Nanxing; Guoshi was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年復官，擢太僕少卿，進右僉都御史，巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen his post was restored; he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then to Right Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Restored in the first year of Chongzhen, he rose to vice minister of the Imperial Stud, then right censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 關中頻歲饑，盜賊蜂起。

translations.literal: Within the passes famine struck year after year and bandits swarmed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Famine stalked Guanzhong year after year, and rebels multiplied.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，神一元陷保安。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Shen Yiyuan took Bao'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year four Shen Yiyuan seized Bao'an.

sentences.zh: 國事遣賀虎臣援延安，而身率副將張全昌連破點燈子於中部、郃陽、韓城，又破別部於宜君、雒川，降其魁李應鰲。

translations.literal: Guoshi sent He Huchen to relieve Yan'an while he personally led Vice General Zhang Quanchang in successive defeats of Diandengzi at Zhongbu, Heyang, and Hancheng, and again defeated another band at Yijun and Luochuan, receiving the surrender of their chieftain Li Ying'ao.
translations.idiomatic: Guoshi dispatched He Huchen to Yan'an and himself led vice commander Zhang Quanchang in repeated victories over Diandengzi at Zhongbu, Heyang, and Hancheng, then routed another band at Yijun and Luochuan and took the surrender of its leader Li Ying'ao.

sentences.zh: 諸將張全昌、趙大允、王承恩、杜文煥、賀虎臣等分剿賊澄城、宜川、耀州、白水、郃陽，斬首千九百有奇。

translations.literal: Generals Zhang Quanchang, Zhao Dayun, Wang Chengen, Du Wenhuan, He Huchen, and others divided forces to pursue bandits at Chengcheng, Yichuan, Yaozhou, Baishui, and Heyang, beheading somewhat more than nineteen hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanchang, Zhao Dayun, Wang Chengen, Du Wenhuan, He Huchen, and other commanders hunted rebels through Chengcheng, Yichuan, Yaozhou, Baishui, and Heyang, taking nearly two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 總督楊鶴既受群賊降，已，復相繼叛，田近庵、李老柴陷中部。

translations.literal: After Governor Yang He had received the surrender of the mass of bandits, before long they rebelled in succession; Tian Jinyan and Li Laochai took Zhongbu.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yang He had accepted the mass surrender of the rebels, but they soon rose again; Tian Jinyan and Li Laochai seized Zhongbu.

sentences.zh: 國事偕承恩攻圍五月，克之，而所部亦頻失事，楊鶴被征，國事亦戴罪自贖。

translations.literal: Guoshi with Chengen besieged and attacked for five months and took it, but his own troops also frequently met disaster; Yang He was summoned away, and Guoshi too continued service while bearing guilt to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guoshi and Chengen besieged the place for five months and recovered it, yet his own units also suffered repeated losses. Yang He was recalled, and Guoshi likewise served on under sentence to redeem his faults.

sentences.zh: 五年，紅軍友、李都司等將犯平涼。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Hong Junyou, Li Dusi, and others were about to invade Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: In year five Hong Junyou, Li Dusi, and their bands were poised to strike Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 國事自涇趨固原，檄大帥楊嘉謨殺賊塘馬，斷其偵探。

translations.literal: Guoshi hurried from Jing to Guyuan and ordered Grand Commander Yang Jiamou to kill the bandits' relay horses and cut off their scouts.
translations.idiomatic: Guoshi rushed from Jing to Guyuan and ordered grand commander Yang Jiamou to kill the rebels' courier mounts and blind their scouts.

sentences.zh: 賊乃走慶陽西壕，嘉謨、曹文詔邀擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: The bandits then fled to the western moat of Qingyang; Jiamou and Cao Wenchao intercepted and struck them and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to the western trenches at Qingyang, where Jiamou and Cao Wenchao ambushed and routed them.

sentences.zh: 自三月至五月，大小數十戰，賊迄破滅。

translations.literal: From the third month to the fifth, in large and small battles numbering several tens, the bandits were finally destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Between the third and fifth months, in dozens of engagements large and small, the rebels were finally wiped out.

sentences.zh: 國事免戴罪。

translations.literal: Guoshi was relieved of bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Guoshi was cleared of his punitive sentence.

sentences.zh: 當是時，關中五鎮，大帥曹文詔、楊嘉謨、王承恩、楊麟、賀虎臣各督邊軍協討，總督洪承疇尤善調度。

translations.literal: At this time within the passes the five garrisons—grand commanders Cao Wenchao, Yang Jiamou, Wang Chengen, Yang Lin, and He Huchen—each directed border troops in joint suppression, while Governor Hong Chengchou was especially skilled in deployment.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the five Shaanxi garrisons—under Cao Wenchao, Yang Jiamou, Wang Chengen, Yang Lin, and He Huchen—coordinated border troops in joint campaigns, while Governor Hong Chengchou proved especially adept at marshaling them.

sentences.zh: 賊魁多殲，余盡走山西，關中稍靖。

translations.literal: Most bandit chieftains were destroyed; the remainder all fled into Shanxi, and within the passes there was gradual calm.
translations.idiomatic: Most rebel leaders were killed; the survivors fled into Shanxi, and Guanzhong grew quieter.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，賊既從澠池渡，入盧氏。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year the bandits crossed at Mianchi and entered Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year six the rebels crossed at Mianchi and entered Lushi.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊遂由河南、湖廣入漢南。

translations.literal: The next year the bandits then went from Henan and Huguang into southern Han.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they pushed from Henan and Huguang into southern Han.

sentences.zh: 總督陳奇瑜檄國事駐商州，協剿商南、盧氏賊。

translations.literal: Governor Chen Qiyu ordered Guoshi to station at Shangzhou and assist in suppressing bandits at Shangnan and Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chen Qiyu ordered Guoshi to hold Shangzhou and help suppress rebels in Shangnan and Lushi.

sentences.zh: 漢南賊遂由寧羌至兩當，掠鳳縣，出棧道，陷寶雞，關中賊復熾。

translations.literal: Southern Han bandits then went from Ningqiang to Liangdang, plundered Feng county, emerged on the plank road, took Baoji, and bandits within the passes flared up again.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong rebels moved from Ningqiang to Liangdang, raided Feng county, came out on the plank road, seized Baoji, and Guanzhong revolted anew.

sentences.zh: 既而奇瑜受賊降，檄諸軍勿擊。

translations.literal: Before long Qiyu accepted the bandits' surrender and ordered the armies not to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qiyu accepted rebel surrender terms and told the armies to stand down.

sentences.zh: 賊出險，遂大掠鳳翔、麟遊、寶雞、扶風、汧陽、乾州、涇陽、醴泉。

translations.literal: The bandits came out of the defiles and then greatly plundered Fengxiang, Linyou, Baoji, Fufeng, Qianyang, Qianzhou, Jingyang, and Liquan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels left the mountains and swept through Fengxiang, Linyou, Baoji, Fufeng, Qianyang, Qianzhou, Jingyang, and Liquan.

sentences.zh: 奇瑜委罪國事以自解，國事上言：「漢南賊盡入棧道，奇瑜檄止兵，臣未知所撫實數。

translations.literal: Qiyu shifted blame onto Guoshi to exonerate himself; Guoshi memorialized: "The southern Han bandits have all entered the plank road; Qiyu ordered the armies to halt; your servant did not know the true number pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyu blamed Guoshi to save himself. Guoshi wrote, "The Hanzhong rebels have all entered the plank road. Qiyu ordered a cease-fire, and I did not yet know how many had actually submitted.

sentences.zh: 及見奇瑜疏，八大王部萬三千餘人，蠍子塊部萬五百餘人，張妙手部九千一百餘人，八大王又一部八千三百餘人，臣不覺仰天長嘆。

translations.literal: When I saw Qiyu's memorial, the division of Ba Dashwang had somewhat more than thirteen thousand men, the division of Xiezikuai somewhat more than ten thousand five hundred, the division of Zhang Miaoshou somewhat more than nine thousand one hundred, and another division of Ba Dashwang somewhat more than eight thousand three hundred; your servant could not but sigh to heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When I read Qiyu's report—Ba Dashwang with over thirteen thousand men, Xiezikuai with over ten thousand five hundred, Zhang Miaoshou with over nine thousand one hundred, and another Ba Dashwang column with over eight thousand three hundred—I could only look up and sigh.

sentences.zh: 夫一月內，撫強寇四萬餘，盡從棧道入內地，食飲何自出，安得無剽掠？

translations.literal: Within one month more than forty thousand fierce bandits were pacified and all entered the interior through the plank road; whence were food and drink to come—how could there be no plundering?
translations.idiomatic: In a single month he had "pacified" forty thousand hardened rebels and sent them all inland by the plank road. Where were they to be fed—how could there be no looting?

sentences.zh: 且一大帥將三千人，而一賊魁反擁萬餘眾，安能受紀律？

translations.literal: Moreover one grand commander commands three thousand men, while one bandit chieftain in turn holds more than ten thousand followers—how can they accept discipline?
translations.idiomatic: A grand commander leads three thousand men, yet a single rebel chief commands more than ten thousand—how can they be kept in order?

sentences.zh: 即藉口回籍，延安州縣驟增四萬餘人，安集何所？

translations.literal: Even if they plead to return to their native districts, the prefectures and counties of Yan'an would suddenly gain more than forty thousand men—where could they be settled?
translations.idiomatic: Even if they claim they wish to go home, Yan'an prefecture would suddenly have to absorb more than forty thousand men—where could they be resettled?

sentences.zh: 合諸征剿兵不滿二萬，而降賊逾四萬，豈內地兵力所能支，宜其連陷名城而不可救也。

translations.literal: Altogether the suppression troops numbered less than twenty thousand, while surrendered bandits exceeded forty thousand—how could interior military strength support this? No wonder famous cities fell in succession and could not be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Our field armies totalled under twenty thousand, while surrendered rebels topped forty thousand. No inland force could bear that weight—no wonder great cities fell one after another beyond rescue.

sentences.zh: 若咎臣不堵剿，則先有止兵檄矣；

translations.literal: If I am blamed for not blocking and pursuing, there was already a cease-fire order;
translations.idiomatic: If I am faulted for failing to intercept them, there was already an order to halt the troops;

sentences.zh: 若雲賊已受撫，因誤殺使人致然，則未誤殺之先，何為破麟遊、永壽。

translations.literal: if it is said the bandits had already been pacified and that killing envoys by mistake caused this, then before any mistaken killing why did they take Linyou and Yongshou.
translations.idiomatic: if it is said the rebels were already pacified and only turned violent because envoys were killed by mistake, why had they already seized Linyou and Yongshou before any such killing.

sentences.zh: 今事已至此，惟急調大軍致討，若仍以願回原籍，禁兵勿剿，三秦之禍安所終極哉！」

translations.literal: Now matters have come to this; only urgently to transfer great armies to strike them down—if we still allow them to plead to return to their native districts and forbid the armies to attack, where will the calamity of the Three Qins end!"
translations.idiomatic: Matters stand as they do. Only a swift mobilization of major forces can answer them. If we again let them plead to go home and forbid our troops to fight, the Three Qins will never see an end to disaster!"

sentences.zh: 疏入，事已不可為，遂逮下獄。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, matters were already beyond remedy, and he was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, nothing could be done, and Guoshi was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 九年正月遣戍廣西。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he was banished to serve in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year nine he was exiled to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 久之，敘前功，赦還，復冠帶。

translations.literal: After a long time his earlier merit was recorded, he was pardoned and returned, and his cap and belt were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Years later his earlier service was recognized, he was pardoned and recalled, and his official rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 福王時，召為戶部左侍郎，尋改兵部。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu he was summoned as Left Vice Minister of Revenue and soon transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was called up as left vice minister of revenue, then moved to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 十二月加尚書，仍蒞侍郎事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was advanced to minister while still performing vice-minister duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was promoted to minister while continuing to handle vice-minister business.

sentences.zh: 明年二月致仕，未幾卒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year he retired from office; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired the following second month and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 丁啟睿，永城人。

translations.literal: Ding Qirui was a native of Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Qirui came from Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the forty-seventh year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，歷山東右參政，坐事謫陜西副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he served as Right Administrative Commissioner of Shandong; for an offense he was demoted to Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he was right administrative commissioner of Shandong, then demoted to Shaanxi vice commissioner after a disciplinary case.

sentences.zh: 九年，寧夏兵變，啟睿捕斬殺巡撫王楫者首惡六人，軍中大定。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when Ningxia troops mutinied, Qirui captured and beheaded the six ringleaders who had killed Grand Coordinator Wang Ji, and the army was greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine, after the Ningxia mutiny, Qirui seized and executed the six chief culprits in the killing of Grand Coordinator Wang Ji, and the garrison calmed.

sentences.zh: 再遷右布政使，分守關南，從巡撫孫傳庭討賊。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, assigned to guard the southern passes, and followed Grand Coordinator Sun Chuanting in suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted again to right provincial administration commissioner, he guarded the southern passes and campaigned with Sun Chuanting against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，就拜右僉都御史，代傳庭巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year he was immediately appointed Right Censor-in-Chief in place of Chuanting as grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year eleven he was appointed right censor-in-chief and replaced Chuanting as grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 歲頻旱，民益為盜，長武、環、白水、長安、臨潼、咸陽賊起如猬毛。

translations.literal: Drought struck year after year and the people turned increasingly to banditry; at Changwu, Huan, Baishui, Chang'an, Lintong, and Xianyang rebels rose thick as hedgehog quills.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated droughts drove more peasants to banditry; rebels sprang up like thorns at Changwu, Huan, Baishui, Chang'an, Lintong, and Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，用督師楊嗣昌薦，擢兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史，代鄭崇儉總督陜西三邊軍務討賊。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, on the recommendation of Supreme Commander Yang Sichang, he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and concurrent Right Censor-in-Chief, replacing Zheng Chongjian as governor-general of the three frontiers of Shaanxi to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen, on Yang Sichang's recommendation, he became vice minister of war and concurrent right censor-in-chief, succeeding Zheng Chongjian as governor-general of Shaanxi's three frontiers to fight the rebels.

sentences.zh: 明年，嗣昌死，加啟睿兵部尚書，改稱督師，代嗣昌盡督陜西、湖廣、河南、四川、山西及江南、北諸軍，仍兼總督陜西三邊軍務，賜劍、敕、印如嗣昌。

translations.literal: The next year, when Sichang died, Qirui was advanced to Minister of War, his title changed to Supreme Commander, and he replaced Sichang in directing all armies of Shaanxi, Huguang, Henan, Sichuan, Shanxi, and the southern and northern circuits of Jiangnan, while still concurrently governing the three frontiers of Shaanxi; he was granted sword, imperial patent, and seal as Sichang had been.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after Sichang's death, Qirui was made minister of war and supreme commander over Shaanxi, Huguang, Henan, Sichuan, Shanxi, and both Jiangnan circuits, while retaining the Shaanxi three-frontier command; he received the same sword, edict, and seal as Sichang.

sentences.zh: 啟睿自謫河西副使，數遷皆在陜西，然實庸才。

translations.literal: Qirui, from his demotion as vice commissioner west of the river, had been promoted several times yet always within Shaanxi; in truth he was a mediocrity.
translations.idiomatic: Since his demotion to the Hexi vice commissionership Qirui had risen several ranks, all within Shaanxi, yet he was genuinely a mediocrity.

sentences.zh: 為督、撫，奉督師期會，謹慎無功過；

translations.literal: As governor or grand coordinator he met the supreme commander's deadlines, was cautious, and had neither merit nor fault;
translations.idiomatic: As governor or coordinator he met Sichang's schedules, played it safe, and neither distinguished himself nor blundered badly;

sentences.zh: 及督師任重專制，即莫知為計。

translations.literal: once the burden of supreme command fell on him with sole discretion, he no longer knew what to do.
translations.idiomatic: but once given supreme command with full authority he was at a loss.

sentences.zh: 啟睿已受命出潼關，將由承天赴嗣昌軍於荊州。

translations.literal: Qirui had already received his commission and left Tong Pass; he was to go by Chengtian to join Sichang's army at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qirui had taken up his commission and crossed Tong Pass, intending to travel via Chengtian to Sichang's camp at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 湖廣巡按汪承詔言大寇在河南，荊、襄幸息警，無煩大軍，盡匿漢津船。

translations.literal: Huguang surveillance commissioner Wang Chengzhao said the great bandits were in Henan, Jing and Xiang were fortunately quiet, there was no need for a great army, and he hid all boats on the Han crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang surveillance commissioner Wang Chengzhao claimed the main rebels were in Henan, that Jing and Xiang were finally calm, that no large force was needed, and hid every boat on the Han crossing.

sentences.zh: 啟睿至，五日不得渡，折而向鄧州，州人閉門詬；

translations.literal: When Qirui arrived he could not cross for five days, turned toward Dengzhou, and the townspeople shut their gates and reviled him;
translations.idiomatic: Qirui waited five days without a crossing, detoured toward Dengzhou, and was met with barred gates and curses;

sentences.zh: 過內鄉，長吏閉之糴。

translations.literal: passing Neixiang, the local officials refused him grain.
translations.idiomatic: at Neixiang the magistrates would not sell his men grain.

sentences.zh: 軍行荒山間，割馬騾，燎以野草，士啖不得飽。

translations.literal: The army marched through barren mountains, butchered horses and mules, roasted them over wild grass, and the soldiers could not eat their fill.
translations.idiomatic: They tramped barren hills, slaughtered horses and mules, roasted the meat over scrub, and the troops still went hungry.

sentences.zh: 是時李自成已陷洛陽，圍開封，有眾七十萬，啟睿憚不敢援。

translations.literal: At this time Li Zicheng had already taken Luoyang and besieged Kaifeng, with a host of seven hundred thousand; Qirui feared him and dared not relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had already seized Luoyang and was besieging Kaifeng with seven hundred thousand men; Qirui was afraid and would not march to its aid.

sentences.zh: 聞張獻忠在光山、固始間，少弱，乃謀於諸將曰：「上命我剿豫賊，此亦豫賊也。」

translations.literal: Hearing that Zhang Xianzhong was between Guangshan and Gushi and was the weaker force, he then deliberated with the generals, saying: "The emperor ordered me to suppress Henan bandits—this too is a Henan bandit."
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhang Xianzhong was operating between Guangshan and Gushi and seemed the weaker foe, he told his commanders, "The throne ordered me to crush Henan rebels—and these are Henan rebels too."

sentences.zh: 遂檄左良玉破之於麻城，斬首千二百。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Zuo Liangyu to defeat them at Macheng and behead twelve hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Zuo Liangyu against them at Macheng, where twelve hundred heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 開封日告急，則曰：「我方有事於獻忠，不赴矣。」

translations.literal: Kaifeng daily reported urgency, and he said: "I am just now busy with Xianzhong and will not go.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng sent desperate appeals daily, but he replied, "I am engaged with Xianzhong and cannot come.

sentences.zh: 聞傅宗龍將入關督秦師，啟睿曰「三邊已置總督矣」，乞帝更敕書，乃更敕書宗龍辦自成。

translations.literal: Hearing that Fu Zonglong was about to enter the pass to command the Qin armies, Qirui said, "The three frontiers already have a governor-general," and begged the emperor for a revised commission; thereupon the commission was revised for Zonglong to handle Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Fu Zonglong was entering the pass to command the Qin armies, Qirui protested, "The three frontiers already have a governor-general," and asked the emperor to rewrite the orders—so Zonglong was directed against Zicheng instead.

sentences.zh: 九月，宗龍敗歿於項城，啟睿不能救。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Zonglong was defeated and killed at Xiangcheng; Qirui could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zonglong was destroyed at Xiangcheng, and Qirui never reached him.

sentences.zh: 賊乘勝陷南陽，殺唐王，開、汝二郡望風下。

translations.literal: The bandits pressed their victory and took Nanyang, killed the Prince of Tang, and the prefectures of Kai and Ru submitted at the mere rumor of their approach.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels swept on to seize Nanyang, kill the Prince of Tang, and bring Kai and Ru prefectures over without a fight.

sentences.zh: 十二月，自成再圍開封。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Zicheng again besieged Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zicheng besieged Kaifeng again.

sentences.zh: 河南巡撫高名衡飛檄至，啟睿督兵赴之，避賊入城，部下大淫掠。

translations.literal: Henan Grand Coordinator Gao Mingheng sent an urgent dispatch; Qirui led troops to the rescue, avoided the bandits by entering the city, and his subordinates committed great licentious plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Gao Mingheng sent frantic dispatches. Qirui marched to relieve the city, slipped inside the walls to avoid the rebels, and his men looted savagely.

sentences.zh: 總兵陳永福射自成，中其左目。

translations.literal: Commander Chen Yongfu shot Zicheng and struck his left eye.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Chen Yongfu shot Zicheng in the left eye.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，賊解圍去。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the bandits lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the rebels raised the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 啟睿之在許州也，畏賊逼，始赴開封。

translations.literal: When Qirui was at Xuzhou he feared the bandits' pressure and only then set out for Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: While Qirui lingered at Xuzhou, afraid of the rebels, he moved toward Kaifeng only under pressure.

sentences.zh: 離城三十里，而城即破。

translations.literal: Thirty li from the city, the city was on the verge of falling.
translations.idiomatic: He was still thirty li away when the city nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 其抵開封，啟門入，賊乘之，幾陷。

translations.literal: When he reached Kaifeng the gates were opened to admit him, and the bandits seized the moment—he was nearly lost.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered Kaifeng the gates were opened for him, the rebels rushed the breach, and the city nearly fell with him inside.

sentences.zh: 四月，自成合群賊復攻開封。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Zicheng united the mass of bandits and again attacked Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zicheng joined the rebel hosts and attacked Kaifeng again.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝釋侯恂於獄，命督援剿諸軍救開封。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the emperor released Hou Xun from prison and ordered him to supervise the relief armies in rescuing Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor freed Hou Xun from prison and put him in charge of the relief forces for Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 未至，開封圍益急。

translations.literal: Before he arrived the siege of Kaifeng grew still more pressing.
translations.idiomatic: Before Hou Xun arrived the siege tightened still further.

sentences.zh: 帝數詔切責啟睿。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly issued edicts sternly reproaching Qirui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent edict after edict sharply rebuking Qirui.

sentences.zh: 啟睿不得已，乃大集良玉、虎大威、楊德政、方國安之軍，偕保定總督楊文嶽，以七月會於朱仙鎮，與賊壘相望。

translations.literal: Qirui had no choice; he then greatly gathered the armies of Liang Yu, Hu Dawei, Yang Dezheng, and Fang Guo'an, together with Baoding Grand Coordinator Yang Wenyue, and in the seventh month met at Zhuxian Town, their camps facing the bandits across the field.
translations.idiomatic: With no alternative, Qirui mustered the forces of Liang Yu, Hu Dawei, Yang Dezheng, and Fang Guo'an, joined by Baoding grand coordinator Yang Wenyue. In the seventh month they assembled at Zhuxian Town, camped face to face with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊眾百萬，啟睿欲戰，良玉曰：「賊鋒銳，未可擊也。」

translations.literal: The bandits numbered a million; Qirui wished to fight. Liang Yu said: "The bandits' front is sharp; they cannot yet be struck."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were said to number a million. Qirui wanted to attack. Liang Yu said, "Their vanguard is too sharp—we cannot strike yet."

sentences.zh: 啟睿曰：「圍已急，必擊之。」

translations.literal: Qirui said: "The siege is already urgent; we must strike them."
translations.idiomatic: Qirui replied, "The siege is critical. We must attack."

sentences.zh: 諸將皆懼。

translations.literal: All the generals were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Every general was afraid.

sentences.zh: 良玉歸營即先走，諸營俱走，啟睿、文嶽聯騎奔汝寧。

translations.literal: Liang Yu returned to camp and fled first; every camp fled; Qirui and Wenyue rode together in flight to Runing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yu went back to camp and fled at once; every camp followed. Qirui and Wenyue rode together to Runing.

sentences.zh: 賊渡河逐之，追奔四百里。

translations.literal: The bandits crossed the river and pursued them, chasing the flight four hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels crossed the river in pursuit and chased the rout four hundred li.

sentences.zh: 喪馬騾七千，將士數萬，啟睿敕書、印、劍俱失。

translations.literal: They lost seven thousand horses and mules and tens of thousands of officers and men; Qirui's imperial patent, seal, and sword were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Seven thousand horses and mules were lost, along with tens of thousands of troops. Qirui's imperial commission, seal, and sword were all lost.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔褫職候代。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict stripped him of office pending replacement.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was stripped of office and ordered to await a successor.

sentences.zh: 九月，賊決馬家口河灌開封，開封遂陷，乃征下吏，久之釋歸。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the bandits breached the river at Majiakou to flood Kaifeng; Kaifeng then fell; he was summoned as a criminal; after a long time he was released to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the rebels broke the river at Majiakou to flood Kaifeng, and the city fell. Qirui was handed over to the judicial authorities; long afterward he was released to go home.

sentences.zh: 自嗣昌死二年而啟睿敗，啟睿敗又二年而明亡矣。

translations.literal: From Sichang's death, two years to Qirui's defeat; from Qirui's defeat, two years more and the Ming perished.
translations.idiomatic: Two years after Sichang's death came Qirui's defeat; two years after Qirui's defeat the Ming dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 福王時，啟睿夤緣馬士英充為事官，督河南勸農、剿寇諸務。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu, Qirui curried favor with Ma Shiying and was appointed Acting Commissioner, overseeing Henan matters of encouraging agriculture and suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Qirui used his connection with Ma Shiying to become an acting commissioner overseeing Henan agriculture and bandit suppression.

sentences.zh: 尋以擒斬歸德偽官，拜兵部尚書，加太子太保，官其一子。

translations.literal: Soon, for capturing and beheading false officials at Guide, he was made Minister of War, advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and one son was granted office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for capturing and executing puppet officials at Guide, he was made minister of war, promoted to grand guardian of the heir apparent, and one son was granted office.

sentences.zh: 事敗，脫身旋裏，久之卒。

translations.literal: When affairs failed he escaped and returned home; after a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the cause collapsed he slipped away home and died years later.

sentences.zh: 從父魁楚，崇禎四年春，以右僉都御史巡撫保定。

translations.literal: His uncle Kui Chu, in the spring of the fourth year of Chongzhen, served as Right Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Kui Chu, in the spring of Chongzhen year four, was right censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢兵部右侍郎，代傅宗龍總督薊、遼、保定軍務。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and replaced Fu Zonglong as grand coordinator of Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he was promoted to right vice minister of war and replaced Fu Zonglong as grand coordinator of Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，畿輔被兵，魁楚坐下吏，久之放還。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year, when the capital region suffered invasion, Kui Chu was handed over to the judicial authorities; after a long time he was released to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year nine the capital region was invaded; Kui Chu was handed over to the courts and, long afterward, released to return home.

sentences.zh: 福王時，起故官，總督河南、湖廣，兼巡撫承天、德安、襄陽。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu he was restored to his former rank, made grand coordinator of Henan and Huguang, and concurrently grand coordinator of Chengde, De'an, and Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was restored to office as grand coordinator of Henan and Huguang, with concurrent charge of Chengde, De'an, and Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 未赴，會兩廣總督沈猶龍入為侍郎，魁楚竟代其任。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, the Grand Coordinator of the Two Guang, Shen Youlong, entered the capital as vice minister; Kui Chu in the end replaced him in that post.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, grand coordinator of the Two Guang Shen Youlong entered the capital as vice minister, and Kui Chu ended up replacing him.

sentences.zh: 尋加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 唐王自立於福州，命以故官協理戎政。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Tang declared himself at Fuzhou, he was ordered to serve in his former rank assisting in military administration.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Tang declared himself at Fuzhou, Kui Chu was ordered to assist in military administration in his former rank.

sentences.zh: 靖江王亨嘉反桂林，下梧州，執巡撫瞿式耜。

translations.literal: Prince Jingjiang Hengjia rebelled at Guilin, descended on Wuzhou, and seized Grand Coordinator Qu Shisi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingjiang Hengjia rebelled at Guilin, marched down to Wuzhou, and seized grand coordinator Qu Shisi.

sentences.zh: 魁楚檄思恩參將陳邦傳等襲走之，獲於桂林。

translations.literal: Kui Chu issued orders to Sinian Assistant Commander Chen Bangchuan and others to attack and drive him off; he was captured at Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Kui Chu ordered Sinian assistant commander Chen Bangchuan and others to attack and drive him off; Hengjia was captured at Guilin.

sentences.zh: 封魁楚平粵伯，仍留鎮兩廣。

translations.literal: Kui Chu was enfeoffed as Earl Pacifier of Yue and remained to garrison the Two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Kui Chu was enfeoffed as Earl Pacifier of Yue and remained to garrison the Two Guang.

sentences.zh: 閩中事敗，與式耜擁立桂王於肇慶，進東閣大學士，兼理戎政。

translations.literal: When affairs in Min failed, he and Shisi installed the Prince of Gui at Zhaoqing; he was advanced to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and concurrently directed military administration.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fujian cause collapsed, he and Shisi installed the Prince of Gui at Zhaoqing; Kui Chu was made grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and directed military affairs.

sentences.zh: 大清兵下廣州，漸迫肇慶。

translations.literal: Great Qing troops took Guangzhou and gradually pressed upon Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Qing forces took Guangzhou and gradually closed on Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 魁楚奉王走梧州，復棄之，走岑溪。

translations.literal: Kui Chu escorted the prince in flight to Wuzhou, then abandoned him again and fled to Cenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Kui Chu escorted the prince to Wuzhou, then abandoned him and fled to Cenxi.

sentences.zh: 輜重多，舳艫相屬，為大將李成棟追獲，魁楚遂降。

translations.literal: With heavy baggage, boats and ships following one another in succession, he was overtaken and captured by the great general Li Chengdong; Kui Chu thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Laden with baggage and a long train of boats, he was overtaken and captured by the great general Li Chengdong, and Kui Chu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 成棟與有隙，錄其家數百人殺之，魁楚乞一子，成棟笑曰：「汝身且莫保，尚求活人耶？」

translations.literal: Chengdong bore a grudge against him and registered several hundred of his household for execution. Kui Chu begged for one son. Chengdong laughed and said: "Your own person cannot even be preserved—yet you still ask for a living person?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengdong bore a grudge against him and registered several hundred of his household for execution. Kui Chu begged for one son. Chengdong laughed and said, "You cannot even save yourself—yet you ask for a living man?"

sentences.zh: 並殺之。

translations.literal: He killed them all together.
translations.idiomatic: He killed them all.

sentences.zh: 鄭崇儉，字大章，寧鄉人。

translations.literal: Zheng Chongjian, styled Dazhang, was a native of Ningxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chongjian, styled Dazhang, was from Ningxiang.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授河南府推官，歷濟南兵備副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Henan prefecture and served successively as military defense vice commissioner of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor of Henan prefecture and later served as Jinan military defense vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，遷陜西右參政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was transferred to Right Administrative Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he was transferred to right administrative commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 屢遷右僉都御史，巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: After repeated promotions he became Right Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he became right censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 數敗套寇，賚銀幣，世蔭錦衣副千戶。

translations.literal: He repeatedly defeated the Tatar bandits, was rewarded with silver and silks, and his family received hereditary appointment as vice battalion commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly defeated the Tatar raiders, was rewarded with silver and silks, and his family received hereditary rank as vice battalion commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，擢兵部右侍郎，代洪承疇總督陜西三邊軍務。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and replaced Hong Chengchou as grand coordinator of the Three Frontiers military affairs in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year twelve he was promoted to right vice minister of war and replaced Hong Chengchou as grand coordinator of Shaanxi's Three Frontiers.

sentences.zh: 五月，張獻忠反谷城，羅汝才等九營皆反，興安告警。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Zhang Xianzhong rebelled at Gucheng; Luo Rucai and the other nine camps all rebelled, and Xing'an raised the alarm.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhang Xianzhong rebelled at Gucheng; Luo Rucai and the other nine camps followed, and Xing'an sounded the alarm.

sentences.zh: 總理熊文燦請敕楚撫方孔炤防荊門、當陽，鄖撫王鰲永防江陵、遠安，陜撫丁啟睿、蜀撫邵捷春各嚴兵於其境。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xiong Wencan requested an imperial order that Huguang Grand Coordinator Fang Kongzhao guard Jingmen and Dangyang, Yun Grand Coordinator Wang Aoyong guard Jiangling and Yuan'an, and Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Ding Qirui and Sichuan Grand Coordinator Shao Jiechun each tighten their troops within their jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretary Xiong Wencan asked for orders that Huguang coordinator Fang Kongzhao hold Jingmen and Dangyang, Yun coordinator Wang Aoyong hold Jiangling and Yuan'an, and Shaanxi coordinator Ding Qirui and Sichuan coordinator Shao Jiechun each tighten defenses in their territories.

sentences.zh: 而崇儉主提兵合擊，時固原、臨洮、寧夏三總兵左光先、曹變蛟、馬科隨承疇人衛，柴時華中道還甘肅，征之不應，崇儉乃檄副將賀人龍、李國奇等軍發西安。

translations.literal: Chongjian advocated leading troops in a joint attack. At the time the three regional commanders of Guyuan, Lintao, and Ningxia—Zuo Guangxian, Cao Bianjiao, and Ma Ke—had followed Chengchou in entering guard [duty]; Chai Shihua had turned back mid-route to Gansu and did not respond when summoned; Chongjian thereupon ordered the armies of Deputy Generals He Renlong, Li Guoqi, and others to depart from Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjian, however, wanted a joint offensive. The three regional commanders of Guyuan, Lintao, and Ningxia—Zuo Guangxian, Cao Bianjiao, and Ma Ke—had gone with Hong Chengchou to enter the capital on guard duty; Chai Shihua had turned back to Gansu en route and did not answer the summons. Chongjian then ordered deputy generals He Renlong, Li Guoqi, and others to march from Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 國奇至洛陽，卒大噪，剽瑞王租。

translations.literal: When Guoqi reached Luoyang the troops made a great uproar and plundered the Prince of Rui's grain rents.
translations.idiomatic: When Guoqi reached Luoyang the troops mutinied loudly and plundered the Prince of Rui's grain rents.

sentences.zh: 國奇已擢陜西總兵官，坐停新命，崇儉亦貶一秩。

translations.literal: Guoqi had already been promoted to regional commander of Shaanxi; for this he was made to halt his new appointment, and Chongjian was also demoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi had already been promoted to Shaanxi regional commander; for the riot his new appointment was suspended, and Chongjian was demoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 獻忠既叛，大敗左良玉軍於房縣之羅英山，謀入陜。

translations.literal: After Xianzhong had rebelled, he utterly defeated Zuo Liangyu's army at Luoying Mountain in Fang County and planned to enter Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xianzhong had rebelled, he crushed Zuo Liangyu's army at Luoying Mountain in Fang County and planned to enter Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 崇儉率人龍、國奇軍扼之興安，賊還走興山、太平，處楚、蜀交。

translations.literal: Chongjian led the armies of Renlong and Guoqi to block them at Xing'an; the bandits turned back through Xingshan and Taiping, in the borderland between Chu and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjian led Renlong and Guoqi to block them at Xing'an; the rebels turned back through Xingshan and Taiping, on the border between Huguang and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 是時，楊嗣昌已出師，入文燦軍而代之矣。

translations.literal: At this time Yang Sichang had already taken the field, entered Wencan's army, and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yang Sichang had taken the field, entered Wencan's command, and replaced him.

sentences.zh: 先是，尚書傅宗龍議令崇儉兼督蜀軍，而嗣昌亦檄秦軍入蜀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Minister Fu Zonglong had proposed that Chongjian concurrently supervise Shu armies, and Sichang also ordered Qin armies into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier minister Fu Zonglong had proposed that Chongjian also supervise Sichuan forces, and Sichang likewise ordered Shaanxi troops into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 崇儉乃以十三年二月率人龍、國奇會良玉大敗賊於瑪瑙山，獲首功千三百三十有三，降賊將二十有五人，獲馬騾、甲仗無算。

translations.literal: Chongjian then in the second month of the thirteenth year led Renlong and Guoqi to join Liangyu and inflicted a great defeat on the bandits at Mount Magna, obtaining 1,333 counted heads, twenty-five surrendered rebel generals, and countless horses, mules, armor, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year thirteen Chongjian led Renlong and Guoqi to join Liangyu and inflicted a great defeat on the rebels at Mount Magna, taking 1,333 heads, twenty-five surrendered rebel generals, and countless horses, mules, armor, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 是役也，崇儉身在行，而嗣昌遠處襄陽。

translations.literal: In this campaign Chongjian was personally in the field, while Sichang remained far away at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign Chongjian was in the field himself, while Sichang stayed far away at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 及論功，所賜半嗣昌，但增一秩，復先所降一秩而已。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed, half the rewards went to Sichang; Chongjian received only one additional rank, merely restoring the rank previously taken from him.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were apportioned, half went to Sichang; Chongjian received only one rank—and that merely restored the rank he had earlier lost.

sentences.zh: 獻忠既敗，竄柯家坪，蜀將張令追之，被圍。

translations.literal: After Xianzhong was defeated he fled to Kejiaping; Shu general Zhang Ling pursued him and was surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat Xianzhong fled to Kejiaping; Sichuan general Zhang Ling pursued him and was surrounded.

sentences.zh: 崇儉遣兵擊走賊，人龍、國奇等復追敗之寒溪寺、鹽井，先後斬首千五百級，其黨順天王、一條龍、一隻龍皆降。

translations.literal: Chongjian sent troops to strike and drive off the bandits; Renlong, Guoqi, and others again pursued and defeated them at Hanxisi and Yanjing, beheading in succession 1,500 ranks; his followers Shuntian Wang, Yitiaolong, and Yizhilong all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjian sent troops to drive the rebels off; Renlong, Guoqi, and others pursued and defeated them again at Hanxisi and Yanjing, taking 1,500 heads in all. Followers Shuntian Wang, Yitiaolong, and Yizhilong all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 崇儉軍五日三捷，威名甚振。

translations.literal: Chongjian's army gained three victories in five days; his renown greatly swelled.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjian's army won three victories in five days, and his fame soared.

sentences.zh: 以年衰乞骸骨，不許，令率總兵鄭家棟還關中，留人龍、國奇討賊。

translations.literal: On account of age he begged to retire with his bones; the request was denied. He was ordered to lead Regional Commander Zheng Jiadong back to Guanzhong, leaving Renlong and Guoqi to pursue the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on grounds of age; the request was denied. He was ordered to lead regional commander Zheng Jiadong back to Guanzhong while Renlong and Guoqi remained to pursue the rebels.

sentences.zh: 當是時，獻忠竄伏興、歸山中。

translations.literal: At that time Xianzhong lurked hidden in the mountains of Xing and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xianzhong was hiding in the mountains of Xing and Gui.

sentences.zh: 秦、楚師俱集於夔，諸將協心窮搜深箐，千餘殘寇可盡殲。

translations.literal: Qin and Chu armies were all gathered at Kui; if the generals united in searching the deep ravines, the remaining thousand-odd bandits could be utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi and Huguang troops were all gathered at Kui; if the generals cooperated in searching the deep ravines, the remaining thousand-odd rebels could be wiped out.

sentences.zh: 崇儉既去，未幾，人龍軍亦自開縣噪而西歸，楚師遂敗績於土地嶺，蜀中由是大亂。

translations.literal: After Chongjian had gone, before long Renlong's army also mutinied at Kaixian and marched westward home; the Chu army then suffered defeat at Tudiling, and Shu was thereby thrown into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongjian left, Renlong's troops soon mutinied at Kaixian and marched west for home; the Huguang army was defeated at Tudiling, and Sichuan fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌因言崇儉撤兵太早，致賊猖獗。

translations.literal: Sichang thereupon said Chongjian had withdrawn troops too early, causing the bandits to grow rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang then said Chongjian had withdrawn too soon, allowing the rebels to run wild.

sentences.zh: 帝初以崇儉不能馭軍，不悅，及是命削籍，以啟睿赴軍前代理，而疑崇儉托疾，令按臣核實。

translations.literal: The emperor had earlier been displeased that Chongjian could not control the army; now he ordered his name struck from the rolls, sent Qirui to the front to act in his place, and suspected Chongjian of feigning illness, ordering the investigating censor to verify the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already been displeased that Chongjian could not control his troops; now he struck him from the rolls, sent Qirui to the front in his place, and suspected Chongjian of feigning illness, ordering the investigating censor to verify it.

sentences.zh: 明年春，獻忠陷襄陽，嗣昌死，帝益恨崇儉不掎角平賊也，逮下獄，責以縱兵擅還，失誤軍律。

translations.literal: The next spring Xianzhong took Xiangyang; Sichang died. The emperor hated Chongjian all the more for not coordinating pincers to pacify the bandits, arrested him and thrown into prison, and charged him with relaxing the army and returning on his own authority in violation of military law.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Xianzhong took Xiangyang and Sichang died. The emperor hated Chongjian all the more for failing to coordinate a pincer, had him arrested, and charged him with letting the army disperse and returning on his own authority in breach of military law.

sentences.zh: 不俟秋後，以五月棄市。

translations.literal: Without waiting for autumn execution, in the fifth month he was executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting for the autumn executions, he was put to death in the marketplace in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 帝自即位以來，誅總督七人，崇儉及袁崇煥、劉策、楊一鵬、熊文燦、范志完、趙光抃也。

translations.literal: From his accession the emperor had executed seven grand coordinators: Chongjian, Yuan Chonghuan, Liu Ce, Yang Yipeng, Xiong Wencan, Fan Zhiwan, and Zhao Guangbian.
translations.idiomatic: From his accession the emperor had executed seven grand coordinators: Chongjian along with Yuan Chonghuan, Liu Ce, Yang Yipeng, Xiong Wencan, Fan Zhiwan, and Zhao Guangbian.

sentences.zh: 帝憤寇日熾，用法益峻，功罪不假貸，而疆事寢壞，卒至於亡。

translations.literal: The emperor, angry that bandits grew daily stronger, applied the law ever more harshly and showed no mercy for merit or fault; frontier affairs steadily worsened until at last the dynasty perished.
translations.idiomatic: Angry that the rebels grew stronger by the day, he applied the law ever more harshly and spared neither merit nor fault; frontier affairs steadily collapsed until the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 福王時，給事中李清言：「崇儉未失一城、喪一旅，因他人巧卸，遂服上刑。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu, Supervising Secretary Li Qing said: "Chongjian lost not a single city or a single detachment; because another cleverly shifted blame onto him, he suffered the supreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, supervising secretary Li Qing said, "Chongjian lost not a single city or a single detachment; because another cleverly shifted the blame onto him, he suffered the supreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 群臣微知其冤，無敢訟言者，臣甚痛之。」

translations.literal: The officials faintly knew his injustice, yet none dared plead on his behalf; your servant is deeply pained."
translations.idiomatic: The officials faintly knew he was wronged, yet none dared speak up; your servant is deeply grieved."

sentences.zh: 崇儉冤始白。

translations.literal: Only then was Chongjian's injustice brought to light.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was Chongjian's injustice publicly acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 方孔炤，字潛夫，桐城人。

translations.literal: Fang Kongzhao, styled Qianfu, was a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Kongzhao, styled Qianfu, was from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，為職方員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he served as an outside secretary in the Bureau of Operations.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianqi he was an outside secretary in the Bureau of Operations.

sentences.zh: 忤崔呈秀，削籍。

translations.literal: He offended Cui Xianxiu and was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He offended Cui Xianxiu and was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起故官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year one he was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for mourning.

sentences.zh: 定桐城民變，還朝。

translations.literal: He quelled the popular uprising in Tongcheng and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: He quelled the Tongcheng popular uprising and returned to court.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以右僉都御史巡撫湖廣，擊賊李萬慶、馬光玉、羅汝才於承天，八戰八捷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, as Right Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Huguang, he attacked the bandits Li Wanqing, Ma Guangyu, and Luo Rucai at Chengde and won eight battles in eight encounters.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven, as right censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Huguang, he fought the rebels Li Wanqing, Ma Guangyu, and Luo Rucai at Chengde and won eight battles in eight encounters.

sentences.zh: 時文燦納獻忠降，處之谷城。

translations.literal: At the time Wencan accepted Xianzhong's surrender and settled him at Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wencan accepted Xianzhong's surrender and settled him at Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 孔炤條上八議，言主撫之誤，不聽，而陰厲士馬備戰守。

translations.literal: Kongzhao submitted eight proposals in detail, stating that relying on pacification was wrong; the court did not heed him, but he secretly strengthened troops and horses for defense and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Kongzhao submitted eight detailed proposals arguing that reliance on pacification was mistaken; the court did not listen, but he secretly strengthened troops and horses for defense.

sentences.zh: 已而賊果叛，如孔炤言。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits did rebel, just as Kongzhao had said.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels did rebel, just as Kongzhao had warned.

sentences.zh: 賊故畏孔炤，不敢東，文燦乃檄孔炤防荊門、當陽，鰲永防江陵、遠安，秦、蜀各嚴兵。

translations.literal: The bandits had long feared Kongzhao and did not dare go east; Wencan then ordered Kongzhao to guard Jingmen and Dangyang, Aoyong to guard Jiangling and Yuan'an, and Qin and Shu each to tighten their troops.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had long feared Kongzhao and would not go east; Wencan then ordered Kongzhao to hold Jingmen and Dangyang, Aoyong to hold Jiangling and Yuan'an, and Shaanxi and Sichuan each to tighten their defenses.

sentences.zh: 崇儉主合擊，孔炤乃請專斷德、黃，守承天，護獻陵；

translations.literal: Chongjian advocated joint attack; Kongzhao then asked for sole discretion over Dezhou and Huangzhou, to hold Chengde and protect the Xian tomb;
translations.idiomatic: Chongjian wanted a joint attack; Kongzhao then asked for sole authority over Dezhou and Huangzhou, to hold Chengde and protect the Xian imperial tombs;

sentences.zh: 而江、漢以南責鰲永。

translations.literal: while south of the Jiang and Han responsibility would fall on Aoyong.
translations.idiomatic: while south of the Jiang and Han the responsibility would fall on Aoyong.

sentences.zh: 會嗣昌代文燦，令孔炤仍駐當陽。

translations.literal: When Sichang replaced Wencan, he ordered Kongzhao to remain stationed at Dangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichang replaced Wencan, he ordered Kongzhao to remain at Dangyang.

sentences.zh: 惠王常潤言：「孔炤遏獻忠，有來家河、神通堡之捷，射中賊魁馬光玉，陵寢得無虞。

translations.literal: Prince Hui Changrun said: "Kongzhao checked Xianzhong and won victories at Laijia River and Shentong Fort, shooting the bandit chieftain Ma Guangyu; the imperial tombs were kept free from harm.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui Changrun said, "Kongzhao checked Xianzhong and won victories at Laijia River and Shentong Fort, shooting the rebel chief Ma Guangyu; the imperial tombs were kept safe.

sentences.zh: 請增秩久任。」

translations.literal: Request increase of rank and long tenure."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that his rank be raised and his tenure extended."

sentences.zh: 章下部，未奏，而部將楊世恩、羅安邦奉調，會川、沅兵剿竹山寇。
