translations.literal: The memorial went to the ministries; before it could be presented, his subordinate generals Yang Shien and Luo Anbang received transfer orders to join Chuan and Yuan troops in suppressing bandits at Zhushan.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the ministries; before it could be presented, his subordinate generals Yang Shien and Luo Anbang were transferred to join Chuan and Yuan troops in suppressing bandits at Zhushan.

sentences.zh: 兩將深入，至香油坪而敗。

translations.literal: The two generals went deep in and were defeated at Xiangyouping.
translations.idiomatic: The two generals advanced deep inland and were defeated at Xiangyouping.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌既以孔炤撫議異己也，又忮其言中，遂因事獨劾孔炤，逮下詔獄。

translations.literal: Sichang, who already resented Kongzhao's pacification views as opposed to his own, also envied that his words had hit the mark; he then used the incident alone to impeach Kongzhao, who was arrested and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang already resented Kongzhao's pacification views and envied that his warnings had proved correct; he used the defeat alone to impeach Kongzhao, who was arrested and sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 子檢討以智，國變後，棄家為僧，號無可者也，伏闕訟父冤，膝行沙塸者兩年。

translations.literal: His son, Hanlin Compiler Fang Yizhi, after the dynastic collapse abandoned his family to become a monk styled Wuke; he lay prostrate at the palace gate pleading his father's innocence, crawling on his knees through the ceremonial yard for two years.
translations.idiomatic: His son, Hanlin compiler Fang Yizhi, after the dynastic collapse abandoned his family to become a monk styled Wuke; he lay prostrate at the palace gate pleading his father's innocence, crawling on his knees through the ceremonial yard for two years.

sentences.zh: 帝為心動，下議，孔炤護陵寢功多，減死戍紹興。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved in heart and sent the case down for deliberation; Kongzhao's merit in protecting the tombs was great, and death was reduced to exile at Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and sent the case down for deliberation; Kongzhao's merit in protecting the tombs was great, and the death sentence was reduced to exile at Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 久之，用薦復官，以右僉都御史屯田山東、河北。

translations.literal: After a long time, on recommendation he was restored to office as Right Censor-in-Chief colonizing fields in Shandong and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, on recommendation he was restored as right censor-in-chief to develop garrison farms in Shandong and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 馳至濟南，復命兼理軍務，督大名、廣平二監司禦賊。

translations.literal: He hurried to Jinan and was again ordered to handle military affairs concurrently, supervising the two surveillance commissions of Daming and Guangping in resisting bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried to Jinan and was again ordered to handle military affairs, supervising the surveillance commissions of Daming and Guangping in resisting the rebels.

sentences.zh: 命甫下而京師陷，孔炤南奔。

translations.literal: The order had just been issued when the capital fell; Kongzhao fled south.
translations.idiomatic: The order had barely been issued when the capital fell; Kongzhao fled south.

sentences.zh: 馬、阮亂政，歸隱十餘年而終。

translations.literal: With Ma and Ruan's corrupt rule of government, he retired to seclusion for more than ten years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: Under the corrupt rule of Ma Shiying and Ruan Dayue, he lived in retirement for more than ten years and then died.

sentences.zh: 先是，有以陵寢失守獲重譴者，為楊一鵬。

translations.literal: Earlier, one who had suffered heavy punishment for the loss of the imperial tombs was Yang Yipeng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, one who had suffered heavy punishment for the loss of the imperial tombs was Yang Yipeng.

sentences.zh: 一鵬，臨湘人。

translations.literal: Yipeng was a native of Linxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yipeng was from Linxiang.

sentences.zh: 歷官大理寺丞，削籍。

translations.literal: He had served as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年，以兵部左侍郎拜戶部尚書兼右僉都御史，總督漕運，巡撫江北四府。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongzhen he was appointed from Left Vice Minister of War as Minister of Revenue concurrently holding Right Censor-in-Chief, grand coordinator of the grain transport, and grand coordinator of the four northern Jiang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year six he was promoted from left vice minister of war to minister of revenue, concurrently right censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of the grain transport, and grand coordinator of the four northern Jiang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽軍民素疾守陵太監楊澤貪虐，引賊來寇。

translations.literal: The troops and people of Fengyang had long resented the tomb-guarding eunuch Yang Ze for greed and cruelty and led bandits to invade.
translations.idiomatic: The troops and people of Fengyang had long resented the tomb-guarding eunuch Yang Ze for greed and cruelty and guided bandits to attack.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，賊遂攻陷鳳陽，焚皇陵，燒龍興寺，燔公私邸舍二萬二千六百五十，戮中都留守朱國相、指揮使程永寧等四十有一員，殺軍民數萬人。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year the bandits thereupon attacked and took Fengyang, burned the imperial tombs, burned Longxing Temple, and burned twenty-two thousand six hundred fifty public and private houses; they slew forty-one persons including Central Capital Garrison Commander Zhu Guoxiang and Commander Cheng Yongning, and killed tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year eight the rebels attacked and took Fengyang, burned the imperial tombs and Longxing Temple, and burned 22,650 public and private buildings; they killed forty-one officials including Central Capital garrison commander Zhu Guoxiang and commander Cheng Yongning, and tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 先是，賊漸逼江北，兵部尚書張鳳翼請敕一鵬移鎮鳳陽，溫體仁格其議。

translations.literal: Earlier, as bandits gradually pressed on northern Jiang, Minister of War Zhang Fengyi requested an edict that Yipeng shift his headquarters to Fengyang; Wen Tiren blocked the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as the rebels gradually pressed on northern Jiang, minister of war Zhang Fengyi asked for an edict moving Yipeng's headquarters to Fengyang; Wen Tiren blocked the proposal.

sentences.zh: 賊驟至，一鵬在淮安，遠不及救。

translations.literal: The bandits arrived suddenly; Yipeng was at Huai'an, too far to rescue in time.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels arrived suddenly; Yipeng was at Huai'an, too far away to rescue in time.

sentences.zh: 帝聞變大驚，素服避殿，親祭告太廟，遂逮一鵬及巡按御史吳振纓、守陵官澤。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of the disaster he was greatly shocked; in plain dress he left the hall, personally offered sacrifice and report at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and then arrested Yipeng, Investigating Censor Wu Zhenyuan, and tomb guard Yang Ze.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard the news he was greatly shocked; in plain dress he left the hall, personally offered sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and then arrested Yipeng, investigating censor Wu Zhenyuan, and tomb guard Yang Ze.

sentences.zh: 澤先自殺，一鵬棄市，振纓戍邊。

translations.literal: Ze first killed himself; Yipeng was executed and displayed in the market; Zhenyuan was banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Ze killed himself first; Yipeng was executed in public; Zhenyuan was banished to border service.

sentences.zh: 邵捷春，字肇復，侯官人。

translations.literal: Shao Jiechun, courtesy name Zhaofu, a native of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Jiechun, courtesy name Zhaofu, was from Houguan.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十七年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the forty-seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Wanli year forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 累官稽勛郎中。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Registrar of Merits in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to registrar of merits in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，出為四川右參政，分守川南，撫定天全六番高、楊二氏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he went out as Right Administration Commissioner of Sichuan, assigned to guard southern Sichuan, and pacified the Gao and Yang clans among the Six Fan of Tianquan.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year two he was appointed right administration commissioner of Sichuan, charged with defending southern Sichuan, and pacified the Gao and Yang clans of the Tianquan Six Fan.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 大計，坐貶。

translations.literal: At the grand evaluation he was demoted for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: At the triennial evaluation he was demoted.

sentences.zh: 久之，起四川副使，以十年秋抵成都。

translations.literal: After a long while he was raised to Vice Commissioner of Sichuan and reached Chengdu in autumn of the tenth year.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was restored as vice commissioner of Sichuan and reached Chengdu in autumn of year ten.

sentences.zh: 時秦賊已入蜀，巡撫王維章、總兵侯良柱悉眾北拒，城中惟屯田軍及蜀府護衛軍，人情恇懼，捷春啟門納鄉民避賊者。

translations.literal: At the time the Shaanxi bandits had already entered Shu; Grand Coordinator Wang Weizhang and Regional Commander Hou Liangzhu gathered all their forces north to resist; in the city there were only the colony troops and the Shu princely residence guard troops; public feeling was fearful and timid; Jiechun opened the gates to admit villagers fleeing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi rebels had already entered Sichuan; grand coordinator Wang Weizhang and regional commander Hou Liangzhu took all their troops north to resist them; only the colony troops and the Shu princely guard remained in the city; the people were terrified; Jiechun opened the gates to admit villagers fleeing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 中尉奉鐕勾賊抵城下，捷春與御史陳廷謨擒擊奉鐕，而募市人、起廢將固守。

translations.literal: The lieutenant prince Feng Zheng colluded with bandits who reached beneath the city wall; Jiechun, together with Censor Chen Tingmo, seized and attacked Feng Zheng, while recruiting townspeople and raising dismissed generals to hold firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Lieutenant prince Feng Zheng colluded with the rebels and brought them to the city walls; Jiechun and censor Chen Tingmo seized and attacked Feng Zheng, recruited townspeople, and reinstated dismissed generals to hold the defense.

sentences.zh: 賊去，蜀王疏其功。

translations.literal: When the bandits left, the Prince of Shu memorialized his merits.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels withdrew, the Prince of Shu memorialized his achievements.

sentences.zh: 會維章罷，傅宗龍代，命捷春監軍，偕總兵羅尚文擊賊。

translations.literal: Just then Weizhang was dismissed and Fu Zonglong replaced him; Jiechun was ordered to oversee the army and, together with Regional Commander Luo Shangwen, attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhang was dismissed and Fu Zonglong replaced him; Jiechun was ordered to supervise the army and attack the rebels with regional commander Luo Shangwen.

sentences.zh: 明年，尚文及安錦副使吳麟征大破賊過天星等。

translations.literal: The next year Shangwen and Vice Commissioner of Anzhou and Jinzhou Wu Linzheng utterly defeated the bandit Guo Tianxing and others.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shangwen and An-Jin vice commissioner Wu Linzheng inflicted a major defeat on Guo Tianxing and other rebel leaders.

sentences.zh: 捷春進右參政，仍監軍。

translations.literal: Jiechun was promoted to Right Administration Commissioner and continued to oversee the army.
translations.idiomatic: Jiechun was promoted to right administration commissioner and continued to supervise the army.

sentences.zh: 十二年五月，宗龍入掌中樞，即擢捷春右僉都御史代之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twelfth year Zonglong entered to head the central secretariat and immediately promoted Jiechun to Right Censor-in-Chief to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year twelve Zonglong took charge of the central secretariat and immediately promoted Jiechun to right censor-in-chief to replace him as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 時張獻忠、羅汝才已叛，謀入秦。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Xianzhong and Luo Rucai had already rebelled and planned to enter Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianzhong and Luo Rucai had already rebelled and planned to enter Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 秦兵扼之興安，乃犯興山及蜀太平，遂窺大寧。

translations.literal: Qin troops blocked them at Xing'an; they then attacked Xingshan and Taiping in Shu and thus eyed Daling.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi troops blocked them at Xing'an; they then attacked Xingshan and Taiping in Sichuan and turned toward Daling.

sentences.zh: 捷春遣副將王之綸、方國安分道扼之。

translations.literal: Jiechun sent Deputy Generals Wang Zhilun and Fang Guo'an to block them by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Jiechun sent deputy generals Wang Zhilun and Fang Guo'an to block them on separate routes.

sentences.zh: 國安連破賊，賊遂還入秦、楚。

translations.literal: Guo'an repeatedly defeated the bandits, and the bandits then returned into Qin and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo'an repeatedly defeated the rebels, who then withdrew into Shaanxi and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十月朔，楊嗣昌誓師襄陽，檄蜀軍受節度。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month Yang Sichang took the oath at Xiangyang and ordered the Shu army to accept his command.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the tenth month Yang Sichang rallied his forces at Xiangyang and ordered the Sichuan army to accept his command.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌以楚地廣衍，賊難制，驅使入蜀，蜀險阻，賊不得逞，蹙之可全勝，又慮蜀重兵扼險，賊將還毒楚，調蜀精銳萬餘為己用，蜀中卒自是益疲弱不足支矣。

translations.literal: Sichang, because Chu territory was broad and spreading and bandits were hard to control, drove them into Shu; Shu was precipitous and obstructed, the bandits could not show their power, and if hemmed in there could be complete victory; he also feared that with heavy Shu troops blocking the passes the bandits would return to harm Chu, so he transferred more than ten thousand elite Shu troops for his own use; from this the troops in Shu daily grew weaker and were insufficient to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang judged that Huguang was too vast for easy control and drove the rebels into Sichuan, where the rugged terrain would hem them in for a complete victory; he also feared that if Sichuan held the passes in force the rebels would turn back to ravage Huguang, so he transferred more than ten thousand elite Sichuan troops to his own command; from then on Sichuan's forces grew steadily weaker and could no longer hold their own.

sentences.zh: 捷春憤曰：「令甲失一城，巡撫坐。

translations.literal: Jiechun said angrily: "By ordinance, if one city is lost, the grand coordinator is liable.
translations.idiomatic: Jiechun said angrily: "By regulation, losing a single city makes the grand coordinator liable.

sentences.zh: 今以蜀委賊，是督師殺我也。」

translations.literal: Now to hand Shu over to the bandits is for the supreme commander to kill me."
translations.idiomatic: Now you are handing Sichuan over to the rebels—that is the supreme commander killing me."

sentences.zh: 爭之，不能得。

translations.literal: He disputed it but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: He protested but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 於是汝才、惠登相遂自興山、遠安犯大寧、大昌，獻忠亦西至太平。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rucai and Hui Dengxiang advanced from Xingshan and Yuan'an to attack Daling and Dachang, and Xianzhong also went west to Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Rucai and Hui Dengxiang advanced from Xingshan and Yuan'an against Daling and Dachang, and Xianzhong also marched west to Taiping.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，左良玉大破獻忠瑪瑙山，他將張應元、張令等復數敗之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year Zuo Liangyu utterly defeated Xianzhong at Mount Mano; other generals Zhang Yingyuan, Zhang Ling, and others again repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year Zuo Liangyu routed Xianzhong at Mount Mano; other generals Zhang Yingyuan and Zhang Ling repeatedly defeated him as well.

sentences.zh: 獻忠乃逃興、歸山中。

translations.literal: Xianzhong then fled into the mountains of Xing and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong fled into the mountains of Xingzhou and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之復振，由汝才入寧昌故道走而西。

translations.literal: After a long while he revived; by way of Rucai entering the old road through Ningchang he went west.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he recovered his strength and, following Rucai along the old Ningchang route, fled west.

sentences.zh: 初，汝才在寧昌阻江，為諸將劉貴、秦良玉、秦翼明、楊茂選等所拒，不得渡。

translations.literal: Initially Rucai at Ningchang was blocked by the river and was resisted by the various generals Liu Gui, Qin Liangyu, Qin Yiming, Yang Maoxuan, and others, and could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Rucai had been blocked at Ningchang by the river; generals Liu Gui, Qin Liangyu, Qin Yiming, Yang Maoxuan, and others held him off and he could not cross.

sentences.zh: 會獻忠西，遂與合。

translations.literal: When Xianzhong went west, they then joined forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhong marched west they joined forces.

sentences.zh: 貴等戰皆卻，賊乃渡江，營萬頃山、苦桃灣，其別部營紅茨崖、青平砦，歸、巫間大震。

translations.literal: Gui and the others were all driven back in battle; the bandits then crossed the river and encamped at Mount Wanqing and Kutao Bay; their separate division encamped at Hongci Cliff and Qingping Stockade; great alarm spread between Gui and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui and the others were driven back in every engagement; the rebels crossed the river and encamped at Mount Wanqing and Kutao Bay, while a detached force encamped at Hongci Cliff and Qingping Stockade; the region between Guizhou and Wushan was thrown into uproar.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌乃上夷陵，而檄捷春扼夔門。

translations.literal: Sichang then went up to Yiling and ordered Jiechun to block Kui Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang then advanced to Yiling and ordered Jiechun to hold Kui Gate.

sentences.zh: 蜀大寧、大昌界楚竹溪、房縣，有三十二隘口，嗣昌欲厚集兵力專守夔，棄寧、昌啖賊，官軍環攻之。

translations.literal: Shu's Daling and Dachang bordered Chu's Zhuxi and Fangxian, with thirty-two pass openings; Sichang wished to mass heavy troops to concentrate on holding Kui, abandon Ning and Chang to feed the bandits, and have government troops encircle and attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Daling and Dachang in Sichuan bordered Zhuxi and Fangxian in Huguang, with thirty-two passes; Sichang wanted to mass troops at Kui, abandon Ningchang and Dachang as bait for the rebels, and have government forces encircle them.

sentences.zh: 捷春曰：「棄隘口不守，是延賊入戶也。」

translations.literal: Jiechun said: "To abandon the passes and not defend them is to invite the bandits into one's house."
translations.idiomatic: Jiechun said: "Abandoning the passes is inviting the rebels into one's own house."

sentences.zh: 乃遣茂選及覃思岱等出關分守。

translations.literal: He then sent Maoxuan and Tan Side and others out of the passes to guard separately.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Maoxuan, Tan Side, and others out to hold the passes separately.

sentences.zh: 二將不相得，思岱鐕殺茂選，捷春令兼統其眾，其眾相率去。

translations.literal: The two generals were incompatible; Side killed Maoxuan by treachery; Jiechun ordered him to take joint command of their troops, and the troops left in groups.
translations.idiomatic: The two generals quarreled; Side treacherously killed Maoxuan; Jiechun had Side take over both commands, and the troops deserted en masse.

sentences.zh: 賊入隘，守者潰，賊夜斬夔關，將士大驚潰，新寧、大竹皆陷。

translations.literal: The bandits entered the pass; the defenders collapsed; by night the bandits cut down Kui Pass; officers and soldiers fled in great alarm; Xinning and Dazhu both fell.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels entered the pass; the defenders broke; that night they stormed Kui Pass; officers and soldiers fled in panic; Xinning and Dazhu both fell.

sentences.zh: 而汝才、登相越巴霧河，陷開縣，為鄭嘉棟、賀人龍所破。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Rucai and Dengxiang crossed the Bayu River, took Kaixian, and were defeated by Zheng Jiadong and He Renlong.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai and Dengxiang crossed the Bayu River and took Kaixian but were defeated by Zheng Jiadong and He Renlong.

sentences.zh: 汝才乃與小秦王、混世王東奔，而登相獨過開縣西。

translations.literal: Rucai then fled east with Little Qin King and World-Mixing King, while Dengxiang alone passed west of Kaixian.
translations.idiomatic: Rucai fled east with Little Qin King and World-Mixing King, while Dengxiang alone marched west of Kaixian.

sentences.zh: 人龍及李國奇又西追之，汝才等遁還興山，屢挫。

translations.literal: Renlong and Li Guoqi again pursued west; Rucai and the others fled back to Xingshan and suffered repeated setbacks.
translations.idiomatic: Renlong and Li Guoqi pursued west; Rucai and his followers fled back to Xingshan and suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 會嗣昌下招降令，小秦王、混世王皆降，惟汝才逸去。

translations.literal: When Sichang issued an order to summon surrender, Little Qin King and World-Mixing King both surrendered; only Rucai escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichang issued surrender summonses, Little Qin King and World-Mixing King submitted; only Rucai escaped.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌見楚地無賊，以八月終率師入蜀，於是群賊盡萃蜀中。

translations.literal: Sichang, seeing no bandits in Chu territory, at the end of the eighth month led his army into Shu, and thus all the bandit groups gathered in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Huguang free of rebels, Sichang at the end of the eighth month led his army into Sichuan, and all the rebel bands gathered there.

sentences.zh: 當是時，捷春提弱卒二萬守重慶，所倚惟秦良玉、張令軍。

translations.literal: At this time Jiechun led twenty thousand weak troops to hold Chongqing; he relied only on the armies of Qin Liangyu and Zhang Ling.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Jiechun held Chongqing with twenty thousand weak troops, relying only on the forces of Qin Liangyu and Zhang Ling.

sentences.zh: 無何，秦師噪而西歸，楚將張應元等敗績於夔州之土地嶺。

translations.literal: Before long the Qin troops clamored and went west homeward; the Chu generals Zhang Yingyuan and others were defeated at Tudi Ridge in Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shaanxi troops clamored and marched west homeward; Huguang generals Zhang Yingyuan and others were defeated at Tudi Ridge in Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 於是捷春以大昌上、中、下馬渡水淺地平，難與持久，乃扼水寨觀音巖為第一隘，以部將邵仲光守之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiechun, because at Dachang the upper, middle, and lower horse crossings the water was shallow and the ground level and hard to hold for long, then blocked the water stockade Guanyin Cliff as the first pass and had his subordinate general Shao Zhongguang defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiechun judged that at Dachang the upper, middle, and lower horse crossings were shallow and level and could not be held long; he made Guanyin Cliff on the water stockade the primary pass and stationed his subordinate Shao Zhongguang there.

sentences.zh: 而夜叉巖、三黃嶺、磨子巖、魚河洞、下湧諸處，各分兵三四百人以守。

translations.literal: Meanwhile at Yecha Cliff, Sanhuang Ridge, Mozi Cliff, Yuhe Cave, Xiayong, and other places he assigned three or four hundred men each to defend.
translations.idiomatic: At Yecha Cliff, Sanhuang Ridge, Mozi Cliff, Yuhe Cave, Xiayong, and other points he posted three or four hundred men each.

sentences.zh: 萬元吉以兵分力弱為憂，捷春不聽。

translations.literal: Wan Yuanji worried that dividing the troops made the forces weak; Jiechun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Yuanji warned that splitting the forces left them too weak; Jiechun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 九月，獻忠突敗仲光軍，破上馬渡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Xianzhong suddenly defeated Zhongguang's army and broke the upper horse crossing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Xianzhong routed Zhongguang's army and broke through the upper horse crossing.

sentences.zh: 元吉急檄諸將分邀之，復令張奏凱屯凈壁，捷春遣二將羅洪政、沈應龍為助。

translations.literal: Yuanji urgently ordered the various generals to intercept by separate routes and again ordered Zhang Zoukai to encamp at Jingbi; Jiechun sent two generals, Luo Hongzheng and Shen Yinglong, to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji urgently ordered the generals to intercept on multiple fronts and stationed Zhang Zoukai at Jingbi; Jiechun sent Luo Hongzheng and Shen Yinglong to assist.

sentences.zh: 十月，獻忠突凈壁，遂陷大昌，屯開縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Xianzhong suddenly attacked Jingbi, then took Dachang and encamped at Kaixian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Xianzhong stormed Jingbi, took Dachang, and encamped at Kaixian.

sentences.zh: 良玉、令兩軍皆覆。

translations.literal: The two armies of Liangyu and Ling were both destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyu's and Ling's armies were both destroyed.

sentences.zh: 賊行則哨探，止則息馬抄糧。

translations.literal: When the bandits marched they sent scouts ahead; when they halted they rested the horses and foraged grain.
translations.idiomatic: When marching the rebels sent scouts ahead; when they halted they rested their horses and foraged for grain.

sentences.zh: 關隘偵候不明，防軍或遠離戍所，賊乘隙而過無人之境。

translations.literal: At the passes scouting was unclear; defensive troops sometimes were far from their garrison posts; the bandits seized gaps to pass through no man's land.
translations.idiomatic: Pass scouts were unreliable; garrison troops sometimes strayed far from their posts; the rebels slipped through unguarded gaps.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌遂收斬仲光，上疏劾捷春失事。

translations.literal: Sichang then arrested and executed Zhongguang and memorialized to impeach Jiechun for losing the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Sichang had Zhongguang arrested and executed and memorialized impeaching Jiechun for the disaster.

sentences.zh: 捷春收兵扼梁山。

translations.literal: Jiechun gathered troops to block Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiechun regrouped his troops to hold Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 時登相已歸正，而汝才復與獻忠合，以梁山河深不能渡，乃自開縣西走達州。

translations.literal: At the time Dengxiang had already submitted; Rucai again joined Xianzhong; because the Liangshan River was deep and could not be crossed, they went from west of Kaixian to flee toward Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dengxiang had already submitted, but Rucai rejoined Xianzhong; unable to cross the deep Liangshan River, they marched west from Kaixian toward Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 捷春退保綿州，扼涪江。

translations.literal: Jiechun withdrew to defend Mianzhou and blocked the Fu River.
translations.idiomatic: Jiechun withdrew to Mianzhou and blocked the Fu River.

sentences.zh: 賊疾走，陷劍州，遂趨廣元，將由間道入漢中，為秦兵所扼，乃復走巴西。

translations.literal: The bandits marched rapidly, took Jianzhou, then pressed toward Guangyuan, intending to enter Hanzhong by a bypath; blocked by Qin troops, they again fled toward Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels marched rapidly, took Jianzhou, and pressed toward Guangyuan, intending to enter Hanzhong by a side route; blocked by Shaanxi troops, they turned back toward Baxi.

sentences.zh: 應元諸軍邀之梓潼，戰小利，既而衄，蜀將曹誌耀等力戰卻之。

translations.literal: Yingyuan's army and others intercepted them at Zitong; they had a small advantage in battle, then were repulsed; the Shu general Cao Zhiyao and others fought fiercely and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyuan's forces intercepted them at Zitong and gained a slight advantage, then were beaten back; Sichuan general Cao Zhiyao and others fought fiercely and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 降將張一川、張載福陷陣死，涪江師遂潰，賊屠綿州。

translations.literal: The surrendered generals Zhang Yichuan and Zhang Zaifu died in the battle line; the Fu River army then collapsed; the bandits slaughtered Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered generals Zhang Yichuan and Zhang Zaifu died in battle; the Fu River army collapsed and the rebels slaughtered Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 捷春歸成都，賊逼成都。

translations.literal: Jiechun returned to Chengdu; the bandits pressed Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiechun returned to Chengdu as the rebels closed on the city.

sentences.zh: 十一月，逮捷春使者至，遂以軍事付代者廖大亨而去。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the messenger arresting Jiechun arrived; he then handed military affairs to his replacement Liao Daheng and left.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the messenger sent to arrest Jiechun arrived; he handed military affairs to his successor Liao Daheng and departed.

sentences.zh: 捷春為人清謹，治蜀有惠政。

translations.literal: Jiechun as a man was pure and careful; in governing Shu he had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Jiechun was upright and prudent; his rule in Sichuan brought real benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 士民哭送者載道，舟不得行，競逐散官旗。

translations.literal: Scholars and common people who wept to send him off filled the road; boats could not advance; they competed to chase and scatter the officials' banners.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners who came weeping to see him off filled the roads; boats could not move; crowds vied to seize and tear the officials' banners.

sentences.zh: 蜀王為疏救，不聽。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu memorialized to save him; the court did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu memorialized in his defense; the court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 敕巡按御史遣官送京師，下獄論死。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the touring censor to send officials escorting him to the capital; he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the touring censor to escort him to the capital; he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 捷春知不可脫，明年八月仰藥死獄中。

translations.literal: Jiechun knew he could not escape; in the eighth month of the next year he drank poison and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not escape, in the eighth month of the following year he took poison and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 福王時，復官，贈兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu his office was restored; he was posthumously given Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu his office was restored and he was posthumously made right vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 余應桂，字二磯，都昌人。

translations.literal: Yu Yinggui, courtesy name Erji, a native of Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yinggui, courtesy name Erji, was from Duchang.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四十七年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the forty-seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Wanli year forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 歷知武康、龍巖、海澄三縣。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Wukang, Longyan, and Haicheng counties.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Wukang, Longyan, and Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，征授御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was summoned and appointed Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year four he was summoned and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 劾戶部尚書畢自嚴朋比，殿試讀卷，取陳於泰第一。

translations.literal: He impeached Minister of Revenue Bi Ziyan for factional collusion; at the palace examination reading of papers he placed Chen Yutai first.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached minister of revenue Bi Ziyan for factional collusion; as a palace examination reader he ranked Chen Yutai first.

sentences.zh: 於泰者，首輔周延儒姻也。

translations.literal: Yutai was a relation by marriage of Chief Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Yutai was related by marriage to chief grand secretary Zhou Yanru.

sentences.zh: 劾延儒納孫元化參、貂，受楊鶴重賂。

translations.literal: He impeached Yanru for accepting from Sun Yuanhua a sable and a marten, and for taking heavy bribes from Yang He.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Yanru for accepting sable and marten furs from Sun Yuanhua and heavy bribes from Yang He.

sentences.zh: 帝方眷延儒，責應桂。

translations.literal: The emperor was then favoring Yanru and reproached Yinggui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was favoring Yanru and rebuked Yinggui.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊陷登州，元化被執，應桂再疏劾延儒。

translations.literal: Before long bandits took Dengzhou; Yuanhua was captured; Yinggui again memorialized to impeach Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Before long rebels took Dengzhou and Yuanhua was captured; Yinggui memorialized again to impeach Yanru.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，貶三秩視事，應桂引疾歸。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, demoted him three ranks and ordered him to remain at his post; Yinggui pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, demoted him three ranks but ordered him to remain in office; Yinggui pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 七年還朝，出按湖廣，居守承天。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he returned to court, went out to investigate Huguang, and remained to guard Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he returned to court, was sent to investigate Huguang, and stayed to guard Chengde.

sentences.zh: 捐贖鍰十餘萬募壯士，繕城治器，賊不敢逼獻陵。

translations.literal: He donated more than one hundred thousand taels of ransom money to recruit braves, repaired the walls and prepared weapons; the bandits did not dare press the Xian tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He donated more than one hundred thousand taels of fine money to recruit fighters, repaired the walls and prepared arms; the rebels did not dare threaten the Xian imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and praised him.

sentences.zh: 期滿，命再巡一年。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was ordered to investigate for one more year.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was ordered to serve another year.

sentences.zh: 貽贖鍰萬五千助盧象昇軍需，而奏報屬城失事，具以實聞。

translations.literal: He sent fifteen thousand taels of ransom money to assist Lu Xiangsheng's military supplies, and in memorials reporting failures in subordinate cities he stated everything truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: He sent fifteen thousand taels of fine money to assist Lu Xiangsheng's army and reported subordinate cities' failures truthfully in his memorials.

sentences.zh: 帝以是知巡撫王夢尹詐，而益信應桂。

translations.literal: By this the emperor knew Grand Coordinator Wang Mengyin was deceitful and trusted Yinggui all the more.
translations.idiomatic: From this the emperor learned that grand coordinator Wang Mengyin was deceptive and trusted Yinggui all the more.

sentences.zh: 期滿，命再巡一年。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was ordered to investigate for one more year.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was ordered to serve another year.

sentences.zh: 十年，即擢應桂右僉都御史，代夢尹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was immediately promoted Yinggui to Right Censor-in-Chief to replace Mengyin.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten Yinggui was immediately promoted to right censor-in-chief to replace Mengyin.

sentences.zh: 當是時，諸監司袁繼咸、包鳳起、高鬥樞輩已削平湖南群賊，而江北賊勢日熾，諸將雖奏捷，不能大創也。

translations.literal: At this time the various surveillance commissioners Yuan Jixian, Bao Fengqi, Gao Doushu, and others had already pacified the bandit groups of Hunan, while north of the river the bandit situation grew daily fiercer; although the generals reported victories they could not inflict major defeats.
translations.idiomatic: By then surveillance commissioners Yuan Jixian, Bao Fengqi, Gao Doushu, and others had already pacified Hunan's rebel bands, but rebel strength north of the river grew daily fiercer and the generals' reported victories could not inflict decisive defeats.

sentences.zh: 帝命熊文燦為總理，文燦主撫。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Xiong Wencan as supreme coordinator; Wencan advocated pacification.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Xiong Wencan supreme coordinator; Wencan favored pacification.

sentences.zh: 明年，降其渠劉國能、張獻忠。

translations.literal: The next year he secured the surrender of their chiefs Liu Guoneng and Zhang Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he secured the surrender of chiefs Liu Guoneng and Zhang Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 馬進忠西走潼關，馬光玉、賀一龍、李萬慶、順義王、九條龍眾十餘萬萃麻城、黃安。

translations.literal: Ma Jinzhong fled west toward Tongguan; Ma Guangyu, He Yilong, Li Wanqing, Shunyi King, Nine-Striped Dragon, and others—more than one hundred thousand—gathered at Macheng and Huang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jinzhong fled west toward Tongguan; Ma Guangyu, He Yilong, Li Wanqing, Shunyi King, Nine-Striped Dragon, and others—more than one hundred thousand strong—gathered at Macheng and Huang'an.

sentences.zh: 應桂諭降光玉、一龍，未至，而遣將擊順天王等於黃福店，賊遂走黃安。

translations.literal: Yinggui urged Guangyu and Yilong to surrender; before they arrived he sent generals to attack Shun Heavenly King and others at Huangfudian; the bandits then fled to Huang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yinggui urged Guangyu and Yilong to surrender; before they arrived he sent generals to attack Shun Heavenly King and others at Huangfudian, and the rebels fled toward Huang'an.

sentences.zh: 會文燦至麻城，應桂請協擊，不從。

translations.literal: When Wencan reached Macheng, Yinggui asked to attack jointly; he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: When Wencan reached Macheng, Yinggui asked to strike jointly; Wencan refused.

sentences.zh: 賊復東走江北，為左良玉所遏，折而走廣濟、蘄水。

translations.literal: The bandits again fled east to the north of the river, were blocked by Zuo Liangyu, turned, and went toward Guangji and Qishui.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled east across the river, were blocked by Zuo Liangyu, turned, and marched toward Guangji and Qishui.

sentences.zh: 文燦檄諸道兵合擊賊於茶山，賊逸於應桂所分地，文燦遂劾其後期誤軍。

translations.literal: Wencan ordered troops of all circuits to combine and attack the bandits at Mount Cha; the bandits slipped through the area Yinggui had been assigned; Wencan then impeached him for arriving late and harming the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan ordered combined attacks at Mount Cha; the rebels escaped through Yinggui's sector; Wencan then impeached him for arriving late and bungling the campaign.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書楊嗣昌以應桂曾劾其父鶴也，奏逮之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Yang Sichang, because Yinggui had once impeached his father He, memorialized to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of war Yang Sichang, because Yinggui had once impeached his father Yang He, memorialized for his arrest.

sentences.zh: 應桂乃陳撫剿始末，白己無罪，而詆文燦，言：

translations.literal: Yinggui then set forth the beginning and end of pacification and suppression, declared himself innocent, and slandered Wencan, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yinggui then laid out the whole pacification-and-suppression affair, declared his innocence, and denounced Wencan, saying:

sentences.zh: 正月初，議撫劉國能，其黨李萬慶等諸大賊盡走泌陽、棗陽。

translations.literal: At the start of the first month they deliberated on pacifying Liu Guoneng; his fellows Li Wanqing and other great bandits all fled to Biyang and Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: "At the start of the first month they deliberated pacifying Liu Guoneng; his associates Li Wanqing and other major rebel leaders all fled toward Biyang and Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 時文燦、良玉並在德安。

translations.literal: At the time Wencan and Liangyu were both at De'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan and Liangyu were then both at De'an.

sentences.zh: 臣以為兵勢方盛，宜乘此追剿，而文燦調良玉諸軍盡赴信陽剿馬進忠。

translations.literal: Your servant thought the military momentum was at its height and it was fitting to pursue and suppress while taking advantage of this, but Wencan shifted all of Liangyu's armies to Xinyang to suppress Ma Jinzhong.
translations.idiomatic: I thought our forces were at their strongest and we should pursue them, but Wencan diverted all of Liangyu's armies to Xinyang against Ma Jinzhong.

sentences.zh: 臣謂進忠小寇，勝之不武，文燦不聽。

translations.literal: Your servant said Jinzhong was a small bandit and defeating him would not be martial valor; Wencan did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: I said Jinzhong was a minor rebel and defeating him would be no great feat; Wencan would not listen."

sentences.zh: 自此機一失，賊走西，而文燦東，致張獻忠攻陷谷城以要撫，李萬慶五部收余燼，勢復振。

translations.literal: From this one opportunity lost, the bandits went west while Wencan went east, causing Zhang Xianzhong to seize Gucheng to demand pacification and Li Wanqing's five divisions to gather the remaining embers—their momentum revived.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment the chance was lost: the rebels went west while Wencan went east, so Zhang Xianzhong took Gucheng to force a pacification deal and Li Wanqing's five bands rallied the survivors—their strength revived.

sentences.zh: 而豫、楚之患，遂自文燦之愎諫貽之矣。

translations.literal: Thus the calamities of Henan and Huguang were bequeathed by Wencan's obstinate counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The troubles of Henan and Huguang were thus bequeathed by Wencan's stubborn advice.

sentences.zh: 迨賊西潰之後，遮飾上聞，妄報斬級。

translations.literal: After the bandits broke westward, he blocked and glossed over reports to the throne and falsely reported heads cut.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels fled west, he concealed the truth from the throne and falsely reported enemy kills.

sentences.zh: 其自恃所長惟火炮火攻，經過州縣用夫至八百，死亡載道，未見其一試也。

translations.literal: What he relied on as his special skill was solely artillery and fire attack; in each prefecture and county he passed he requisitioned corvée laborers up to eight hundred, corpses filled the roads, yet not one trial of it was seen.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted only cannon and fire attacks; every prefecture and county he passed was forced to supply up to eight hundred laborers, the dead lined the roads, and not once was this weaponry used.

sentences.zh: 且文燦辦賊之策曰「先撫後剿」。

translations.literal: Moreover Wencan's policy for handling bandits was called "pacify first, suppress afterward."
translations.idiomatic: Wencan's bandit policy was "pacify first, suppress later."

sentences.zh: 乃茶山不效，麻城又不效，第見招撫之旗絡繹於道。

translations.literal: Yet at Chashan it did not work, at Macheng it did not work again; one saw only pacification banners streaming along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification failed at Chashan and failed again at Macheng; all one saw were pacification banners crowding the highways.

sentences.zh: 一遣使招賀一龍，而使者被殺；

translations.literal: Once he sent an envoy to recruit He Yilong, and the envoy was killed;
translations.idiomatic: Once he sent an envoy to win over He Yilong, and the envoy was killed;

sentences.zh: 一遣使招李萬慶，而饋鹽椒運魚肉與通市，賊反因之焚掠，未見一賊歸順也。

translations.literal: Once he sent an envoy to recruit Li Wanqing, but presented salt, pepper, fish and meat and opened trade with them; the bandits instead used this to burn and plunder—not one bandit was seen to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Once he sent an envoy to win over Li Wanqing, but sent salt, pepper, fish and meat and opened trade; the rebels used it to raid and burn—not a single rebel submitted.

sentences.zh: 天下有如是撫法乎！

translations.literal: Under Heaven is there such a method of pacification!
translations.idiomatic: Is this pacification under Heaven!

sentences.zh: 其一切軍需，悉取於所歷之有司，名曰「借辦」，致城市空虛，孑遺盡絕。

translations.literal: All his military supplies he took entirely from the local officials in places he passed, calling it "borrowed provisions," so that cities became empty and not a survivor was left.
translations.idiomatic: All military supplies were seized from every local official he passed, under the name "borrowed provisioning," until cities were hollowed out and scarcely a soul remained.

sentences.zh: 三月至麻城，民不堪淫掠，欲焚其署，始踉蹌而走。

translations.literal: In the third month he reached Macheng; the people could not bear the rapine and wanted to burn his yamen; only then did he stagger away.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he reached Macheng; the people, unable to endure the looting, tried to burn his office, and only then did he flee in disarray.

sentences.zh: 麻城，文燦婿家也，戚裏如是，余可知矣。

translations.literal: Macheng was Wencan's son-in-law's home—if kinfolk were treated thus, the rest may be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: Macheng was where Wencan's son-in-law lived—if his in-laws were treated thus, the rest can be imagined.

sentences.zh: 三月在蘄水，其兵殺鄉民報捷，民家環哭，竟不敢治一兵。

translations.literal: In the third month at Qishui his troops killed village folk to report victory; households wailed all around, yet in the end he dared not punish a single soldier.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month at Qishui his soldiers killed villagers to claim victory; families wailed on every side, yet he dared not discipline a single man.

sentences.zh: 蘄水，文燦家園也，鄉里如是，余可知矣。

translations.literal: Qishui was Wencan's own homeland—if his native district was thus, the rest may be imagined.
translations.idiomatic: Qishui was Wencan's home country—if his own countryside was treated thus, the rest can be imagined.

sentences.zh: 是以捷報日張，寇勢愈熾。

translations.literal: Hence victory reports daily multiplied, while the rebels' power grew ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Thus victory bulletins multiplied daily while rebel strength grew ever fiercer.

sentences.zh: 十三家之賊蹂躪南陽、汝寧，如履無人之境。

translations.literal: The bandits of the Thirteen Families trampled Nanyang and Runing as if treading an empty land.
translations.idiomatic: The Thirteen Families' rebels ravaged Nanyang and Runing as if no one were there.

sentences.zh: 文燦駐宛、汝已久，調度不聞，天下有如是剿法乎！

translations.literal: Wencan had long been stationed at Wan and Ru, yet not a word of disposition was heard—under Heaven is there such a method of suppression!
translations.idiomatic: Wencan had long been posted at Wan and Ru, yet no word of command was heard—is this suppression under Heaven!

sentences.zh: 獻忠在谷城招納亡命，買馬置器，人人知其叵測。

translations.literal: Xianzhong at Gucheng recruited runaways, bought horses and laid up weapons; every man knew his designs were unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: At Gucheng Xianzhong recruited fugitives, bought horses and stockpiled arms; everyone knew his intentions were treacherous.

sentences.zh: 文燦顧欲借之為前茅，遣官調之，非惟不應，復留解餉之官，求總兵湖廣。

translations.literal: Wencan nevertheless wished to use him as a vanguard, sent an official to mobilize him; not only did he not comply, he detained the official bringing pay supplies and demanded to be regional commander of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan still meant to use him as a vanguard and sent an officer to summon him; he not only refused but detained the pay officer and demanded the regional command of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 今已造浮橋跨漢水矣。

translations.literal: Now they have already built a pontoon bridge across the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: They have already built a floating bridge across the Han River.

sentences.zh: 文燦前既誇張而敘功，後復掩匿而不報，可不謂之欺君乎！

translations.literal: Wencan had first exaggerated in narrating merit, then again concealed and did not report—can this not be called deceiving the ruler!
translations.idiomatic: Wencan first inflated his achievements, then hid defeats from report—is this not deceiving the throne!

sentences.zh: 以總理之大柄畀之顛蹶之耄夫，臣不知其可也。

translations.literal: To give the great seal of the grand coordinator to a tottering old man in his dotage—your servant does not see how this can be approved.
translations.idiomatic: To entrust the grand coordinator's great authority to a stumbling old man—I do not see how that can be right.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 逮至，下獄。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Wencan arrived, he was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 初，應桂貽書文燦，言獻忠必反，可先未發圖之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yinggui had sent a letter to Wencan saying Xianzhong would surely rebel and they could plot against him before he acted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yinggui had written Wencan that Xianzhong would surely rebel and they should strike before he rose.

sentences.zh: 其書為獻忠邏者所得，獻忠騰牒鄖陽巡撫戴東旻，言「撫軍欲殺我」，東旻聞之文燦，文燦再糾應桂。

translations.literal: The letter was obtained by Xianzhong's scouts; Xianzhong sent up a placard to Yunyang grand coordinator Dai Dongmin saying "The pacification commissioner wishes to kill me"; Dongmin reported it to Wencan, and Wencan again impeached Yinggui.
translations.idiomatic: The letter was seized by Xianzhong's scouts; Xianzhong posted a notice to Yunyang grand coordinator Dai Dongmin: "The pacification commissioner means to kill me." Dongmin informed Wencan, and Wencan impeached Yinggui again.

sentences.zh: 應桂再疏辨，帝亦不納。

translations.literal: Yinggui memorialized again in self-defense; the emperor also did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Yinggui memorialized again in defense; the emperor again refused.

sentences.zh: 應桂竟遣戍。

translations.literal: Yinggui was finally banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Yinggui was finally banished to military exile.

sentences.zh: 無何，獻忠果反，廷臣交章薦應桂。

translations.literal: Before long Xianzhong did rebel; court officials one after another memorialized recommending Yinggui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xianzhong did rebel, and court officials memorialized one after another to recommend Yinggui.

sentences.zh: 十六年，起應桂兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Yinggui was recalled as vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Yinggui was recalled as vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 十月，潼關陷，帝召問大臣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Tong Pass fell; the emperor summoned the great ministers for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Tong Pass fell; the emperor summoned the senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 陳演言：「賊入關中，必戀子女玉帛，猶虎入陷阱。」

translations.literal: Chen Yan said: "When the bandits enter the passes they are sure to cling to women, children, jade and silk—like a tiger entering a trap."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan said: "Once the rebels enter the passes they will cling to women, children, jade and silk—like a tiger in a trap."

sentences.zh: 應桂叱之曰：「壯士健馬咸出關西。

translations.literal: Yinggui rebuked him, saying: "Stalwart warriors and fine horses all come from west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Yinggui rebuked him: "Brave men and strong horses all come from west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 賊得之，必長驅橫行，大臣安得面謾！」

translations.literal: If the bandits obtain them they are sure to drive far and rampage unchecked—how can great ministers face us and deceive!"
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels get them they will drive straight ahead unchecked—how can senior ministers lie to our faces!"

sentences.zh: 演股栗失色。

translations.literal: Yan's legs trembled and he turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's legs shook and he turned pale.

sentences.zh: 十一月，督師孫傳庭戰歿，命應桂兼右僉都御史往代之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month grand coordinator Sun Chuanting died in battle; Yinggui was ordered to serve additionally as right vice censor-in-chief and go to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month grand coordinator Sun Chuanting fell in battle; Yinggui was ordered to take the additional post of right vice censor-in-chief and replace him.

sentences.zh: 應桂以無兵無餉，入見帝而泣。

translations.literal: Yinggui, having no troops and no rations, entered to see the emperor and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Yinggui had no troops and no supplies; he went in to see the emperor and wept.

sentences.zh: 帝但遣京軍千人護行，給御用銀萬兩、銀花四百、銀牌二百、蟒幣二百、雜幣倍之，為軍前賞功之用而已。

translations.literal: The emperor only sent a thousand capital troops to escort him on his way, and gave imperial silver ten thousand taels, four hundred silver flowers, two hundred silver plates, two hundred python robes, and double that in miscellaneous silks—nothing but funds for rewarding merit at the front.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor only sent a thousand capital troops as escort and gave ten thousand taels of imperial silver, four hundred silver flowers, two hundred silver plaques, two hundred python robes, and twice as much in assorted silks—only bounty for rewarding merit at the front.

sentences.zh: 應桂既受命，日夜悲疑，將至山西，則偽官充斥，逡巡不得前。

translations.literal: Once Yinggui had accepted the commission he grieved and wavered day and night; when he was about to reach Shanxi, false officials thronged everywhere and he hesitated, unable to advance.
translations.idiomatic: After accepting the post Yinggui grieved and hesitated day and night; nearing Shanxi he found rebel officials everywhere and hung back, unable to advance.

sentences.zh: 帝責以逗遛，奪職，命新擢陜西巡撫李化熙代之，化熙亦不能進也。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for delay and stripped his post, ordering the newly promoted Shaanxi grand coordinator Li Huaxi to replace him; Huaxi also could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for dallying, removed him from office, and ordered the newly appointed Shaanxi grand coordinator Li Huaxi to replace him; Huaxi could not advance either.

sentences.zh: 未幾，京師陷。

translations.literal: Before long the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 應桂家居不出。

translations.literal: Yinggui remained at home and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Yinggui stayed home and did not go out.

sentences.zh: 久之，死於難。

translations.literal: After a long while he died in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he died in the upheaval.

sentences.zh: 高鬥樞，字象先，鄞人。

translations.literal: Gao Doushu, style name Xiangxian, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Doushu, courtesy name Xiangxian, was from Yin county.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年進士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 坐議巡撫耿如杞獄，與同列四人下詔獄。

translations.literal: For deliberating in the case of grand coordinator Geng Ruzhi, he and four colleagues of the same rank were cast into the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in deliberating the case of grand coordinator Geng Ruzhi, he and four colleagues were sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 尋復官，進員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon his office was restored and he was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored to office and promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷荊州知府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢長沙兵備副使。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to vice commissioner for military preparations at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was promoted to vice commissioner for military preparations at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 楚郡之在湖北者，盡罹賊禍，勢且及湖南，臨、藍、湖、湘間土寇蜂起。

translations.literal: Of the prefectures of Chu in Hubei, all had suffered bandit disaster; the momentum was about to reach Hunan, and local bandits rose in swarms between Lin, Lan, Hu and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Every Chu prefecture in Hubei had suffered rebel raids; the tide was about to reach Hunan, and local bandits swarmed through Lin, Lan, Hu, and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 長沙止老弱衛卒五百，又遣二百戍攸縣，城庫雉堞盡圮。

translations.literal: Changsha had only five hundred aged and weak guard soldiers, and had also sent two hundred to garrison You county; the city walls, arsenals and battlements were all in ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha had only five hundred old and weak garrison troops and had sent two hundred more to guard You county; walls, arsenals, and parapets were all ruined.

sentences.zh: 鬥樞至，建飛樓四十，大修守具。

translations.literal: When Doushu arrived he built forty flying towers and greatly repaired defensive equipment.
translations.idiomatic: When Doushu arrived he built forty watchtowers and greatly strengthened the defenses.

sentences.zh: 臨、藍賊艘二百餘，由衡、湘抵城下，相拒十餘日乃卻去，轉攻袁州。

translations.literal: Over two hundred bandit boats from Lin and Lan came by Heng and Xiang to the foot of the city; after resisting more than ten days they withdrew and turned to attack Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred rebel boats from Lin and Lan came down the Heng and Xiang to the city; after ten-odd days of resistance they withdrew and turned on Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣都司陳上才躡其後，賊亦解去。

translations.literal: He sent colonel Chen Shangcai to trail them, and the bandits also dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent colonel Chen Shangcai in pursuit, and the rebels dispersed as well.

sentences.zh: 尋擊殺亂賊劉高峰等，撫定余眾。

translations.literal: Soon he attacked and killed the disorderly bandits Liu Gaofeng and others, and pacified the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he killed the rebel chieftain Liu Gaofeng and others and pacified the remainder.

sentences.zh: 詔錄其功。

translations.literal: An edict recorded his merit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recorded his achievements.

sentences.zh: 巡撫陳睿謨大征臨、藍寇，鬥樞當南面，大小十餘戰，賊盡平。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Chen Ruimo launched a great campaign against the Lin-Lan bandits; Doushu held the southern face; in more than ten battles large and small the bandits were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Chen Ruimo mounted a major campaign against the Lin-Lan rebels; Doushu held the southern front; in more than ten engagements the rebels were wholly subdued.

sentences.zh: 詔賚銀幣。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rewarded him with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月進按察使，移守鄖陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year he was promoted to surveillance commissioner and transferred to defend Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year he was promoted to surveillance commissioner and moved to defend Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 鄖被寇且十載，屬邑有六，居民不四千，數百里荊榛。

translations.literal: Yunyang had suffered bandits for nearly ten years; of its six subordinate districts the residents numbered fewer than four thousand, and for hundreds of li it was thorns and brambles.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyang had been ravaged by rebels for nearly ten years; of six subordinate districts fewer than four thousand people remained, and for hundreds of li there was only wilderness.

sentences.zh: 撫治王永祚以襄陽急，移師鎮之。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Wang Yongzuo, because Xiangyang was urgent, shifted his army to garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Wang Yongzuo, finding Xiangyang critical, moved his troops to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 鬥樞至甫六日，張獻忠自陜引而東。

translations.literal: Doushu had been there only six days when Zhang Xianzhong led his forces east from Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Doushu had been there only six days when Zhang Xianzhong marched east from Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 鬥樞與知府徐啟元遣遊擊王光恩及弟光興分扼之，戰頻捷，賊不敢犯。

translations.literal: Doushu and prefect Xu Qiyuan sent guerrilla officer Wang Guang'en and his brother Guangxing to hold him off in separate positions; they fought often with success and the bandits dared not attack.
translations.idiomatic: Doushu and prefect Xu Qiyuan sent guerrilla officer Wang Guang'en and his brother Guangxing to block him in separate posts; they won repeated skirmishes and the rebels dared not attack.

sentences.zh: 光恩者，均州降渠小秦王也。

translations.literal: Guang'en was the Little King of Qin, a surrendered bandit chieftain from Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guang'en was the Little King of Qin, a surrendered rebel leader from Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 初與張獻忠、羅汝才輩為賊，獻忠、汝才降而復叛，均州五營懼見討自疑。

translations.literal: At first he had been a bandit with Zhang Xianzhong, Luo Rucai and company; Xianzhong and Rucai surrendered then rebelled again, and Junzhou's Five Camps feared punitive action and grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been a rebel with Zhang Xianzhong, Luo Rucai, and others; when Xianzhong and Rucai surrendered and rebelled again, Junzhou's Five Camps feared punishment and grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 又以獻忠強，慮為所並，光恩斂眾據要害以拒獻忠。

translations.literal: Also because Xianzhong was strong they feared being absorbed by him; Guang'en gathered his followers and held strategic points to resist Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Xianzhong's strength and absorption, Guang'en gathered his men and held key ground against him.

sentences.zh: 居久之，乃有稍稍飏去者，光恩亦去，已而復降。

translations.literal: After a long while some gradually drifted away; Guang'en also left, then later surrendered again.
translations.idiomatic: In time some drifted away; Guang'en left too, then surrendered again.

sentences.zh: 光恩善用其下，下亦樂為之用。

translations.literal: Guang'en knew how to use his subordinates well, and they were also glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Guang'en knew how to lead his men, and they were glad to follow him.

sentences.zh: 鬥樞察其誠，招入郡守。

translations.literal: Doushu perceived his sincerity and summoned him into the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Doushu saw his good faith and brought him into the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 當是時，鬥樞、啟元善謀，光恩善戰，鄖城危而復全。

translations.literal: At that time Doushu and Qiyuan were adept at planning, Guang'en adept at fighting—and Yuncheng, though in peril, was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Then Doushu and Qiyuan planned well, Guang'en fought well, and Yuncheng, though endangered, was saved.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，李自成陷襄陽、均州，攻鄖陽四日而去。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year Li Zicheng seized Xiangyang and Junzhou and attacked Yunyang for four days before departing.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifteenth year Li Zicheng took Xiangyang and Junzhou and besieged Yunyang for four days before leaving.

sentences.zh: 明年春，復來攻，十餘日不克，乃退屯楊溪。

translations.literal: The next spring he came to attack again; for more than ten days he could not take it and withdrew to encamp at Yangxi.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he attacked again; after more than ten days he could not take the city and withdrew to camp at Yangxi.

sentences.zh: 五月，鬥樞召遊擊劉調元入城，旬日間殺賊三千餘。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Doushu summoned guerrilla officer Liu Tiaoyuan into the city; within ten days more than three thousand bandits were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Doushu called guerrilla officer Liu Tiaoyuan into the city; within ten days they killed more than three thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 自成將來攻，卒不克而去。

translations.literal: Zicheng was about to come attack but in the end could not take it and left.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng was about to attack again but in the end could not take it and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 乃令光恩復均州，調元下光化，躬率將士復谷城。

translations.literal: He then ordered Guang'en to recover Junzhou, Tiaoyuan to descend on Guanghua, and himself led officers and soldiers to recover Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Guang'en to retake Junzhou, Tiaoyuan downriver to Guanghua, and led his officers to recover Gucheng himself.

sentences.zh: 將襲襄陽，聞孫傳庭敗，旋師，均州復為賊有。

translations.literal: He was about to strike at Xiangyang when he heard Sun Chuanting had been defeated; he wheeled his army, and Junzhou was again in bandit hands.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to strike Xiangyang when news came that Sun Chuanting had been defeated; he turned back, and Junzhou fell to the rebels again.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，自成遣將路應標等以三萬人攻鄖。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year Zicheng sent generals Lu Yingbiao and others with thirty thousand men to attack Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventeenth year Zicheng sent generals Lu Yingbiao and others with thirty thousand men against Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 鬥樞遣人入均州，燒其蓄積，賊乏食而退。

translations.literal: Doushu sent men into Junzhou to burn their stored grain; the bandits lacked food and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Doushu sent men into Junzhou to burn their stores; short of food, the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 當是時，湖南、北十四郡皆陷，獨鄖在。

translations.literal: At that time fourteen prefectures of Hunan and Hubei had all fallen; only Yunyang remained.
translations.idiomatic: By then fourteen prefectures in Hunan and Hubei had fallen; only Yunyang held out.

sentences.zh: 自十五年冬撫治王永祚被逮，連命李乾德、郭景昌代之，路絕不能至，中朝謂鄖已陷，不復設撫治。

translations.literal: From the winter of the fifteenth year when pacification commissioner Wang Yongzuo was arrested, Li Qiande and Guo Jingchang were appointed in succession to replace him, but the routes were cut off and they could not reach it; the court supposed Yunyang had fallen and no longer appointed a pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: From the winter of the fifteenth year, when pacification commissioner Wang Yongzuo was arrested, Li Qiande and Guo Jingchang were appointed in turn, but routes were cut and they could not arrive; the court assumed Yunyang had fallen and stopped appointing a pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十六年夏，鬥樞上請兵疏，始知鄖存，眾議即任鬥樞。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixteenth year Doushu memorialized requesting troops; only then did they learn Yunyang still stood, and the consensus was to appoint Doushu on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixteenth year Doushu memorialized for troops; only then did the court learn Yunyang still stood, and many urged appointing Doushu there.

sentences.zh: 而陳演與之有隙，乃擢啟元右僉都御史任之，加鬥樞太僕少卿，路阻亦不能達。

translations.literal: But Chen Yan bore him a grudge, so Xu Qiyuan was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief to take the post, and Doushu was given the additional title of vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud—yet the routes were blocked and neither appointment could reach him.
translations.idiomatic: But Chen Yan bore a grudge against him, so Xu Qiyuan was made right vice censor-in-chief in his place and Doushu was given the Court of the Imperial Stud as vice director—yet roads were blocked and neither order reached him.

sentences.zh: 是年二月，朝議設漢中巡撫，兼督川北軍務，擢鬥樞右副都御史以往，朝命亦不達。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year the court deliberated establishing a Hanzhong grand coordinator to supervise also northern Sichuan military affairs; Doushu was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and sent—but the court order also did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the court decided to establish a Hanzhong grand coordinator also overseeing northern Sichuan; Doushu was promoted right vice censor-in-chief and sent—but that order never arrived either.

sentences.zh: 至三月始聞太僕之命，即以軍事付啟元。

translations.literal: Only in the third month did he hear of the Court of the Imperial Stud appointment; he forthwith handed military affairs over to Qiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the third month did he hear of the Court of the Imperial Stud appointment; he then handed military affairs to Qiyuan.

sentences.zh: 七月而北都變聞，並聞漢中之命，地已失，不可往。

translations.literal: In the seventh month word came of the change at the northern capital, and he also heard of the Hanzhong appointment—but the territory was already lost and he could not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month came word of the fall of the northern capital and of the Hanzhong post—but the region was lost and he could not go.

sentences.zh: 福王立，移鬥樞巡撫湖廣，代何騰蛟。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, Doushu was transferred to grand coordinator of Huguang in place of He Tengjiao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, Doushu was transferred to grand coordinator of Huguang to replace He Tengjiao.

sentences.zh: 復以道路不通，改用王驥，鬥樞皆不聞也。

translations.literal: Again because the roads were impassable Wang Ji was substituted; Doushu heard of neither appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Again the roads were blocked and Wang Ji was substituted; Doushu heard of neither change.

sentences.zh: 國變後數年卒。

translations.literal: Several years after the dynastic turn he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died several years after the dynastic collapse.

sentences.zh: 啟元、光恩亦皆以功名終。

translations.literal: Qiyuan and Guang'en also both ended their careers with reputation intact.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan and Guang'en also finished their careers with honor.

sentences.zh: 張任學，安嶽人，天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: Zhang Renxue, a native of Anyue, passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Renxue, a native of Anyue, passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 授太原知縣，以才調榆次。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Taiyuan and, for his ability, was transferred to Yuci.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Taiyuan and, for his talent, was moved to Yuci.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，舉治行卓異入為御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was recommended for outstanding administrative performance and entered service as an investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was recommended for outstanding governance and entered the censorate.

sentences.zh: 陳蜀中私稅、催科、訟獄三大苦，帝為飭行。

translations.literal: He stated the three great afflictions in Shu—private levies, harsh collection, and litigation—and the emperor ordered corrective action.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the three great abuses in Shu—private levies, harsh tax collection, and lawsuits—and the emperor ordered reforms.

sentences.zh: 出視兩浙鹽法，數條奏利弊。

translations.literal: He went on an inspection tour of the salt laws of the two Zhe provinces and repeatedly memorialized on advantages and disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the salt administration of the two Zhe provinces and repeatedly memorialized on its pros and cons.

sentences.zh: 八年，流賊陷鳳陽，詔逮巡按吳振纓，命任學往代。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when roaming bandits seized Fengyang, an edict ordered the arrest of touring censor Wu Zhenying and commanded Renxue to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when roaming rebels took Fengyang, an edict arrested touring censor Wu Zhenying and sent Renxue to replace him.

sentences.zh: 還朝，復按河南，監軍討賊。

translations.literal: Returning to court he again served as censor for Henan and supervised the army in suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he again served as Henan censor and supervised troops against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時群盜縱橫，而諸將縮朒不敢擊。

translations.literal: At the time bandit hosts rampaged everywhere while the generals shrank and dared not strike.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels ran wild everywhere while the generals shrank back and dared not fight.

sentences.zh: 任學慨然曰：「事不辭難，臣職也。

translations.literal: Renxue said with indignation: "One does not shrink from difficulty in the matter—that is a minister's duty.
translations.idiomatic: Renxue said angrily: "A minister does not shirk hard tasks—that is his duty.

sentences.zh: 賊勢如此，我輩可雍容坐鎮耶！」

translations.literal: The bandit power is thus—can we sit at ease in dignified repose?"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are this strong—can we sit at ease in dignified repose?

sentences.zh: 十一年二月，遂上疏極詆諸將。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year he then memorialized, fiercely denouncing the generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eleventh year he submitted a memorial fiercely denouncing the generals.

sentences.zh: 請易武階，親執干戈，為國平賊。

translations.literal: He asked to change to a military rank, personally take up weapons, and pacify bandits for the state.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to exchange his civil rank for a military one, take up arms himself, and crush the rebels for the state.

sentences.zh: 帝壯之，下吏、兵二部及都察院議。

translations.literal: The emperor was impressed by his spirit and referred the matter to the Ministries of Personnel and War and the Censorate for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stirred by his resolve and ordered the Ministries of Personnel and War and the Censorate to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 諸臣以文吏無改武職者，請仍以監軍御史兼總兵事。

translations.literal: The officials held that no civil official had ever changed to a military post and asked that he still serve as army-supervising censor while concurrently commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: The officials argued that no civil official had ever switched to a military post and proposed that he remain army-supervising censor while taking overall command.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，命授署都督僉事，為河南總兵官。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree and ordered him appointed acting regional commander-in-chief and made regional commander of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and appointed him acting regional commander-in-chief as regional commander of Henan.

sentences.zh: 河南舊無總兵，左良玉、陳永福並以客兵備援剿，至是大將特設，而麾下無一官，兵部乃以署鎮許定國兵授之，使參將羅岱為中軍。

translations.literal: Henan had formerly had no regional commander; Zuo Liangyu and Chen Yongfu both served with guest troops for relief and suppression—now a great commander was specially established, yet under his command there was not a single officer; the Ministry of War therefore gave him the troops of acting garrison commander Xu Dingguo and made Brigade General Luo Dai his central army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Henan had never had a regional commander; Zuo Liangyu and Chen Yongfu had both served there with outside troops for relief operations. Now a full commander was specially appointed, but he had no staff of his own, so the Ministry of War assigned him the forces of acting garrison commander Xu Dingguo and made Brigade General Luo Dai his chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 岱，健將，屢著戰功，任學倚以自強。

translations.literal: Dai was a vigorous commander who had repeatedly won battle merit; Renxue relied on him to strengthen himself.
translations.idiomatic: Dai was a formidable fighter with repeated victories to his credit, and Renxue leaned on him to build his strength.

sentences.zh: 時熊文燦專主撫，劉國能、張獻忠俱降，羅汝才、馬進忠、李萬慶等躪中原如故。

translations.literal: At this time Xiong Wencan devoted himself solely to pacification; Liu Guoneng and Zhang Xianzhong had both surrendered, while Luo Ruocai, Ma Jinzhong, Li Wanqing, and others trampled the Central Plain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Wencan was committed entirely to appeasement; Liu Guoneng and Zhang Xianzhong had submitted, but Luo Ruocai, Ma Jinzhong, Li Wanqing, and others still ravaged the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 河南人據塢壁自保者數十，賊悉摧破之，踞息縣、光州，磔人投汝水，水為赤，任學不能大創也。

translations.literal: Several tens of Henan people held stockaded villages for self-defense; the bandits destroyed them all, occupied Xi County and Guangzhou, dismembered people and threw them into the Ru River until the water turned red—Renxue could not inflict a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of fortified villages in Henan where locals had tried to defend themselves were all smashed; the rebels held Xi County and Guangzhou, dismembered captives and threw them into the Ru River until the water ran red—and Renxue could not break them decisively.

sentences.zh: 進忠勢衰，佯求撫，文燦及巡撫常道立許之，乘間逸去。

translations.literal: Jinzhong's power waned; he pretended to seek pacification, and Wencan and Grand Coordinator Chang Daoli agreed; he slipped away when he found an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong's strength was failing; he feigned willingness to surrender, and Wencan and Grand Coordinator Chang Daoli accepted—then he escaped at the first opportunity.

sentences.zh: 事聞，任學與文燦、道立並鐫秩。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, Renxue, Wencan, and Daoli were all demoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, Renxue, Wencan, and Daoli were all demoted.

sentences.zh: 七月，任學督岱等赴羅山，合左良玉軍擊汝才、萬慶及紫微星、順義王，大敗之，追奔五十里，斬首一千四百有奇，獲黑虎狼、滿天星，賊奔遂平。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Renxue directed Dai and others to Luoshan, joined Liangyu's army to strike Ruocai, Wanqing, Purple Micro Star, and Righteousness King, inflicted a great defeat, pursued them fifty li, beheaded more than fourteen hundred, captured Black Wolf and Filling-the-Sky Star, and the bandits fled toward Suiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Renxue led Dai and others to Luoshan, joined Zuo Liangyu's army, and routed Ruocai, Wanqing, Purple Micro Star, and Righteousness King; they pursued the enemy fifty li, took more than fourteen hundred heads, captured Black Wolf and Filling-the-Sky Star, and drove the rebels toward Suiping.

sentences.zh: 九月，進忠寇開封，至瓦子坡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jinzhong raided Kaifeng and reached Wazi Slope.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jinzhong attacked Kaifeng and reached Wazi Slope.

sentences.zh: 岱奮擊，賊盡棄輜重遁入大隗山，獲其妻子。

translations.literal: Dai struck fiercely; the bandits abandoned all baggage and fled into Mount Dawei, and their wives and children were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Dai attacked fiercely; the rebels abandoned all their baggage and fled into Mount Dawei, and their families were captured.

sentences.zh: 其冬，京師戒嚴，任學入衛，道謁文燦，言：「獻忠狼子野心，終為國患，我以勤王為名，出其不意，可立縛也。」

translations.literal: That winter the capital was placed on alert; Renxue entered to guard the throne, called on Wencan en route, and said: "Xianzhong has the heart of a wolf cub—he will end as a national calamity. If I use aiding the throne as my pretext and take him unawares, he can be bound at once."
translations.idiomatic: That winter the capital went on alert; Renxue marched to defend the throne and visited Wencan on the way, saying, "Xianzhong is treacherous by nature and will become a lasting menace to the state. Under the pretext of aiding the throne I could take him by surprise and seize him at once.

sentences.zh: 文燦不能用。

translations.literal: Wencan could not adopt the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan would not act on the plan.

sentences.zh: 抵畿南，有詔卻還。

translations.literal: When he reached the south of the capital region, an edict ordered him to turn back.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the region south of the capital, an edict ordered him to turn back.

sentences.zh: 巡撫道立調良玉兵於陜州，賊乘盧氏虛，遁入內鄉、淅川，為文燦所劾。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Daoli shifted Liangyu's troops to Shaanzhou; the bandits seized the opening at Lushi and fled into Neixiang and Xichuan, and Wencan impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Daoli had shifted Liangyu's troops to Shaanzhou; the rebels exploited the gap at Lushi and fled into Neixiang and Xichuan, and Wencan impeached him for it.

sentences.zh: 明年除道立名，任學亦鐫一秩。

translations.literal: The next year Daoli's name was struck from the rolls; Renxue was also demoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Daoli was dismissed from office and Renxue was demoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 遊擊宋懷智、都司孔道興再破賊陳州，部將王應龍、尤之龍等破賊襄城，五戰皆勝。

translations.literal: Mobile Corps Commander Song Huaizhi and Regional Commander Kong Daoxing again defeated bandits at Chenzhou; subordinate commanders Wang Yinglong, You Zhilong, and others defeated bandits at Xiangcheng—five battles, all victories.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Corps Commander Song Huaizhi and Regional Commander Kong Daoxing again defeated rebels at Chenzhou; subordinates Wang Yinglong, You Zhilong, and others beat them at Xiangcheng—five engagements, all won.

sentences.zh: 副將岱與應龍、懷智等復破賊葉縣，十日奏八捷，帝詔所司核實。

translations.literal: Vice General Dai with Yinglong, Huaizhi, and others again defeated bandits at Ye County; in ten days eight victories were reported—the emperor ordered the relevant offices to verify.
translations.idiomatic: Vice General Dai, with Yinglong, Huaizhi, and others, again defeated rebels at Ye County; within ten days eight victories were reported, and the emperor ordered verification.

sentences.zh: 已，又挫賊裕州。

translations.literal: Then they again repulsed bandits at Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They then repulsed the rebels again at Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 而是時總兵孫應元、黃得功統京軍討賊，屢奏大捷。
